resource_contention.description: (resource) Whether resource contention monitoring for a resource is active or inactive for catalog requests and, if active, how long the system should allow a catalog request to wait before notifying the operator and (optionally) redriving the request.

active.description: Resource contention monitoring for a resource is active.

wait_time.description: Specifies how long the system should allow a catalog request to wait before notifying the operator and (optionally) redriving the request. The value is specified in seconds.

action.description: Specifies the action to be taken when a catalog request has waited for the specified wait time.

https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.$comment:
(CDSVERSIONBACKUP JOURNAL) Defining parameters and subparameters affecting DFSMShsm CDS journaling and backup functions. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=parameters-setsys-fast-path-dfsmshsm-functions

cds_journaling.description:
(NOJOURNAL|JOURNAL(RECOVERY|SPEED)) Specifying whether to write updated control data set records in the journal data set. If enabled (JOURNAL), DFSMShsm writes the BCDS, MCDS, and OCDS data set records in the journal data set when DFSMShsm updates them. If disabled (NOJOURNAL) DFSMShsm is not to write the updated BCDS, MCDS, and OCDS records in the journal data set. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-journal-nojournal-specifying-whether-write-updated-control-data-set-records-in-journal-data-set.

cds_version_backup.description:
(CDSVERSIONBACKUP) Specifying whether the control data sets should be backed up to multiple data sets. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-cdsversionbackup-specifying-whether-control-data-sets-should-be-backed-up-multiple-data-sets

copies.description:
(BACKUPCOPIES(number) Specify number to indicate the number of CDS backup copies DFSMShsm should keep. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-cdsversionbackup-backupcopies-specifying-number-backup-copies-keep-each-control-data-set-journal-data-set

anyOf.$comment: (DASD|TAPE) can be specified without additional subparameter.

unit_name.$comment: (UNITNAME) can be specified without a subparemeter.

expiration_date.description: (EXPIRATIONDATE) Specify an expiration date in yyyyddd format. yyyy and ddd are the year and day of the year. For yyyy, specify a year between the current year and 2155. For ddd, specify a day between 001 and 366.
expiration_date.$comment: Validate a future julian date. yyddd is invalid beyond 1999

retention_period.description:
(RETENTIONPERIOD) Specify a 1- to 4-digit number representing the number of days DFSMShsm must keep the backup copy before DFSMShsm can delete it. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-cdsversionbackup-backupdevicecategory-specifying-backup-device-which-control-data-sets-journal-will-be-backed-up

data_mover.description:
(DATAMOVER) Specifying the type of data movement used when performing CDSVERSIONBACKUP. 
 If (HSM) is specified, DFSMShsm control data sets are backed up using the AMS EXPORT function. The journal data set is backed up using sequential I/O. 
 If (DSS) is specified, DFSMShsm control data sets are backed up by invoking the DFSMSdss logical dump function for each data set. The journal is backed up using sequential I/O. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-cdsversionbackup-datamover-specifying-type-data-movement-used-when-performing-cdsversionbackup

bcds_backup_dataset_name.description:
(BCDSBACKUPDSN) Specifies the initial characters of the data set name to be used when allocating the backup data set for the BCDS. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-cdsversionbackup-bcdsbackupdsn-specifying-initial-characters-backup-data-set-name-backup-control-data-set

mcds_backup_dataset_name.description:

ocds_backup_dataset_name.description:
(OCDSBACKUPDSN) Specifies the initial characters of the data set name to be used when allocating the backup data set for the BCDS.

https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.title: BPXPRM Data Definitions
https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.description: (BPXPRMxx) Data-oriented definitions for z/OS UNIX System Services, including file system types, mounts, sysplex sharing, version selection, and superuser naming. https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=parameters-statements-bpxprmxx

file_system_types.description: (FILESYSTYPE TYPE(...)) Defines one or more physical file system types that z/OS UNIX can initialize and use during startup.

zos_file_system.description: (FILESYSTYPE TYPE(ZFS)) Handles z/OS File System requests.

hierarchical_file_system.description: (FILESYSTYPE TYPE(HFS)) Handles deprecated HFS type file systems.

automnt_file_system.description: (FILESYSTYPE TYPE(AUTOMNT)) Handles automatic mounting and unmounting of file systems. The AUTOMNT file system is mounted as AUTOMOVE(YES). However, if the parent file system has the automove unmount attribute, then the automount file system will have that attribute instead of AUTOMOUNT(YES).

network_file_system.description: (FILESYSTYPE TYPE(NFS)) Handles Network File System requests for access to remote files. For NFS Client, you must create a procedure to run a PFS in a colony address space.

process_file_system.description: (FILESYSTYPE TYPE(PROC)) Manages files that contain process and system information..

temporary_file_system.description: (FILESYSTYPE TYPE(TFS)) Handles requests to the temporary file system (TFS).

unified_file_system.description: (FILESYSTYPE TYPE(UFS)) Obtains unified view of two or more directories.

root_file_system.description: (ROOT) Defines and mounts the root file system for z/OS UNIX.

file_system.description: (FILESYSTEM) Specifies the name of the root file system data set. Exactly one of file_system or dd_name must be specified.

dd_name.description: (DDNAME) Specifies the DD name for the root file system. Exactly one of file_system or dd_name must be specified.

mode.description: (MODE) Specifies whether the root file system is mounted read-only or read/write.

parm.description: (PARM) Specifies a file-system-specific parameter string for the root file system.

allOf.title: Exactly one of file_system or dd_name must be specified for ROOT.

alternate_root.description: (ALTROOT) Specifies the alternate sysplex root file system.

file_system.description: (FILESYSTEM) Specifies the name of the alternate root file system data set.

parm.description: (PARM) Specifies a file-system-specific parameter string for the alternate root file system.

mount_point.description: (MOUNTPOINT) Specifies the path name where the alternate root file system is mounted.

file_systems.description: (MOUNT) Defines one or more file systems to be mounted during z/OS UNIX initialization.

file_system.description: (FILESYSTEM) Specifies the name of the file system to be mounted.

mount_point.description: (MOUNTPOINT) Specifies the z/OS UNIX path name on which the file system is mounted.

mode.description: (MODE) Specifies whether the mounted file system is read-only or read/write.

security.description: (SECURITY|NOSECURITY) Specifies whether RACF or equivalent security checking is performed for the mounted file system.

unmount.description: (UNMOUNT) Specifies that the file system is to be unmounted instead of automatically moved. When true, renders as UNMOUNT. When false, nothing is rendered.

automove_list.description: (AUTOMOVE(INCLUDE|EXLCUDE,...) Specifies a prioritized system list for file system movement when the owning system goes down. The first item must be either 'INCLUDE' or 'EXCLUDE'. When 'INCLUDE' is the first item, the following systems are treated as a prioritized list of systems eligible to transfer ownership to. If the none of the specified systems are available, then the file system is unmounted unless an asterik '*' is the last item in the list. When asterisk (*) is listed last in INCLUDE lists, then any other avaialble system will be used if all other specified systems are unavailable.  When 'EXCLUDE' is the first item, the following systems are treated as ineligble for ownership transfer. If the file system cannot be moved as directed, it is unmounted.

parm.description: (PARM) Specifies a file-system-specific mount parameter string.

allOf.title: automove, unmount, and automove_list are mutually exclusive; do not specify automove with unmount.
automove, unmount, and automove_list are mutually exclusive; do not specify automove with automove_list.
automove, unmount, and automove_list are mutually exclusive; do not specify unmount with automove_list.

sysplex.description: (SYSPLEX) Specifies whether the system joins the SYSBPX XCF group to share z/OS UNIX resources across the sysplex.

version_file_system.description: (VERSION) The VERSION statement applies only to systems that are exploiting shared file systems. VERSION allows multiple releases and service levels of the binaries to coexist and participate in a shared file system. A directory with the value version specified on VERSION is dynamically created at system initialization under the sysplex root that is used as a mount point for the version file system. However, this directory is only dynamically created if the root file system for the sysplex is mounted as read/write.

version.description: ('version') A Directory with value 'version' is dynamically created at system initialization under the sysplex root that is used as a mount point for the version file system.

unmount.description: (UNMOUNT|NOUNMOUNT) Specifies whether mounted file systems are unmounted during version processing.

super_user.description: (SUPERUSER) Specifies the z/OS UNIX superuser ID. This value must conform to z/OS user ID naming restrictions.

nonempty_mount_point.description: (NONEMPTYMOUNTPT) Specifies how the system is to mount any file system on a mount point when it is a nonempty directory. If NONEMPTYMOUNTPT is not specified, default values are used. NOWARN enables the system to mount any file system on mount point without any warning message when the mount point is a nonempty directory (contents hidden for the duration of the mount). WARN enables the system to mount any file system on mount point with a warning message when the mount point is a nonempty directory (contents hidden for the duration of the mount). DENY prevents the system from mounting any file system when the mount point is a nonempty directory.

zos_name_pattern.description: Standard z/OS name pattern (1-8 characters, starting with A-Z, $, #, or @)

setuid.description: (SETUID|NOSETUID) Specifies whether setuid and setgid processing is allowed.

automove.description: (AUTOMOVE|NOAUTOMOVE) Specifies whether the file system can be automatically moved.

tag.description: (TAG) Specifies whether implicit file tags are assigned to untagged files.

auto_convert.description: (TEXT|NOTEXT) Specifies whether untagged files are treated as text. true renders as TEXT; false renders as NOTEXT.

ccsid.description: (ccsid) Specifies the coded character set identifier to assign to untagged files.

mkdir.description: (MKDIR) Specifies a path name to create if it does not already exist.

entry_point.description: (ENTRYPOINT) Specifies the name of the load module entry point that z/OS calls to initialize the physical file system during startup.

address_space.description: (ASNAME) Specifies the started procedure name for the file system address space and optional start parameters.

procedure_name.description: Procedure name used to start the file system address space for ASNAME.

start_parameters.description: Optional ASNAME start parameters string appended when the procedure is started.

parm.description: (PARM) Specifies a file-system-specific parameter string passed directly to the physical file system.

https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.title: DFSMShsm DEFINE DUMPCLASS
https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.description:
DEFINE DUMPCLASS is an optional parameter specifying a volume dump class to be added or changed
https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=dfsmshsm-syntax-define-command

class_name.description:
DEFINE DUMPCLASS(..)Substitute from one to eight characters for the class name to be defined
https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-dumpclass-adding-changing-volume-dump-class

auto_reuse.description:
DUMPCLASS(AUTOREUSE and NOAUTOREUSE) Specifies whether DUMP volumes are automatically available for reuse when invalidated 
 - When true, DUMPCLASS(AUTOREUSE) specifies that when DFSMShsm initiates the invalidation of a dump copy, the dump volumes are automatically made available for reuse. 
 - When false, DUMPCLASS(NOAUTOREUSE) specifies that when DFSMShsm initiates the invalidation of a dump copy, the dump volumes are marked unavailable for selection by DFSMShsm
https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opdc-dumpclassautoreuse-noautoreuse-specifies-whether-dump-volumes-are-automatically-available-reuse-when-invalidated

dataset_restore.description:
DUMPCLASS(DATASETRESTORE|NODATASETRESTORE) Specifying whether data set restore is allowed from a full-volume dump copy in this dump class. 
 - If true, DUMPCLASS(DATASETRESTORE) specifies that physical restores of individual data sets from dump volumes in this class are allowed. The dump volumes must remain available to satisfy mount requests. A physical data set restore requires the mounting of one or more tapes to complete the request. 
 - If false, DUMPCLASS(NODATASETRESTORE) specifies that dump volumes in this class are not available to do individual physical data set restores. All data set recoveries are from incremental backup versions unless a dump volume is explicitly requested on the RECOVER command. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opdc-dumpclassdatasetrestore-nodatasetrestore-data-set-restore-is-allowed-from-full-volume-dump-copy-in-this-dump-class#s4201

day.description:
DUMPCLASS(DAY(day)) Specifying the target day of the dump cycle for this class. For day, specify a decimal number from 0 to the number of days in the dump cycle. A value of 0 removes a previous association with a day in the dump cycle. Any other value must be from 1 to a value less than or equal to the number of days specified in the dump cycle (must be a 'Y' day specified in the DUMPCYCLE parameter).
https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opdc-dumpclassday-specifying-target-day-dump-cycle-this-class

disable.description:
DUMPCLASS(DISABLE) Specifying the volume dump class and making it unavailable as a target of any full-volume dump
https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opdc-dumpclassdisable-specifying-volume-dump-class-making-it-unavailable-as-target-any-full-volume-dump

disposition.description:
DUMPCLASS(DISPOSITION(?disposition?)): For disposition, substitute a character string from 1 to 20 characters describing the intended disposition of the dump volumes. The disposition is inserted into message ARC0637I, which is issued for each dump copy successfully created for a source volume. If disposition is not specified, message ARC0637I is sent to the dump activity log, but not to the system console.
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-dumpclassdisposition-specifying-disposition-dump-volumes#s4204

encrypt.description:
DUMPCLASS(ENCRYPT) Specifying whether to encrypt the dump data with host based encryption
https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opdc-dumpclassencrypt-specifying-whether-encrypt-dump-data-host-based-encryption

none.description:
DUMPCLASS(ENCRYPT(NONE))Specifies that data encryption is not performed for this dump class. This option overrides the encryption settings, if any, in the existing dump class
https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opdc-dumpclassencrypt-specifying-whether-encrypt-dump-data-host-based-encryption

rsa.description:
DUMPCLASS(ENCRYPT(RSA) TYPE()) Specifies the RSA key label to be used when secure cryptographic hardware is used to encrypt the data to be dumped. keylabel identifies the key label that is to be used to encrypt the data. The key label is 1-64 characters long, and the first character must be an alphabetic or special character.
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opdc-dumpclassencrypt-specifying-whether-encrypt-dump-data-host-based-encryption

key_password.description:
DUMPCLASS(ENCRYPT(KEYPASSWORD) TYPE()) Specifies that the data is to be encrypted without secure cryptographic hardware. The password, which is used to generate a key for the data encryption, is 8-32 characters long.
https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opdc-dumpclassencrypt-specifying-whether-encrypt-dump-data-host-based-encryption

icount.description:
DUMPCLASS(ENCRYPT(ICOUNT) TYPE()) Specifies the number of hash iterations to be performed on the password when the PKCS #12 algorithm is used to generate the key. For the iteration count (count), specify an integer between 1 and 10000.
https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opdc-dumpclassencrypt-specifying-whether-encrypt-dump-data-host-based-encryption

type.description:
DUMPCLASS(ENCRYPT(RSA/KEYPASSWORD/ICOUNT) TYPE())Specifies the type of encryption to be performed on the data.
CLRAES128 encrypts the dumped data with a clear 128-bit AES key. 
CLRTDES encrypts the dumped data with a clear, triple-length DES key. 
ENCTDES encrypts the dumped data with a secure triple-length DES key. 
https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opdc-dumpclassencrypt-specifying-whether-encrypt-dump-data-host-based-encryption

then.title: ENCRYPT(NONE) cannot be combined with RSA, TYPE, KEYPASSWORD, or ICOUNT
When ENCRYPT(RSA) is specified PASSWORD cannot be specified

frequency.description:
DUMPCLASS(FREQUENCY) Specifying the minimum number of days that must elapse between volume dumps of a volume to this class
https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opdc-dumpclassfrequency-specifying-minimum-number-days-that-must-elapse-between-volume-dumps-volume-this-class

fast_replication_dump.description:
DUMPCLASS(FASTREPLICATIONDUMP) Specifying whether a dump class is required or optional
https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opdc-dumpclassfastreplicationdump-specifying-whether-dump-class-is-required-optional

fast_replication_recover.description:
DUMPCLASS(FASTREPLICATIONRECOVER) Specifying whether a dump class copy is immediately available to be mounted for recovery
https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opdc-dumpclassfastreplicationrecover-specifying-whether-dump-class-copy-is-immediately-available-be-mounted-recovery

available_for_mount.description:
DUMPCLASS(FASTREPLICATIONRECOVER(AVAILABLEFORMOUNT(YES|NO))) Specifies whether the fast replication dump copy is immediately available to be mounted for recovery. If YES, the dump copy is immediately available for mounting. If NO, the dump copy is not immediately available for mounting.
https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opdc-dumpclassfastreplicationrecover-specifying-whether-dump-class-copy-is-immediately-available-be-mounted-recovery

hardware_compression.description:
DUMPCLASS(HWCOMPRESS(YES|NO)) Specifying whether to use hardware assisted compression on the dump data before encryption. 
 - If true, DUMPCLASS(HWCOMPRESS(YES)) When YES is specified, hardware-assisted compression will be performed. Specify this option only when encryption is being used; it specifies that the data should be compressed before it is encrypted. 
 - If false, DUMPCLASS(HWCOMPRESS(NO)) When NO is specified, hardware-assisted compression will not be performed. HWCOMPRESS(NO) can be specified to override an existing setting of HWCOMPRESS(YES). If the data is not being encrypted, specify HWCOMPRESS(NO) so that tape hardware compression is used. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-dumpclasshwcompress-specifying-whether-compress-data-be-encrypted#hwpress

recover_reset.description:
DUMPCLASS(RECOVERRESET) Specifying whether to reset the data-set-changed indicator in the VTOC entry
https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opdc-dumpclassrecoverreset-specifying-whether-reset-data-set-changed-indicator-in-vtoc-entry

reset.description:
DUMPCLASS(RESET|NORESET): Specifying whether DFSMSdss resets the change bit for each data set following a full-volume dump.
 If true, DUMPCLASS(RESET) specifies that the change bit for each data set should be reset.
 If false, DUMPCLASS(NORESET) specifies that the change bit for each data set should not be reset. 
https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opdc-dumpclassreset-noreset-specifying-whether-dfsmsdss-resets-change-bit-each-data-set-following-full-volume-dump

retention_period.description:
DUMPCLASS(RETENTIONPERIOD) Specifying the enforcement of retention periods for the dump copies in this class
https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opdc-dumpclassretentionperiod-specifying-enforcement-retention-periods-dump-copies-in-this-class

max_dump_copies.description:
DUMPCLASS(STACK/MAXSTACK) Specifying the maximum number of dump copies that are stacked for this dump class
https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opdc-dumpclassstackmaxstack-dumpclassminstack-specifying-maximum-minimum-number-dump-copies-that-are-stacked-this-dump-class

min_dump_copies.description:
DUMPCLASS(MINSTACK) Specifying the minimum number of dump copies that are stacked for this dump class
https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opdc-dumpclassstackmaxstack-dumpclassminstack-specifying-maximum-minimum-number-dump-copies-that-are-stacked-this-dump-class

tape_expiration_date.description:
DUMPCLASS(TAPEEXPIRATIONDATE(yyyyddd)): Specifying a unique expiration date for all dump copies created in this dump class. For year and day, specify a 7-digit number in the format of yyyyddd. The yyyy value and the ddd value are the year and day of the year for the expiration date of the dump copies. For yyyy, specify a year between the current year and 2155. For ddd, specify a day between 001 and 366.

Note: For TAPEEXPIRATIONDATE to be effective, the security options in effect must include EXPIRATION or EXPIRATIONINCLUDE. Values for yyyyddd of 1999365 and 1999366 are recognized as 'never expire' dates. Values of 1998000 and 1999000 are recognized as meaningful to certain tape management systems. If you do not specify TAPEEXPIRATIONDATE for a dump class and a tape security option of EXPIRATION or EXPIRATIONINCLUDE is in effect, DFSMShsm provides an expiration date of 1999365 for dump volumes written for this class. Past dates are not recognized as expiration dates.

https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opdc-dumpclasstapeexpirationdate-specifying-unique-expiration-date-all-dump-copies-created-in-dump

year.description:
Year value for the expiration date. Specify a 4-digit year between the current year and 2155. Special values: 1998 and 1999 are recognized by certain tape management systems (e.g., 1998000, 1999000 for special tape management values; 1999365, 1999366 for 'never expire' dates). 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opdc-dumpclasstapeexpirationdate-specifying-unique-expiration-date-all-dump-copies-created-in-dump

day.description:
Day of year for the expiration date. Specify a day between 001 and 366 (366 for leap years). Special value 000 is recognized as meaningful to certain tape management systems (e.g., 1998000, 1999000). Values 1999365 and 1999366 are recognized as 'never expire' dates. The value is automatically rendered with leading zeros as a 3-digit value (e.g., 000, 001, 042, 365). 

IMPORTANT: In YAML, do NOT use leading zeros (e.g., use 42, not 042) as YAML interprets numbers with leading zeros as octal. The schema will automatically format the output with leading zeros.

https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opdc-dumpclasstapeexpirationdate-specifying-unique-expiration-date-all-dump-copies-created-in-dump

unit.description:
DUMPCLASS(UNIT) Specifying a default tape unit name
https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-dumpclassunit-specifying-default-tape-unit-name

Tape-only parameters are not allowed when CLOUD is specified
When DISABLE is specified, no other parameters are allowed

primary_space_management_cycle.description:
(PRIMARYSPMGMTCYCLE | PRIMARYSPMGMTCYCLE(...)) Specifying the cycle for automatic primary space management functions. 
 If "default" (PRIMARYSPMGMTCYCLE),  DFSMShsm will set the cycle to a one-day cycle. Therefore, if a start time has been specified by a SETSYS PRIMARYSPMGMTSTART or AUTOMIGRATIONSTART command, automatic primary space management functions will run every day. 
 If object PRIMARYSPMGMTCYCLE(...), use the available properties to fine tune the primary space management cycle and start date. 
 See
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-primaryspmgmtcycle-specifying-cycle-automatic-primary-space-management

secondary_space_management_cycle.description:
(SECONDARYSPMGMTCYCLE | SECONDARYSPMGMTCYCLE(...)) Specifying the cycle for automatic secondary space management functions. 
 If "default" (SECONDARYSPMGMTCYCLE),  DFSMShsm will set the cycle to a one-day cycle. Therefore, if a start time has been specified by a SETSYS SECONDARYSPMGMTSTART command, automatic primary space management functions will run every day. 
 If object SECONDARYSPMGMTCYCLE(...), use the available properties to fine tune the secondary space management cycle and start date. 
 See
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opdc-migrationcleanupcycle-secondaryspmgmtcycle-specifying-cycle-automatic-secondary-space-management-functions

dump_cycle.description:
(DUMPCYCLE) is an optional parameter specifying the days in a cycle when the automatic dump process should run. See
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-dumpcycle-specifying-automatic-dump-cycle

backup.description:
(BACKUP | BACKUP(...)) Specifying the days in a cycle when the automatic backup process should run. 
 If true (BACKUP), DFSMShsm automatic backup cycle defaults to a seven-day cycle with automatic backup every day. The number of DASD backup volumes used per cycle day defaults to one. 
 If false (or omitted), DFSMShsm automatic backup will be disabled 
 If object (BACKUP(...)), use the available properties to specify the cycle days and cycle start date.
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-backup-specifying-backup-cycle

bvols.description:
(BVOLS) is decimal number from 1 to 9999 representing the number of DASD backup volumes DFSMShsm assigns to a given day in the backup cycle (daily limit). If omitted, defaults to 1. See
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-backup-specifying-backup-cycle

cycle.description:
(CYCLE) is substitute a string of alphabetic Ys and Ns. Each Y represents a day in the cycle when automatic primary space management is to run. Each N represents a day in the cycle when automatic primary space management is not to run. You can represent up to 31 days with the Ys and Ns. The current day is the first day of the cycle, unless you specify the cycle start date. See
 For PRIMARYSPMGMT: https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-primaryspmgmtcycle-specifying-cycle-automatic-primary-space-management 
 For SECONDARYSPMGMT: https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opdc-migrationcleanupcycle-secondaryspmgmtcycle-specifying-cycle-automatic-secondary-space-management-functions 
 For MIGRATIONCLEANUP: https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opdc-migrationcleanupcycle-secondaryspmgmtcycle-specifying-cycle-automatic-secondary-space-management-functions 
 For DUMP: https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-dumpcycle-specifying-automatic-dump-cycle 
 For BACKUP: https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-backup-specifying-backup-cycle

cycle_start_date.description:
(CYCLESTARTDATE) is an optional subparameter specifying the start date or reset date of a cycle. If you do not specify CYCLESTARTDATE, the current date is the start date of the cycle, and If you specify CYCLESTARTDATE, you must also specify cycle; otherwise, the command will fail. See
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-cyclestartdate-specifying-start-date-cycle#hr3007

https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.title: DFSMShsm ARCCMDxx HOLD Command
https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.description:
The HOLD command prevents all or some DFSMShsm functions from running. For example, you specify
HOLD when a temporary software or hardware problem occurs that can be compounded if data
movement continues in DFSMShsm.
Migration, backup, dump, recovery, and restore have an optional keyword related to stopping volume
processing after the current data set (EOD) or delaying until the end of processing the user volume (EOV).
 
Note:
• HOLD ALL will hold the sub-function of AUTOEXPIRATION of data sets beginning with PTF UA99661 in
2.4 and above.
• HOLD MIGRATION or HOLD MIGRATION(AUTO) will not hold AUTOEXPIRATION. You must use HOLD
AUTOEXPIRATION if you want this function held.
 
The WAIT and NOWAIT parameters of the HSENDCMD command have implications to HOLD command
processing that are function specific. Refer to the specific processing function for an explanation.
All nonWAIT-type requests remain on the processing queue when the appropriate HOLD command is in
effect.
If the HOLD command is issued while the TAPECOPY or TAPEREPL commands are processing more than
one volume, either from a volume list from the command or from an input data set, processing stops after
the current volume.
You can issue the RELEASE command to release for processing all or some of the DFSMShsm functions
held with the HOLD command.
Functions held from processing by the HOLD command are no longer prevented from processing if
DFSMShsm is reinitialized.


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=reference-hold-command-preventing-dfsmshsm-functions-from-running

aggregate_backup.description:
ABACKUP is an optional parameter specifying that the process of backing up aggregated data sets stops after completion of any currently running aggregate backup. 
 It can either be a boolean type (only true allowed), or be an object with key 'aggregate_group_name'. 


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-abackup-preventing-aggregate-backup

aggregate_group_name.description:
ABACKUP(agname) is an optional parameter specifying an SMS aggregate group. 


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-abackup-preventing-aggregate-backup

all.description:
ALL is an optional parameter specifying that all functions controlled by this HOLD command, except logging, are prevented. 
 It can either be a boolean type (only true allowed), or be an object with key 'aggregate_group_name' and 'controlfile_dsn'. 


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-all-preventing-all-dfsmshsm-functions

aggregate_recover.description:
ARECOVER is an optional parameter specifying that the process of recovering aggregated data sets stop after completion of any currently running aggregate recovery.


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-arecover-preventing-aggregate-recovery

aggregate_group_name.description:
ARECOVER AGGREGATE(agname) is an optional parameter specifying an SMS aggregate group.


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-arecover-preventing-aggregate-recovery

controlfile_dsn.description:
ARECOVER DATASETNAME(controlfiledsn) is an optional parameter specifying a control file name. For controlfile_dsn, substitute the name of the control file against which you want DFSMShsm to hold processing.


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-arecover-preventing-aggregate-recovery

audit.description:
AUDIT is an optional parameter specifying that DFSMShsm stop the audit function after it finishes processing the current data set.


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-audit-ending-audit-function

auto_expiration.description:
AUTOEXPIRATION is an optional parameter specifying that DFSMShsm stop the automatic expiration of data sets during space management.


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-autoexpiration-preventing-data-sets-from-expiring

auto_migration.description:
AUTOMIGRATION is an optional parameter specifying that automatic volume and automatic secondary space management are prevented. If automatic volume and automatic secondary space management are running when you issue the HOLD command, automatic volume and automatic secondary space management stop. The point at which processing stops is controlled by the "end_of_dataset" and "end_of_volume" parameters.


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=ophc-automigration-preventing-automatic-volume-automatic-secondary-space-management

backup.description:
BACKUP is an optional parameter that specifies whether you want DFSMShsm to prevent all backup processing or to prevent only the following processing:
 - All data set backup requests
 - All data set backup requests to either DASD or tape
 - Data set backups to DASD
 - Data set backups to tape
 - All automatic backups


The BACKUP parameter also specifies whether you want DFSMShsm to demount tapes that are used by command backup.
The BACKUP parameter, without any subparameters, prevents all backup processing tasks and demounts all tapes mounted for command data set backup. No more tasks are started for backup processing. Any command requests that specified the WAIT keyword are failed. 
 'backup' can either be a boolean type (only true allowed), or be an object with key 'auto' and 'dataset_command'. 


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-backup-preventing-backups

auto.description:
BACKUP( AUTO ) specifies that automatic backup processing is prevented. No more automatic backup processing tasks are started. You can still perform command backup processing tasks.


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-backup-preventing-backups

dataset_command.description:
BACKUP( DSCOMMAND( <blank> | DASD | TAPE | SWITCHTAPES) ), prevent backup to various media. Option takes 1 of 4 values...
1. true (boolean) - Hold all data set backups by command and all INUSE RETRY backups from autobackup.
2. DASD (enum) - Hold data set backups directed to ML1 DASD.
3. TAPE (enum) - Hold data set backups directed to tape.
4. SWITCHTAPES (enum) - Switch tapes at the end of backup to tape.


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-backup-preventing-backups

common_queue.description:
COMMONQUEUE is an optional parameter that specifies that DFSMShsm prevent all common queue processing. If you specify COMMONQUEUE without any parameters, a host neither places recall requests in the CRQ, nor selects recall requests from the CRQ. 
 It can be set in two ways: 
  - boolean type, only true is allowed, i.e. (COMMONQUE) without RECALL option. 
  - object, with key 'recall'.
     -  'recall' can either be a boolean type (only true allowed), or be an object with two keys, 'placement' and 'selection'.


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-commonqueue-preventing-common-queue-functions

recall.description:
COMMONQUEUE(RECALL) specifies that a host neither places recall requests in the CRQ, nor selects recall requests from the CRQ.


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-commonqueue-preventing-common-queue-functions

placement.description:
COMMONQUEUE(RECALL(PLACEMENT)) specifies that the host does not place additional requests in the CRQ. All new requests will be placed on the host's local recall queue.


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-commonqueue-preventing-common-queue-functions

selection.description:
COMMONQUEUE(RECALL(SELECTION)) specifies that the host does not select recall requests from the CRQ.


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-commonqueue-preventing-common-queue-functions

dump.description:
DUMP is an optional parameter specifying whether DFSMShsm prevents all dump processing (command and automatic) or prevents only automatic dump processing. Can be specified as a boolean true value, or as an object with dump_type property. When object, dump_type can be 1 of 3 enums...

 1. ALL : specifies that all dump processing tasks are prevented
 2. AUTO : specifies that automatic dump processing is prevented. No additional automatic dump processing tasks are started. You can still perform command dump processing tasks. Also prevents auto dump tasks for fast replication copy pool volumes from starting. This setting does not affect dump tasks started through the FRBACKUP command.
 3. FRBACKUP : specifies that dump processing of FRBACKUP target volumes is prevented. No additional FRBACKUP DUMP tasks or FRBACKUP DUMPONLY tasks are started.


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-dump-preventing-dumps

dump_type.description:
Type of dump processing to hold. 1 of 3 enums can be given...

 1. ALL : specifies that all dump processing tasks are prevented
 2. AUTO : specifies that automatic dump processing is prevented
 3. FRBACKUP : specifies that dump processing of FRBACKUP target volumes is prevented


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-dump-preventing-dumps

expire_backup_versions.description:
EXPIREBV is an optional parameter specifying that DFSMShsm stop the process of deleting old, unwanted backup versions from the BCDS at the end of the current data set and not allow an expire backup versions command to be started.


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-expirebv-ending-expire-backup-function

event_driven_migration.description:
EVENTDRIVENMIGRATION is an optional parameter specifying that DFSMShsm stop both interval Migration and On-demand Migration. Other automatic migration functions may still run.


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-eventdrivenmigration-preventing-interval-demand-migration

fast_replication_backup.description:
FRBACKUP is an optional parameter that you specify to prevent new Fast Replication commands from processing.


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-frbackup-preventing-fast-replication-backup-dump-processing

fast_replication_recover.description:
FRRECOV is an optional parameter that you specify to prevent new FRRECOV commands from processing. May either be a boolean 'true' value or 1 of 3 enums as follows...
1. ALL - hold all FRRECOV processing.
2. DATASET - hold FRRECOV processing of data sets from DASD.
3. TAPE - hold FRRECOV processing from tape/dump.


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-frrecov-preventing-fast-replication-recovery-processing

list.description:
LIST is an optional parameter specifying that DFSMShsm stop the list function after it finishes processing the control data set record of the current request.


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-list-ending-list-function

log.description:
LOG is an optional parameter specifying that DFSMShsm stop recording in the DFSMShsm log. No records are written in the DFSMShsm log for those DFSMShsm functions that continue to run. DFSMShsm continues recording information in the activity logs.


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-log-preventing-logging

migration.description:
MIGRATION is an optional parameter specifying whether DFSMShsm should prevent all space management processing or prevent only automatic space management processing. Can be specified as a boolean true value (holds all migration), or as an object with only_auto property to hold only automatic migration.


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-migration-preventing-space-management

only_auto.description:
When true, specifies that only automatic migration processing is prevented. Command migration can still run.


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-migration-preventing-space-management

recall.description:
RECALL is an optional parameter specifying which recalls (automatic or command) and deletions of a migrated data set are prevented. 1 of 3 enums can be specified...

 1. ALL : prevents all recall processing
 2. TAPE : RECALL(TAPE) specifies that recall requests from all tape volumes do not process.
 3. TSO_TAPE : RECALL(TAPE(TSO)) specifies that TSO recall requests from migration level 2 tapes are prevented. Recall requests from tape submitted from a batch job and all nontape volumes are still processed.


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-recall-preventing-recall-deletion

recover.description:
RECOVER is an optional parameter specifying whether DFSMShsm prevents all recovery and restore processing or prevents only tape data set recovery processing. 1 of 2 enums are allowed...
1. ALL - hold all recover processing.
2. TAPEDATASET - hold recover processing from tape.


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-recover-preventing-recovery-restore

recycle.description:
RECYCLE is an optional parameter specifying that the recycle function ends after DFSMShsm processes the current backup version or migration copy on each volume being recycled.


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-recycle-ending-recycle-function

report.description:
REPORT is an optional parameter specifying that DFSMShsm stop the report function after it has finished processing the control data set record for the current request.


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-report-ending-report-function

tape_copy.description:
TAPECOPY is an optional parameter specifying that DFSMShsm hold all tape copy processes.


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-tapecopy-preventing-dfsmshsm-from-copying-tape

tape_replacement.description:
TAPEREPL is an optional parameter specifying that DFSMShsm hold all tape replacement processes.


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=ophc-taperepl-preventing-dfsmshsm-from-replacing-original-tape-volume-alternate

then.description: end_of_dataset is mutually exclusive with end_of_volume
end_of_volume is mutually exclusive with end_of_dataset

end_of_dataset.description:
When EOD is specified after ABACKUP, i.e. key 'aggregate_backup', it means Stop current executing Aggregate Backup at end of current Data Set processing.


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-abackup-preventing-aggregate-backup 

 For others, ENDOFDATASET (EOD) specifies to stop volume processing at the end of the current dataset for one of the following:
 - Space management (automatic or command)
 - Backup (automatic or command)
 - Dump (automatic or command, including fast replication dump)
 - Recover (including fast replication recovery from a dump volume)
 - Restore.

This option is mutually exclusive with end_of_volume.


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=ophc-endofdataset-endofvolume-specifying-when-volume-processing-should-stop

end_of_volume.description:
ENDOFVOLUME (EOV) specifies to stop volume processing at the end of the current volume for one of the following:
 - Space management (automatic or command)
 - Backup (automatic or command)
 - Dump (automatic or command, including fast replication dump)
 - Recover (including fast replication recovery from a dump volume)
 - Restore.

This option is mutually exclusive with end_of_dataset.


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=ophc-endofdataset-endofvolume-specifying-when-volume-processing-should-stop

https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.title: DFSMShsm ARCCMDxx SETSYS commands for DFSMShsm installation exits
https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.description:
(SETSYS) Parameters controlling the DFSMShsm exits. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=dsar-setsys-command-establishing-changing-values-dfsmshsm-control-parameters
https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.$comment:
(EXITOFF | EXITON) Defining parameters and subparameters that are essential to your installation's DFSMShsm environment. These parameters affect multiple DFSMShsm functions. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=parameters-setsys-fast-path-dfsmshsm-functions

exit_off.description:
(EXITOFF) specifies inactive installation exits. If true is specified for the DFSMShsm installation exit name, the exit will be included in the (EXITOFF(modname, modname, ...)) parameter for inactive exits. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-exitoff-specifying-inactive-installation-exits 
 For more information about DFSMShsm installation exits, see z/OS DFSMS Installation Exits. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=zdie-dfsmshsm-installation-exits

dataset_deletion.description:
(EXITOFF(AD)) Specifies whether the data set deletion exit is active during data set deletion or data set retirement. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=exit-characteristics-arcadext

dataset_backup.description:
(EXITOFF(BD)) Specifies whether the data set backup exit is active during volume or command data set backup. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=exits-arcbdext-data-set-backup-installation-exit

control_dataset_backup.description:
(EXITOFF(CB)) Specifies whether the control data set backup exit is active after DFSMShsm creates backup copies of the control data set. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=exits-arccbext-control-data-set-backup-installation-exit

dataset_reblock.description:
(EXITOFF(CD)) Specifies whether the data set reblock exit is active during recall or recovery processing. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=exits-arccdext-data-set-reblock-installation-exit

initialization.description:
(EXITOFF(IN)) Specifies whether the initialization exit is active after DFSMShsm startup, before functional subtasks become active. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=exits-arcinext-initialization-installation-exit

space_management.description:
(EXITOFF(MD) Specifies whether the space management exit is active when a data set fulfills the selection criteria for the level 0 volume being managed, but before the data set migrates or transitions. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=exits-arcmdext-space-management-exit

secondary_migration_dataset.description:
(EXITOFF(MM)) Specifies whether the second-level migration exit is active when a command or automatic selection process selects to migrate an already migrated data set. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=die-arcmmext-second-level-migration-data-set-installation-exit

space_management_volume.description:
(EXITOFF(MV)) Specifies whether the space mamagement volume exit is active after DFSMShsm completes processing at level 0 volume during volume space management. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=exits-arcmvext-space-management-volume-installation-exit

recall.description:
(EXITOFF(RD)) Specifies whether the recall exit is active during recall of non-SMS-managed data sets. This exit is not called for SMS-managed data sets. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=exits-arcrdext-recall-installation-exit

return_priority.description:
(EXITOFF(RP)) Specifies whether the return-priority exit is active Before a recall, delete, or recover (data set or volume) request is queued. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=exits-arcrpext-return-priority-installation-exit

space_management_and_backup.description:
(EXITOFF(SA)) Specifies whether the space management and backup exit is active. It is called once for each data set processed during volume space management or backup. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=exits-arcsaext-space-management-backup-installation-exit

shutdown.description:
(EXITOFF(SD)) Specifies whether the shutdown exit is active after DFSMShsm has received a shutdown command or is shutting itself down because of some unanticipated condition. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=exits-arcsdext-shutdown-installation-exit

tape_dataset.description:
(EXITOFF(TD)) Specifies whether the tape data set exit is active when an output tape data set is opened during backup, migration, recycle, or tape copy processing. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=exits-arctdext-tape-data-set-installation-exit

tape_ejected.description:
(EXITOFF(TE)) Specifies whether the tape-ejected exit is active when an input tape is required for recall, data set or volume recovery, data set or volume restore, or volume recycle processing. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=exits-arcteext-tape-ejected-installation-exit

tape_volume.description:
(EXITOFF(TV)) Specifies whether the tape volume exit is active when a DFSMShsm-owned tape no longer contains valid data, and therefore becomes empty. This exit also supports tapes used in ABARS processing. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=exits-arctvext-tape-volume-installation-exit

abars_backup_error.description:
(EXITOFF(BE)) Specifies whether the ABARS backup error exit is active during aggregate backup. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=exits-arcbeext-abars-backup-error-installation-exit#beext

abars_dataset_conflict_resolution.description:
(EXITOFF(CR)) Specifies whether the ABARS data set conflict resolution exit is active during aggregate recovery verification when an INCLUDE data set to be recovered has the same name as a data set already existing at the aggregate recovery site. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=exits-arccrext-abars-conflict-resolution-in-installation

abars_expiration_date.description:
(EXITOFF(ED)) Specifies whether the ABARS expiration data set exit is active prior to allocation of an ABACKUP output file. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=exits-arcedext-abars-expiration-date-installation-exit

abars_migration_level2_dataset.description:
(EXITOFF(M2)) Specifies whether the ABARS migration level 2 data set exit is active during aggregate backup when a data set on a migration level 2 volume is to be backed up. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=daie-arcm2ext-abars-migration-level-2-data-set-installation-exit

abars_dataset_skip.description:
(EXITOFF(SK)) Specifies whether the ABARS data set skip exit is active during aggregate recovery for each data set being restored. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=exits-arcskext-abars-data-set-skip-installation-exit

exit_on.description:
(EXITON) specifies active installation exits. If true is specified for the DFSMShsm installation exit name, the exit will be included in the (EXITON(modname, modname, ...)) parameter for active exits. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-exiton-specifying-active-installation-exits 
 For more information about DFSMShsm installation exits, see z/OS DFSMS Installation Exits. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=zdie-dfsmshsm-installation-exits

dataset_deletion.description:
(EXITON(AD)) Specifies whether the data set deletion exit is active during data set deletion or data set retirement. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=exit-characteristics-arcadext

dataset_backup.description:
(EXITON(BD)) Specifies whether the data set backup exit is active during volume or command data set backup. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=exits-arcbdext-data-set-backup-installation-exit

control_dataset_backup.description:
(EXITON(CB)) Specifies whether the control data set backup exit is active after DFSMShsm creates backup copies of the control data set. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=exits-arccbext-control-data-set-backup-installation-exit

dataset_reblock.description:
(EXITON(CD)) Specifies whether the data set reblock exit is active during recall or recovery processing. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=exits-arccdext-data-set-reblock-installation-exit

initialization.description:
(EXITON(IN)) Specifies whether the initialization exit is active after DFSMShsm startup, before functional subtasks become active. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=exits-arcinext-initialization-installation-exit

space_management.description:
(EXITON(MD) Specifies whether the space management exit is active when a data set fulfills the selection criteria for the level 0 volume being managed, but before the data set migrates or transitions. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=exits-arcmdext-space-management-exit

secondary_migration_dataset.description:
(EXITON(MM)) Specifies whether the second-level migration exit is active when a command or automatic selection process selects to migrate an already migrated data set. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=die-arcmmext-second-level-migration-data-set-installation-exit

space_management_volume.description:
(EXITON(MV)) Specifies whether the space mamagement volume exit is active after DFSMShsm completes processing at level 0 volume during volume space management. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=exits-arcmvext-space-management-volume-installation-exit

recall.description:
(EXITON(RD)) Specifies whether the recall exit is active during recall of non-SMS-managed data sets. This exit is not called for SMS-managed data sets. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=exits-arcrdext-recall-installation-exit

return_priority.description:
(EXITON(RP)) Specifies whether the return-priority exit is active Before a recall, delete, or recover (data set or volume) request is queued. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=exits-arcrpext-return-priority-installation-exit

space_management_and_backup.description:
(EXITON(SA)) Specifies whether the space management and backup exit is active. It is called once for each data set processed during volume space management or backup. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=exits-arcsaext-space-management-backup-installation-exit

shutdown.description:
(EXITON(SD)) Specifies whether the shutdown exit is active after DFSMShsm has received a shutdown command or is shutting itself down because of some unanticipated condition. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=exits-arcsdext-shutdown-installation-exit

tape_dataset.description:
(EXITON(TD)) Specifies whether the tape data set exit is active when an output tape data set is opened during backup, migration, recycle, or tape copy processing 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=exits-arctdext-tape-data-set-installation-exit

tape_ejected.description:
(EXITON(TE)) Specifies whether the tape-ejected exit is active when an input tape is required for recall, data set or volume recovery, data set or volume restore, or volume recycle processing. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=exits-arcteext-tape-ejected-installation-exit

tape_volume.description:
(EXITON(TV)) Specifies whether the tape volume exit is active when a DFSMShsm-owned tape no longer contains valid data, and therefore becomes empty. This exit also supports tapes used in ABARS processing. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=exits-arctvext-tape-volume-installation-exit

abars_backup_error.description:
(EXITON(BE)) Specifies whether the ABARS backup error exit is active during aggregate backup.
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=exits-arcbeext-abars-backup-error-installation-exit#beext

abars_dataset_conflict_resolution.description:
(EXITON(CR)) Specifies whether the ABARS data set conflict resolution exit is active during aggregate recovery verification when an INCLUDE data set to be recovered has the same name as a data set already existing at the aggregate recovery site. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=exits-arccrext-abars-conflict-resolution-in-installation

abars_expiration_date.description:
(EXITON(ED)) Specifies whether the ABARS expiration data set exit is active prior to allocation of an ABACKUP output file. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=exits-arcedext-abars-expiration-date-installation-exit

abars_migration_level2_dataset.description:
(EXITON(M2)) Specifies whether the ABARS migration level 2 data set exit is active during aggregate backup when a data set on a migration level 2 volume is to be backed up. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=daie-arcm2ext-abars-migration-level-2-data-set-installation-exit

abars_dataset_skip.description:
(EXITON(SK)) Specifies whether the ABARS data set skip exit is active during aggregate recovery for each data set being restored. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=exits-arcskext-abars-data-set-skip-installation-exit

https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.title: DFSMShsm ARCCMDxx SETSYS commands for automatic backup and backup prefix functions
https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.description:
(SETSYS AUTOBACKUPSTART AND BACKUPPREFIX) Parameters controlling the automatic backup and backup prefix start environment. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=dsar-setsys-command-establishing-changing-values-dfsmshsm-control-parameters

auto_backup_start.description:
(AUTOBACKUPSTART) An optional parameter specifying the time when automatic backup can start. If you do not specify a nonzero value for hhmm1 during this start up of DFSMShsm, DFSMShsm does not do automatic backup. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-autobackupstart-specifying-when-automatic-backup-is-start

planned_start_time.description:
(hhmm1) The planned time for DFSMShsm to start automatic backup. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-autobackupstart-specifying-when-automatic-backup-is-start

latest_start_time.description:
(hhmm2) The latest time DFSMShsm can start automatic backup. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-autobackupstart-specifying-when-automatic-backup-is-start

stop_time.description:
(hhmm3) The time after which DFSMShsm can no longer start automatic backup of additional volumes. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-autobackupstart-specifying-when-automatic-backup-is-start

backup_prefix.description:
(BACKUPPREFIX) Specifying the prefix (high-level qualifier) for the backup version name or the dump copy data set name. prefix must be defined as 1 to 7 alphanumeric characters; the first character must be alphabetic only. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-backupprefix-specifying-prefix-backup-version-name-dump-copy-data-set-name

nonsms_backup_frequency.description:
(FREQUENCY) Specifying the number of days from 0 to 999 that must have elapsed since the last time DFSMShsm backed up a data set before DFSMShsm will back up the data set again. Parameter does not apply to SMS-managed DASD volumes or data sets. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-frequency-specifying-number-days-between-backup-versions-data-set

incremental_backup.description:
(INCREMENTALBACKUP) Specifies whether to back up only changed data sets during incremental volume backup. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-incrementalbackup-specifying-whether-back-up-only-changed-data-sets-during-incremental-volume-backup

max_tasks_backup.description:
(MAXBACKUPTASKS) The maximum number of volume backup tasks DFSMShsm can process concurrently. Specify a decimal number from 1 to 15. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-maxbackuptasks-specifying-maximum-number-concurrent-volume-backup-tasks

skip_auto_backup_primary.description:
(SKIPABPRIMARY|NOSKIPABPRIMARY) Specifies whether to skip automatic backup of primary volumes. If true (SKIPABPRIMARY), DFSMShsm skips the backup of DFSMShsm‑managed primary volumes during automatic backup. If false (NOSKIPABPRIMARY), DFSMShsm backs up of DFSMShsm-managed primary volumes. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-skipabprimary-noskipabprimary-specifying-whether-skip-automatic-backup-primary-volumes

use_cylinder_managed_space.description:
(USECYLINDERMANAGEDSPACE) Specifies whether to allow use of cylinder managed space for migration copies and backup versions. Specify values true or false. If true, USECYLINDERMANAGEDSPACE(Y) specifies that migration copies and backup versions can reside in EAS. If false, USECYLINDERMANAGEDSPACE(N) specifies that migration copies and backup versions cannot reside in EAS. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-usecylindermanagedspace-specifying-whether-allow-use-cylinder-managed-space-migration-copies-backup-versions
use_cylinder_managed_space.$comments: The default has been changed to USECMS(Y) in release 3.3. If USECMS is not specified or if USECMS is specified, it means USECMS(Y).

nonsms_backup_versions.description:
(VERSIONS) Specifying the maximum number of backup versions to keep for all your non-SMS-managed data sets. Parameter does not apply to SMS-managed DASD volumes or data sets. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-versions-specifying-maximum-number-backup-versions-keep-any-data-set

anyOf.description:
(SPILL|NOSPILL) Specifies whether DFSMShsm can do spill or cleanup processing on full-DASD daily backup volumes during backup volume selection. If true (SPILL), DFSMShsm spills full DASD daily backup volumes when a DASD daily backup volume is needed and none is available. Spill processing moves all but the latest backup version of each data set from the daily backup volumes to the spill backup volumes. If false (NOSPILL), DFSMShsm never spills full DASD daily backup volumes. Instead, DFSMShsm cleans up full DASD daily backup volumes when one is needed and none is available. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-spill-nospill-specifying-whether-dfsmshsm-does-spill-cleanup-processing-full-dasd-daily-backup-volumes

(SPILL) SPILL with ANY or DASD volume type - specifies that DFSMShsm spills full DASD daily backup volumes. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-spill-nospill-specifying-whether-dfsmshsm-does-spill-cleanup-processing-full-dasd-daily-backup-volumes

volume_device_category.description:
(ANY|DASD) Specifies the type of volume can be used for output during spill processing. ANY, Any type of spill backup volume can be used. DASD, Only DASD spill backup volumes are used. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-spill-nospill-specifying-whether-dfsmshsm-does-spill-cleanup-processing-full-dasd-daily-backup-volumes

anyOf.description:
(SPILL) SPILL with TAPE volume type - specifies that DFSMShsm spills full DASD daily backup volumes to tape. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-spill-nospill-specifying-whether-dfsmshsm-does-spill-cleanup-processing-full-dasd-daily-backup-volumes

volume_device_category.description:
(TAPE) Only tape spill backup volumes that can be mounted and written on the specified unittype are used. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-spill-nospill-specifying-whether-dfsmshsm-does-spill-cleanup-processing-full-dasd-daily-backup-volumes

tape_unittype.description:
(unittype) Only tape spill backup volumes that can be mounted and written on the specified unittype are used during spill processing, only valid when volume_device_category is TAPE. Can be a specific device type (3480X, 3480, 3490, 3590-1) or an esoteric unit name. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-spill-nospill-specifying-whether-dfsmshsm-does-spill-cleanup-processing-full-dasd-daily-backup-volumes

anyOf.description:
(BACKUP|NOBACKUP) Specifies that you intend to or do not intend to use DFSMShsm backup, dump, recovery, or expire backup versions. If true (BACKUP), specifies that you intend to use some or all of the following DFSMShsm functions: backup (automatic or command), dump (automatic or command), recovery, and expire backup versions. If false (NOBACKUP), specifies that you do not intend to use DFSMShsm backup, dump, recovery, or expire backup versions. When you specify this parameter, automatic backup and automatic dump are not run, and DFSMShsm fails any backup, dump, recovery, or expire backup versions commands. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-backup-nobackup-specifying-whether-you-intend-use-dfsmshsm-backup-recovery-dump

(BACKUP) Specifies whether you intend to use DFSMShsm backup, recovery, and dump. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-backup-nobackup-specifying-whether-you-intend-use-dfsmshsm-backup-recovery-dump

volume_device_category.description:
(ANY|DASD|TAPE|TAPE(unittype)) The target device type used for volume backups. If BACKUP has been specified but never (within this start-up of DFSMShsm) with any of the ANY|DASD|TAPE options specified, then the default option of ANY is used. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-backup-nobackup-specifying-whether-you-intend-use-dfsmshsm-backup-recovery-dump

device_type.description:
(ANY|DASD|TAPE|TAPE(unittype)) The target device type used for volume backups. If BACKUP has been specified but never (within this start-up of DFSMShsm) with any of the ANY|DASD|TAPE options specified, then the default option of ANY is used. 
 - Any: Any type of daily backup volume (DASD or Tape) defined to DFSMShsm by the ADDVOL can be used for output. 
 - DASD daily: Only DASD daily backup volumes defined by the DFSMShsm ADDVOL command can be used for output. 
 - Tape daily: Only tape daily backup volumes defined to DFSMShsm via the ADDVOL command can be used for output. 
 - Tape unittype: Only tape daily backup volumes that can be mounted and written on the specified type unittype can be used for output. Use the tape_unittype key to specify the unittype. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-backup-nobackup-specifying-whether-you-intend-use-dfsmshsm-backup-recovery-dump

tape_unittype.description:
(unittype) Tape unittype specification. A generic or esoteric unit name can be specified, only valid when volume_device_category is TAPE. Can be a specific device type (3480X, 3480, 3490, 3590-1) or an esoteric unit name. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-backup-nobackup-specifying-whether-you-intend-use-dfsmshsm-backup-recovery-dump

else.title: tape_unittype is only valid with device_type 'Tape unittype'

inuse.description:
(INUSE) INUSE, with its subparameters, specifies how DFSMShsm should handle backing up a data set that is found to be in use (open for update) during volume backup processing. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-backup-nobackup-specifying-whether-you-intend-use-dfsmshsm-backup-recovery-dump

retry.description:
(RETRY) DFSMShsm to retry the backup of data set or does not retry a backup. iF true (RETRY(Y)), DFSMShsm will retry once to back up a data set if the first attempt fails because - the data set is in use, or a BWO candidate suffers a CA/CI split and the backup is discarded. If false (RETRY(N)), DFSMShsm does not retry a backup if the first attempt fails because the data set is in use. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-backup-nobackup-specifying-whether-you-intend-use-dfsmshsm-backup-recovery-dump

delay.description:
(DELAY) DFSMShsm delays for minutes before retrying a backup attempt which failed because a data set was in use. Specify a decimal number between 0 to 999. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-backup-nobackup-specifying-whether-you-intend-use-dfsmshsm-backup-recovery-dump

serialization.description:
(SERIALIZATION) If DFSMShsm retries backing up a data set (after some delay) and finds the data set still (or again) in use, it should back up the data set anyway or fail the backup.
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-backup-nobackup-specifying-whether-you-intend-use-dfsmshsm-backup-recovery-dump

dataset_backup.description:
(DSBACKUP) Allows you to control the command dataset backup environment. You can balance the backup workload between DASD and tape tasks and you can tailor DFSMShsm tape mounting and demounting for command dataset backups. DFSMShsm can run up to 64 concurrent command dataset backup tasks. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-dsbackup-controlling-data-set-backup-environment

generate_vsam_component_names.description:
(GENVSAMCOMPNAMES) Names assigned to the VSAM data and index components. If true (GENVSAMCOMPNAMES(YES)|GVCN(YES)), dsname is a VSAM base cluster and newdsname is either migrated or uncataloged, DFSMShsm will process the request, and default names will be assigned to the VSAM data and index components. If false (GENVSAMCOMPNAMES(NO)|GVCN(NO)), dsname is a VSAM base cluster and newdsname is either migrated or uncataloged, the data set backup command will fail. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-dsbackup-controlling-data-set-backup-environment

dasd_selection_size.description:
(DASDSELECTIONSIZE) Balance the workload between DASD and TAPE tasks for all WAIT-type requests that do not target tape. DASDSELECTIONSIZE is only applicable if both tape and ML1 DASD are allowed for command dataset backups. DFSMShsm directs small data sets (a WAIT-type request) to DASD if a tape task is not immediately available to process the request. DFSMShsm directs NOWAIT requests to tape, if tape tasks are allowed. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-dsbackup-controlling-data-set-backup-environment

maximum.description:
(MAXIMUM) Size, in kilobytes, of the largest data set, (a WAIT-type request) that is directed to ML1 DASD. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-dsbackup-controlling-data-set-backup-environment

standard.description:
(STANDARD) Largest size, in kilobytes, that is considered to be a small data set. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-dsbackup-controlling-data-set-backup-environment

dasd.description:
(DASD) Specify that you want to use ML1 DASD for command data set backups. DASD(TASKS) and TAPE(TASKS) are dependent, and their combined total must be greater than zero and cannot exceed 64; if the sum is 0, any request fails. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-dsbackup-controlling-data-set-backup-environment

tasks.description:
DASD(TASKS) Maximum number of concurrent command dataset backup tasks that DFSMShsm directs to ML1 DASD. Specify a number between 0 to 64. If the number of DASD tasks specified is 0, all command data set backup requests targeting the backup to DASD fail. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-dsbackup-controlling-data-set-backup-environment

tape.description:
(TAPE) Specify that you want to use tape for command data set backups. DASD(TASKS) and TAPE(TASKS) are dependent, and their combined total must be greater than zero and cannot exceed 64; if the sum is 0, any request fails. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-dsbackup-controlling-data-set-backup-environment

tasks.description:
(TAPE(TASKS)) Maximum number of concurrent command dataset backup tasks that DFSMShsm directs to TAPE. Specify a number between 0 to 64. If the number of Tape tasks specified is 0, all command dataset backup requests targeting the backup to TAPE fail. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-dsbackup-controlling-data-set-backup-environment

demount_delay.description:
(DEMOUNTDELAY) Allows to tailor the DFSMShsm tape mounting and demounting for command dataset backup. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-dsbackup-controlling-data-set-backup-environment

max_tasks_idle.description:
(MAXIDLETASKS) The maximum number of tape drives that DEMOUNTDELAY can accommodate. Specify a number between 0 to 64. You can specify a maximum of 64 drives for MAXIDLETASKS, regardless of the number of TAPE tasks specified. However, the effective number of tasks for MAXIDLETASKS is bound by the number of TAPE tasks. So, if you specify MAXIDLETASKS(64) and TAPE(TASKS(5)), the effective MAXIDLETASKS is 5. If at a later time you respecify TAPE(TASKS(7)), the effective MAXIDLETASKS becomes 7. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-dsbackup-controlling-data-set-backup-environment

minutes.description:
(MINUTES) The number of minutes that you want DFSMShsm to wait before it deallocates the tape associated with continuously inactive (idle) command dataset backup tasks. Specify a value between 0 and 1440. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-dsbackup-controlling-data-set-backup-environment

https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.title: DFSMShsm ARCSTRxx RESTART Startup Parameter
https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.description:
(RESTART) Specifies that DFSMShsm should be automatically restarted for all DFSMShsm abnormal ends. The RESTART=‘(a, b)’ keyword specifies that DFSMShsm should be automatically restarted for all DFSMShsm abnormal ends. a specifies the name of the procedure to be started and b specifies any additional keywords or parameters to be passed to the procedure. For example, if the DFSMShsm procedure DFHSM01 is started for all automatic restarts, and EMERG is set to YES, then the RESTART keyword would be specified as: RESTART=‘(DFHSM01.HSM,EMERG=YES)’. Note that in this example HSM can be used by the operator as an identifier for DFHSM01.
Note: If you are accessing your CDSs in RLS mode, use the RESTART keyword so that DFSMShsm automatically restarts after shutting down due to SMS VSAM server error.
https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=keywords-restart

procedure_name.description:
Name of the procedure to be started after abnormal termination of DFSMShsm.
Rule: Any alternate procedures (DFHSM05, for example) must have an entry in the RACF started-procedures table and must be associated with the DFSMShsm user ID for RACF.
https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=spk-using-restart-keyword-automatically-restart-dfsmshsm-after-abnormal-end#userestartkwd

https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.title: DFSMShsm ARCCMDxx SETSYS commands for ABARS functions
https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.description:
(SETSYS) DFSMShsm SETSYS parameters controlling the ABARS functions including: 
  - ABARSACTLOGMSGLVL(FULL | REDUCED) 
  - ABARSACTLOGTYPE(DASD | SYSOUT(class))
  - ABARSBUFFERS(n) 
  - ABARSDELETEACTIVITY(Y | N) 
  - ABARSKIP(PPRC | NOPPRC  XRC | NOXRC)
  - ABARSOPTIMIZE(option)
  - ABARSPROCNAME(name)
  - ABARSTAPES(STACK | NOSTACK)
  - ABARSUNITNAME(unitype)
  - ABARSVOLCOUNT(ANY | NONE)
  - ARECOVERML2UNIT(unitype)
  - ARECOVERPERCENTUTILIZED(nnn)
  - ARECOVERTGTGDS(SOURCE | ACTIVE | DEFERRED | ROLLEDOFF)
  - ARECOVERUNITNAME(unitype)
  - MAXABARSADDRESSSPACE(nn)

abars_activity_log_message_level_full.description:
(ABARSACTLOGMSGLVL(FULL | REDUCED)) Specifies which DFSMSdss messages are written to the log including: 
  - true: (FULL), Specifies that all DFSMSdss messages are intercepted and written to the ABARS activity log. 
  - false: (REDUCED) Specifies that only DFSMSdss warning or error messages are displayed in the ABARS activity log. No informational messages will be written. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-abarsactlogmsglvl-specifying-which-dfsmsdss-messages-are-written-log

abars_activity_log_type.description:
(ABARSACTLOGTYPE(DASD | SYSOUT(class)) Specifies the ABARS activity log output data set type. 
 - The key 'spool_dataset' is a boolen type.  
   - If true, i.e. 'SYSOUT': Messages are written out to a spool data set. It has an optional sub-parameter 'sysout_class', i.e. 'SYSOUT(class)'. If 'sysout_class' is not specified, the default will be the SETSYS ACTLOGTYPE SYSOUT class. 
 - The key 'sysout_class' is for the 'class' in 'SYSOUT(class)', an alphanumeric character for the class ABARS is to use for output.  
   - If false, i.e. 'DASD': DFSMShsm dynamically allocates DASD data sets with a unit name of SYSALLDA and a size of 20 tracks for primary allocation and 50 tracks for secondary allocation. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-abarsactlogtype-specifying-abars-activity-log-output-data-set-type

abars_io_buffer_num.description:
(ABARSBUFFERS(n)) Specifies the number of I/O buffers for ABARS. The number is in the range of 1 to 9 indicating the number of buffers used for I/O processing. If the number of buffers is not specified by the SETSYS ABARSBUFFERS(n) command, the default is one. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-abarsbuffers-specifying-number-io-buffers-abars

abars_delete_activity.description:
(ABARSDELETEACTIVITY(Y | N)) Allows DFSMShsm to automatically delete the ABARS activity log. 
  - Y specifies that DFSMShsm is to delete the ABARS activity log during ABARS processing. 
  - N specifies that no automatic deletion is performed by DFSMShsm. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-abarsdeleteactivity-allowing-dfsmshsm-automatically-delete-abars-activity-log

abars_dataset_skip.description:
(ABARSKIP) Specifies which types of data sets ABACKUP should skip including both 'peer_to_peer_remote_copy' and 'extended_remote_copy'. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-abarskip-specifying-which-types-data-sets-abackup-should-skip

peer_to_peer_remote_copy.description:
peer-to-peer remote copy,  
  - true: ABARSKIP(PPRC) causes ABACKUP processing to skip the data set and not back it up, if a data set in an aggregate group is on a volume or volumes that are protected by peer-to-peer remote copy.  
  - false: ABARSKIP(NOPPRC) causes ABACKUP processing to not skip the corresponding data set and it is backed up. 
 The DFSMShsm default is false, NOPPRC.

extended_remote_copy.description:
extended remote copy, 
  - true: ABARSKIP(XRC) causes ABACKUP processing to skip the data set and not back it up, if a data set is on a volume or volumes protected by extended remote copy.  
  - false: ABARSKIP(NOXRC), causes ABACKUP processing to not skip the corresponding data set and it is backed up. 
 The DFSMShsm default is false, NOXRC.

abars_optimize_option.description:
(ABARSOPTIMIZE(option)) Adjusts performance when backing up level 0 DASD specified in INCLUDE list. It is used to control the value that the ABACKUP function specifies in the OPTIMIZE parameter when invoking DFSMSdss to backup level 0 DASD data sets. The valid specifications for the option value are 1-4: 
  - 1: DFSMSdss reads one track at a time 
  - 2: DFSMSdss reads two tracks at a time 
  - 3: DFSMSdss reads five tracks at a time 
  - 4: DFSMSdss reads one cylinder at a time 
 The default value for option is 3. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-abarsoptimize-adjusting-performance-when-backing-up-level-0-dasd-specified-in-include-list

abars_procedure_name.description:
(ABARSPROCNAME(name)) is used to specify the JCL procedure name used on the START command issued by DFSMShsm to start the ABARS secondary address space. For name, specify a procedure name that conforms to standard MVS JCL naming conventions. 
 If you do not specify a procedure name on any SETSYS command, the DFSMShsm default is DFHSMABR. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-abarsprocname-specifying-base-procedure-name-start-abars-secondary-address-space

abars_tape_stack.description:
(ABARSTAPES(STACK | NOSTACK)) Allows DFSMShsm to stack the ABACKUP output files. 
  - true: ABARSTAPES(STACK), DFSMShsm stacks the ABACKUP output files onto a minimum number of tape volumes. 
  - false: ABARSTAPES(NOSTACK), DFSMShsm does not stack the ABACKUP output files. 
 The default is STACK. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-abarstapes-allowing-dfsmshsm-stack-abackup-output-files

abars_unit_name.description:
(ABARSUNITNAME(unittype)) Specifies the unit to be used when invoking aggregate backup or aggregate recovery. 
 If unitname is not specified by the SETSYS ABARSUNITNAME(unittype) or the UNIT parameter on the ABACKUP or ARECOVER command, it defaults to 3590-1. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-abarsunitname-specifying-unit-name-abars

abars_vol_count.description:
(ABARSVOLCOUNT(ANY | NONE)) is an optional parameter that affects how DFSMShsm will invoke DFSMSdss during the ARECOVER of data sets that were dumped by DFSMSdss. 
  - 'ANY': DFSMShsm passes the VOLCOUNT(ANY) parameter to DFSMSdss during the ARECOVER of data dumped by DFSMSdss (L0 data sets).
