 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-compact-tapemigrate-notapemigrate-specifying-whether-compact-data-sets-during-migration-tape

compact_percent.description:
(COMPACTPERCENT(percent) is an optional parameter specifying the percentage of space saved if DFSMShsm compacts all data sets. For percent, substitute with a decimal number from 0 to 99 to specify the least amount of space you want saved if DFSMShsm compacts a data set. 
 Compaction always occurs during backup processing if SETSYS COMPACTPERCENT(0) is specified and DFSMShsm is to compact the data set. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-compactpercent-specifying-percentage-space-saved-compaction

compact_object_names.description:
(OBJECTNAMES(name1,name2,...)) is an optional parameter specifying the compaction control qualifier of all data sets that should be compacted with the compaction table for object data sets. 
 For name1,name2,..., specify the compaction-control qualifiers of the data set names of those data sets you want to compact with the compaction table for data sets that contain object code. For example, you could specify LINKLIB as a compaction-control qualifier.
compact_object_names.$comment:
Validate low level qualifier of MVS data set names as comma-separated string. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-objectnames-specifying-compaction-control-qualifier-object-data-set

compact_source_names.description:
(SOURCENAMES(name1,name2,...)) is an optional parameter specifying the compaction control qualifier of data sets that should be compacted with the table for source data sets. 
 For name1,name2..., specify the compaction-control qualifiers of the data set names of those data sets you want to compact with the table for data sets that contain source code for programming languages. 
https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-sourcenames-specifying-compaction-control-qualifier-source-data-set
compact_source_names.$comment: Validate low level qualifier of MVS data set names as comma-separated string.

remove_compact_names.description:
(REMOVECOMPACTNAMES(name1,name2,...)) is an optional parameter specifying the compaction-control qualifier of all data sets to be removed from the SOURCENAMES or OBJECTNAMES table. 
 For (name1,name2,...), specify the compaction-control qualifiers of those data sets you no longer want to have compacted by the source or object compaction table. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-removecompactnames-removing-compaction-control-qualifier-source-object-data-sets
remove_compact_names.$comment: Validate MVS data set names either fully qualified or generic, as comma-separated string. Supports variable number of comma-separated values.

z_compress.description:
(ZCOMPRESS) An optional parameter set that you use to specify the type of compression used during migration or backup for all data sets. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-zcompress-specifying-when-compression-zedc-should-be-done

all.description:
(ZCOMPRESS(ALL|NONE)) Specifying whether to use zEDC Services for data sets. ZCOMPRESS(NONE) is the default. 
 If true (ZCOMPRESS(ALL)), it specifies DFSMShsm will use zEDC during migration and backup if this function is supported by the system. If zEDC Services are not available, DFSMShsm will use the SETSYS COMPACT settings to determine what type of software compaction is used for migration and backup. 
 If false (ZCOMPRESS(NONE)), it specifies DFSMShsm does not use zEDC for a data set during migration or backup. DFSMShsm will use the SETSYS COMPACT settings. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-zcompress-none-all-specifying-whether-use-zedc-services-data-sets

cloud_migrate.description:
(ZCOMPRESS(CLOUDMIGRATE(YES|NO)) Specifying whether or not to use CDA compression with zEDC Services when DFSMShsm migrates to DIRECT cloud. 
 If true (CLOUDMIGRATE(YES)), it specifies DFSMShsm will use CDA compression with zEDC Services during migration to DIRECT cloud connections if this function is supported by the system. If CDA compression is unavailable, the data sets will not be compressed during migration to DIRECT cloud connections. 
 If false (CLOUDMIGRATE(NO)), it specifies DFSMShsm does not use CDA compression for migration to DIRECT cloud connections. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-zcompresscloudmigrateno-yes-specifying-whether-use-cda-compression-data-sets-during-migration-direct-cloud-connections

dasd_backup.description:
(ZCOMPRESS(DASDBACKUP(YES|NO)) Specifying whether to use zEDC Services for data sets during backup to DASD. 
 If true (DASDBACKUP(YES)), it specifies DFSMShsm will use zEDC Services during backup to DASD if this function is supported by the system. If zEDC is not available, DFSMShsm will use the SETSYS COMPACT settings to determine what type of software compaction is used for backup. 
 If false (DASDBACKUP(NO)), it specifies DFSMShsm does not use zEDC for a data set backup to DASD. DFSMShsm will use the SETSYS COMPACT settings. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-zcompress-dasdbackup-no-yes-specifying-whether-use-zedc-services-data-sets-during-backup-dasd

dasd_migrate.description:
(ZCOMPRESS(DASDMIGRATE(YES|NO)) Specifying whether to use zEDC Services for data sets during migration to DASD. 
 If true (DASDMIGRATE(YES)), it specifies DFSMShsm will use zEDC Services during migration to DASD if this function is supported by the system. If zEDC is not available, DFSMShsm will use the SETSYS COMPACT settings to determine what type of software compaction is used for migration. 
 If false (DASDMIGRATE(NO)), it specifies DFSMShsm does not use zEDC for a data set migration to DASD. DFSMShsm will use the SETSYS COMPACT settings. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-zcompress-dasdmigrate-no-yes-specifying-whether-use-zedc-services-data-sets-during-migration-dasd

tape_backup.description:
(ZCOMPRESS(TAPEBACKUP(YES|NO)) Specifying whether to use zEDC Services for data sets during backup to tape. 
 If true (TAPEBAKUP(YES)), it specifies DFSMShsm will use zEDC Services during backup to tape, if this function is supported by the system. If zEDC is not available, DFSMShsm will use the SETSYS COMPACT settings to determine what type of software compaction is used for backup. 
 If false (TAPEBACKUP(NO)), it specifies DFSMShsm does not use zEDC for a data set backup to tape. DFSMShsm will use the SETSYS COMPACT settings. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-zcompress-tapebackup-no-yes-specifying-whether-use-zedc-services-data-sets-during-backup-tape

tape_migrate.description:
(ZCOMPRESS(TAPEMIGRATE(YES|NO)) Specifying whether to use zEDC Services for data sets during migration to tape. 
 If true (TAPEMIGRATE(YES)), it specifies DFSMShsm will use zEDC Services during migration to tape if this function is supported by the system. If zEDC is not available, DFSMShsm will use the SETSYS COMPACT settings to determine what type of software compaction is used for migration. 
 If false (TAPEMIGRATE(NO)), it specifies DFSMShsm does not use zEDC for a data set migration to tape. DFSMShsm will use the SETSYS COMPACT settings. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-zcompress-tapemigrate-no-yes-specifying-whether-use-zedc-services-data-sets-during-migration-tape

https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.title: DFSMShsm ARCCMDxx SETSYS commands for tape settings
https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.description:
DFSMShsm ARCCMDxx SETSYS commands for tape settings. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=dsar-setsys-command-establishing-changing-values-dfsmshsm-control-parameters

tape_disaster_mode.description:
(DISASTERMODE) specifying the tape operation mode for DFSMShsm in disaster mode. 
  If specified as true, i.e. (Y), for this parameter on the SETSYS command, DFSMShsm checks the TTOC record of the original tape volume to see if a disaster alternate volume exists and if so, requests the use of it to return the data. 
  - If specified as false, i.e. (N), for this parameter on the SETSYS command or no disaster alternate volume exists, DFSMShsm will request the original tape volume and makes no substitution. 
 If you specify DISASTERMODE without specifying any subparameter, the default is Y. If you do not specify this parameter on any SETSYS command, the DFSMShsm default is N. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-disastermode-specifying-tape-operation-mode-dfsmshsm-in-disaster-mode

extended_tape_table_of_contents.description:
EXTENDEDTTOC(Y|N) specifying whether to use extended tape table of contents (TTOC). 
  - If specified as true, i.e. (Y), it means to use extended TTOCs in your installation. 
  - If specified as false, i.e. (N), it means to return to using non-extended TTOCs. 
 If you do not specify this parameter on any SETSYS command, the DFSMShsm default is not to use extended TTOCs. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-extendedttoc-specifying-whether-use-extended-tape-table-contents-ttoc

wait_input_tape_allocation.description:
INPUTTAPEALLOCATION(WAIT | NOWAIT) specifying whether DFSMShsm should wait until the tape unit is allocated for the input tape for recall, recovery, or restore. 
  - If specified as true, i.e. (WAIT), specifies that DFSMShsm waits until the input tape unit is allocated. All DFSMShsm functions stop until this allocation request is satisfied.  
  - If specified as false, i.e. (NOWAIT),specifies that DFSMShsm does not wait until the input tape unit is allocated. 
 If you do not specify either subparameter on any SETSYS command, the DFSMShsm default is NOWAIT. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-inputtapeallocation-specifying-whether-wait-input-tape-be-allocated

tape_mount_wait_time.description:
(MOUNTWAITTIME) specifying the time, in minutes, that DFSMShsm waits for the tape volume to be mounted and opened. If you do not specify this parameter on any SETSYS command, the DFSMShsm default is 15 minutes. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-mountwaittime-specifying-tape-mount-wait-time

wait_output_tape_allocation.description:
OUTPUTTAPEALLOCATION (WAIT | NOWAIT) specifying whether DFSMShsm should wait until the tape unit is allocated for the output tape for migration or backup. 
  - If specified as true, i.e. (WAIT), DFSMShsm waits until the output tape unit is allocated. Any DFSMShsm function requiring dynamic allocation services will be unable to proceed until this tape unit is allocated.  
  - If specified as false, i.e. (NOWAIT),DFSMShsm does not wait until the output tape unit is allocated. 
 If you do not specify either subparameter on any SETSYS command, the DFSMShsm default is NOWAIT. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-outputtapeallocation-specifying-if-wait-output-tape-be-allocated

preselect_output_tape.description:
(TAPELIBRARYPRESELECT) Preselecting output tape volumes in IBM Tape Library tape environment. 
  - If specified as true, i.e (YES), allow users to have DFSMShsm preselect tape volumes for output in an IBM Tape Library environment. If an existing tape is selected, its volser will be specified to the allocation. 
 If you specify TAPELIBRARYPRESELECT without mentioning any sub parameter, the default is YES. If you do not specify this parameter on any SETSYS command, the DFSMShsm default is NO. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-tapelibrarypreselect-preselecting-output-tape-volumes-in-tape-library-tape-environment

tape_hardware_compact.description:
(TAPEHARDWARECOMPACT | NOTAPEHARDWARECOMPACT) are mutually exclusive, that specify whether the Improved Data Recording Capability (IDRC) should be used when a 3480X is used as the output device. 
  - If specified as true, i.e. (TAPEHARDWARECOMPACT) specifies that DFSMShsm will request that IDRC be used on eligible 3480 tape cartridges. 
  - If specified as false, i.e. (NOTAPEHARDWARECOMPACT) specifies that DFSMShsm will not use IDRC. 
 If you do not specify either TAPEHARDWARECOMPACT or NOTAPEHARDWARECOMPACT, the DFSMShsm default is NOTAPEHARDWARECOMPACT.
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-tapehardwarecompact-specifying-whether-use-tape-hardware-compaction

tape_output_messages_suppress.description:
TAPEOUTPUTPROMPT(TAPECOPY(YES | NO)) allows correct decisions by the operator when mounting a tape during TAPECOPY. 
  - If specified as true, i.e. (YES), DFSMShsm issues a message to the operator during TAPECOPY processing indicating which type of target tape be mounted on a particular device; however, this message goes away after the tape has been mounted. 
  - If specified as false, i.e. (NO), DFSMShsm issues no message to the operator during TAPECOPY processing indicating which type of target tape is to be mounted on a particular device. 
 If you do not specify this parameter on the SETSYS command, the default is NO. If you do specify this parameter on the SETSYS command, a message is issued without requesting a reply when the option to patch the MCVT is not used. If the option to patch the MCVT is used, a message is issued requesting a reply. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-tapeoutputprompt-specifying-whether-suppress-tape-output-messages

min_dataset_size_span_tape.description:
TAPESPANSIZE(nnnn) is used to reduce the occurrences of data sets spanning migration or backup tape volumes. For nnnn, specify a value between 0 and 9999 in units of megabytes (MB). This value is the minimum size of a data set that is allowed to span tape volumes. Data sets whose size is less than the value do not normally span volumes. Only those data sets whose size is greater than or equal to the specified value are allowed to span volumes. 
 If you do not specify TAPESPANSIZE, the default is 500MB. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-tapespansize-reducing-tape-volume-spanning

use_worm_media.description:
TAPETYPE(WORM | NOWORM) pecifies that you want DFSMShsm to use WORM media for non-ABARS functions. 
  - If specified as true, i.e. (WORM), DFSMShsm should allow non-ABARS functions to use WORM media. 
  - If specified as false, i.e. (NOWORM), DFSMShsm should not use WORM media for non-ABARS functions.
  If you do not specify the TAPETYPE parameter on any SETSYS command, DFSMShsm does not use WORM media for non-ABARS functions by default. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-tapetype-specifying-whether-use-worm-media-non-abars-functions

tape_unit_name.description:
UNITNAME(unitname) identifying the type of unit that should be specified the first time DFSMShsm requests that a scratch tape be mounted during backup or dump. 
 If you do not specify this parameter on any SETSYS command, the DFSMShsm default is 3590-1. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-unitname-specifying-tape-unit-name

esoteric_tape_unit.description:
USERUNITTABLE() and NOUSERUNITTABLE specifying esoteric tape unit names to DFSMShsm. It can be specified in two different types. 
  - boolean type: only false is allowed indicating (NOUSERUNITTABLE). 
  - array type: Array of objects where each object specifies an esoteric tape unit. Each object has: 
    - unit_name (required): The esoteric tape unit name to identify to DFSMShsm 
    - translation (optional): Controls translation of esoteric output unit names. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-userunittable-nouserunittable-specifying-esoteric-tape-unit-names-dfsmshsm

unit_name.description: The esoteric tape unit name to identify to DFSMShsm as valid. Output allocations are made to units associated with this esoteric tape unit name.

translation_unit_name.description:
(Optional) The unit name to be used for translation. 
 When you specify a value for translation, the esoteric unit names specified on unit_name and translation are both identified to DFSMShsm as valid. Translation to an esoteric can take place. The esoteric unit name requested for the output allocation (unit_name) may be translated to the esoteric tape unit name specified on this key (translation_unit_name) when output processing is completed. If translation occurs, then when the tape volume is requested to be read, input allocations are made to units associated with this key (translation_unit_name). The purpose of this translation is to allow the user to use different devices for input than output.
 If this key (translation_unit_name) is omitted, the esoteric tape unit name specified by the key unit_name is identified to DFSMShsm as valid. Output allocations are made to units associated with the particular esoteric tape unit name requested for the output function. Any cartridge loader esoteric translation is assigned to the generic unit name equivalent to the type of units associated with the esoteric tape unit name.

reuse_partially_full_tape.description:
(PARTIALTAPE) specifying that you want DFSMShsm to mark a cartridge-type single-file formatted tape volume full when the volume has been demounted. Three boolean subkeys can be specified, including 'all', 'migration', 'backup'. 'all' is exclusive to either 'migration' or 'backup'. If 'all' specified, that setup applies to both migration and backup tapes. 
  - If specified as true, i.e. (REUSE), DFSMShsm uses the normal process of marking a single-file formatted tape full only when the percent ful 
  - If specified as false, i.e. (MARKFULL), DFSMShsm automatically marks a single-file-formatted tape volume full (except after data set migration or data set backup) independent of the block count when it demounts the tape. 
 The default is REUSE, meaning that DFSMShsm marks the tape volume full only when the volume reaches the maximum block count specified with the SETSYS TAPEUTILIZATION parameter. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-partialtape-specifying-whether-reuse-partially-full-tapes

all.description:
This setup applies to both migration and backup tapes. 
  - If specified as true, i.e. (REUSE), DFSMShsm uses the normal process of marking a single-file formatted tape full only when the percent ful 
  - If specified as false, i.e. (MARKFULL), DFSMShsm automatically marks a single-file-formatted tape volume full (except after data set migration or data set backup) independent of the block count when it demounts the tape. 
 The default is REUSE, meaning that DFSMShsm marks the tape volume full only when the volume reaches the maximum block count specified with the SETSYS TAPEUTILIZATION parameter.

migration.description:
MIGRATION(REUSE | MARKFULL)
  - If specified as true, i.e. (REUSE), DFSMShsm uses the normal process of marking a single-file formatted tape full only when the percent ful 
  - If specified as false, i.e. (MARKFULL), DFSMShsm automatically marks a single-file-formatted tape volume full (except after data set migration or data set backup) independent of the block count when it demounts the tape.

backup.description:
BACKUP(REUSE | MARKFULL)
  - If specified as true, i.e. (REUSE), DFSMShsm uses the normal process of marking a single-file formatted tape full only when the percent ful 
  - If specified as false, i.e. (MARKFULL), DFSMShsm automatically marks a single-file-formatted tape volume full (except after data set migration or data set backup) independent of the block count when it demounts the tape.

scratch_tape_select.description:
(SELECTVOLUME) specifying whether DFSMShsm chooses a tape volume owned by DFSMShsm or a scratch tape volume when an end-of-volume (EOV) condition occurs while DFSMShsm is writing on a tape volume.  Four boolean subkeys can be specified, including 'all', 'migration', 'backup', 'dump'.'all' is exclusive to either 'migration', 'dump', or 'backup'. If 'all' specified, that setup applies to migration, backup and dump tapes. 
  - If specified as true, i.e. (SCRATCH), A PRIVAT mount request is always sent to the operator when an EOV condition occurs on a tape backup volume, tape migration level 2 volume, or dump tape volume. The operator should mount a private scratch tape volume. 
  - If specified as false, i.e. (SPECIFIC), DFSMShsm chooses another tape volume when an EOV condition occurs on a tape backup volume, tape migration level 2 volume, or dump tape volume. 
 If you do not specify either parameter on any SETSYS command, the DFSMShsm default is SCRATCH. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-selectvolume-specifying-whether-dfsmshsm-should-select-scratch-tape-volume-dfsmshsm-tape-volume

all.description:
This setup applies to migration, backup and dump tapes. 
  - If specified as true, i.e. (SCRATCH), A PRIVAT mount request is always sent to the operator when an EOV condition occurs on a tape backup volume, tape migration level 2 volume, or dump tape volume. The operator should mount a private scratch tape volume. 
  - If specified as false, i.e. (SPECIFIC), DFSMShsm chooses another tape volume when an EOV condition occurs on a tape backup volume, tape migration level 2 volume, or dump tape volume. 
 If you do not specify either parameter on any SETSYS command, the DFSMShsm default is SCRATCH.

migration.description:
MIGRATION(SCRATCH | SPECIFIC) 
  - If specified as true, i.e. (SCRATCH), A PRIVAT mount request is always sent to the operator when an EOV condition occurs on a tape tape migration level 2 volume. The operator should mount a private scratch tape volume. 
  - If specified as false, i.e. (SPECIFIC), DFSMShsm chooses another tape volume when an EOV condition occurs on a tape migration level 2 volume. 
 If you do not specify either parameter on any SETSYS command, the DFSMShsm default is SCRATCH.

backup.description:
BACKUP(SCRATCH | SPECIFIC) 
  - If specified as true, i.e. (SCRATCH), A PRIVAT mount request is always sent to the operator when an EOV condition occurs on a tape backup volume. The operator should mount a private scratch tape volume. 
  - If specified as false, i.e. (SPECIFIC), DFSMShsm chooses another tape volume when an EOV condition occurs on a tape backup volume. 
 If you do not specify either parameter on any SETSYS command, the DFSMShsm default is SCRATCH.

dump.description:
DUMP(SCRATCH | SPECIFIC) 
  - If specified as true, i.e. (SCRATCH), A PRIVAT mount request is always sent to the operator when an EOV condition occurs on a dump tape volume. The operator should mount a private scratch tape volume. 
  - If specified as false, i.e. (SPECIFIC), DFSMShsm chooses another tape volume when an EOV condition occurs on a dump tape volume. 
 If you do not specify either parameter on any SETSYS command, the DFSMShsm default is SCRATCH.

tape_processing_order.description:
(TAPEDATASETORDER) specifies the order in which you want DFSMShsm to recall or recover data sets from a single tape. Three string type subkeys can be specified, including 'all', 'recall', 'recover'.'all' is exclusive to either 'recall' or 'recover'. If 'all' specified, that setup applies to both recall and recover processing. Two optional strings can be specified. 
  - 'PRIORITY': DFSMShsm processes data sets in the priority order. Data sets within the same priority are processed in the FIFO order. 
  - FBID: DFSMShsm processes the data sets in the ascending file block id order. 
 If you do not enter the TAPEDATASETORDER command, the DFSMShsm default is PRIORITY. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-tapedatasetorder-specifying-order-processing-tape

all.description:
If 'all' specified, that setup applies to both recall and recover processing. Two optional strings can be specified. 
  - 'PRIORITY': DFSMShsm processes data sets in the priority order. Data sets within the same priority are processed in the FIFO order. 
  - FBID: DFSMShsm processes the data sets in the ascending file block id order. 
 If you do not enter the TAPEDATASETORDER command, the DFSMShsm default is PRIORITY.

recall.description:
RECALL(PRIORITY | FBID) 
  - 'PRIORITY': DFSMShsm RECALL processes data sets in the priority order. Data sets within the same priority are processed in the FIFO order. 
  - FBID: DFSMShsm RECALL processes the data sets in the ascending file block id order.

recover.description:
RECOVER(PRIORITY | FBID) 
  - 'PRIORITY': DFSMShsm RECOVER processes data sets in the priority order. Data sets within the same priority are processed in the FIFO order. 
  - FBID: DFSMShsm RECOVER processes the data sets in the ascending file block id order.

tape_deletion_scratch.description:
(TAPEDELETION) specifying whether recycled tape volumes be deleted from DFSMShsm control and become scratch tapes, or are to remain under DFSMShsm control as unassigned, available tape backup volumes, migration level 2 volumes, or dump volumes. Four boolean subkeys can be specified, including 'all', 'migration', 'backup', 'dump'.'all' is exclusive to either 'migration', 'dump', or 'backup'. If 'all' specified, that setup applies to migration, backup and dump tapes. 
  - If specified as true, i.e. (SCRATCHTAPE), the recycled tape volumes are deleted from DFSMShsm control and become scratch tapes after DFSMShsm recycles them.  
  - If specified as false, i.e. (HSMTAPE), the recycled volumes remain under DFSMShsm control and become either unassigned backup volumes or available migration level 2 volumes, based on the previous definition of the volume. The tape volume is now available to be selected as a daily or spill backup volume, or as a target volume for data set migration, volume migration, or recycling of tape migration level 2 or dump volumes. 
 If you do not specify this parameter on any SETSYS command, the DFSMShsm default is SCRATCHTAPE. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-tapedeletion-specifying-what-do-tapes-that-no-longer-contain-valid-data

all.description:
If 'all' specified, that setup applies to migration, backup and dump tapes. 
  - If specified as true, i.e. (SCRATCHTAPE), the recycled tape volumes are deleted from DFSMShsm control and become scratch tapes after DFSMShsm recycles them.  
  - If specified as false, i.e. (HSMTAPE), the recycled volumes remain under DFSMShsm control and become either unassigned backup volumes or available migration level 2 volumes, based on the previous definition of the volume. The tape volume is now available to be selected as a daily or spill backup volume, or as a target volume for data set migration, volume migration, or recycling of tape migration level 2 or dump volumes. 
 If you do not specify this parameter on any SETSYS command, the DFSMShsm default is SCRATCHTAPE.

migration.description:
MIGRATION(SCRATCHTAPE | HSMTAPE) 
  - If specified as true, i.e. (SCRATCHTAPE), the recycled tape volumes are deleted from DFSMShsm control and become scratch tapes after DFSMShsm recycles them.  
  - If specified as false, i.e. (HSMTAPE), the recycled volumes remain under DFSMShsm control and become available migration level 2 volumes based on the previous definition of the volume. The tape volume is now available to be selected as a target volume for data set migration, volume migration, or recycling of tape migration level 2. 
 If you do not specify this parameter on any SETSYS command, the DFSMShsm default is SCRATCHTAPE.

backup.description:
BACKUP(SCRATCHTAPE | HSMTAPE) 
  - If specified as true, i.e. (SCRATCHTAPE), the recycled tape volumes are deleted from DFSMShsm control and become scratch tapes after DFSMShsm recycles them.  
  - If specified as false, i.e. (HSMTAPE), the recycled volumes remain under DFSMShsm control and become unassigned backup volumes based on the previous definition of the volume. The tape volume is now available to be selected as a daily or spill backup volume. 
 If you do not specify this parameter on any SETSYS command, the DFSMShsm default is SCRATCHTAPE.

dump.description:
DUMP(SCRATCHTAPE | HSMTAPE) 
  - If specified as true, i.e. (SCRATCHTAPE), the recycled tape volumes are deleted from DFSMShsm control and become scratch tapes after DFSMShsm recycles them.  
  - If specified as false, i.e. (HSMTAPE), the recycled volumes remain under DFSMShsm control and become a dump volume based on the previous definition of the volume. The tape volume is now available to be selected as a dump volume. 
 If you do not specify this parameter on any SETSYS command, the DFSMShsm default is SCRATCHTAPE.

tape_input_messages_suppress.description:
(TAPEINPUTPROMPT) specifies whether DFSMShsm should issue action messages to the operator asking if input tapes needed by DFSMShsm are available. Each function using tapes (backup, migration, dump) is handled separately by specifiying specific keys in boolean type including 'migration', 'backup', 'dump'. 
  - If specified as true, i.e. (YES), that allows DFSMShsm to continue normal operation, which is to issue action messages ARC0313A, ARC0314A, and ARC0366A.  
  - If specified as false, i.e. (NO), that allows you to suppress the input messages, if they are not necessary in your system configuration.

tape_utilization_backup.description:
(TAPEUTILIZATION(LIBRARYBACKUP() | LIBRARYMIGRATION()) is used to specify the desired tape utilization for a backup or migration tape written in single-file format stored in an SMS-managed tape library. The key 'lib_backup' is for backup tape volume and the key 'lib_migration' is for migration tape volume. The specification for those two keys are the same including two exclusive subkeys, either 'nolimit' or 'percent_full'. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-tapeutilization-specifying-desired-tape-utilization

lib_backup.description:
Two exclusive subkeys,'nolimit' or 'percent_full, can be specified. 
  - 'nolimit': boolean type, only 'true' is allowed, means there is no tape limiting, no action is taken to reduce data set tape volume spanning and DFSMShsm writes data until the end-of-volume is reached. 
  -n 'percent_full': percentage of size of a volume used before spanning. More detail is at 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-tapeutilization-specifying-desired-tape-utilization   
 For TAPEUTILIZATION the DFSMShsm default value is 97%.

percent_full.description:
PERCENTFULL(pct), percentage of size of a volume used before spanning. If you have tape cartridges that have a capacity larger than the IBM enhanced-capacity tape cartridges, it is recommended that you specify the PERCENTFULL(pct) parameter for the unit type when those tapes will be used instead of specifying NOLIMIT. For pct, specify a value between 1 and 9999. More detail is at 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-tapeutilization-specifying-desired-tape-utilization   
 For TAPEUTILIZATION the DFSMShsm default value is 97%.

nolimit.description: (NOLIMIT), boolean type, only 'true' is allowed, means there is no tape limiting, no action is taken to reduce data set tape volume spanning and DFSMShsm writes data until the end-of-volume is reached.

(TAPEUTILIZATION(UNITTYPE(unittype)) is used to specify the desired tape utilization for a backup or migration tape written in single-file format outside of any library. Multiple items can be specified as an array below 'tape_utilization_unittype'. The subkeys of each item including: 
  - 'unit_type': tape unit name 
  - 'capacity_mode': the maximum capacity to which a tape is filled 
  - 'percent_full': percentage of tape capacity used 
  - 'nolimit': no limit on tape utilization 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-tapeutilization-specifying-desired-tape-utilization

unit_type.description: UNITTYPE(unittype) Specify a tape unit name.

capacity_mode.description:
CAPACITYMODE(COMPATIBILITY | EXTENDED) specifies the maximum capacity to which a tape is filled. Two exclusive optional string specifications: 
  - 'COMPATIBILITY' specifies that an IBM® 3590 that emulates an IBM 3490 fills a tape to no more than the capacity allowed by an IBM 3590 that emulates an IBM 3490 that is not operating in extended capacity mode. 
  - 'EXTENDED' specifies that an IBM 3590 that emulates an IBM 3490 fills a tape to the same capacity as 3590 drives allow.

For pct, specify a value between 1 and 9999. More detail is at

tape_duplex.description:
(DUPLEX) allows DFSMShsm to create two tapes concurrently, the original tape intended to be kept onsite and the alternate tape taken offsite or written to a remote tape library. Two keys are available to be specified, 'migration' and 'backup'. 
 When either BACKUP or MIGRATION is specified with no subparameter, the default is Y. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-duplex-allowing-dfsmshsm-create-two-tapes-concurrently

migration.description:
MIGRATION(Y|N) determines whether duplex alternates will or will not be made for migration volumes. It can be either specifed as 
  - a boolean with constant value 'false', i.e. MIGRATION(N), no duplexing for migration volumes, 
  or 
  - an object with two exclusive optional subkey 'error_alternate_tapecopy' and 'error_alternate_mark_full', which specifies the process if an error occurs on the alternate volume.

error_alternate_tapecopy.description:
ERRORALTERNATE(CONTINUE(TAPECOPY | RECYCLE)) specifies that if an error occurs on the alternate volume, then the processing will continue on the original tape. 
  - If true, i.e. CONTINUE(TAPECOPY), A TCN record for tapecopy is created and written to OCDS. The TCN record indicates that TAPECOPY should be used to create the duplex tape. This is the default if neither TAPECOPY nor RECYCLE are specified. 
  If false, i.e. CONTINUE(RECYCLE), A TCN record for recycle is created and written to OCDS. The TCN record indicates that the original volume should be recycled in order to create new original and duplex tapes.

error_alternate_mark_full.description: ERRORALTERNATE(MARKFULL) that both the original and alternate tapes will be marked full if an error occurs on the alternate tape and the failing data set will be retried on a new set of tapes. It is boolean type and only true value is allowed. If you want to the processing continue on the original tape, specify key 'error_alternate_tapecopy' instead.

backup.description:
BACKUP(Y|N) determines whether duplex alternates will or will not be made for backup volumes. It can be either specifed as 
  - a boolean with constant value 'false', i.e. BACKUP(N), no duplexing for backup volumes, 
  or 
  - an object with two exclusive optional subkey 'error_alternate_tapecopy' and 'error_alternate_mark_full', which specifies the process if an error occurs on the alternate volume.

error_alternate_tapecopy.description:
ERRORALTERNATE(CONTINUE(TAPECOPY | RECYCLE)) specifies that if an error occurs on the alternate volume, then the processing will continue on the original tape. 
  - If true, i.e. CONTINUE(TAPECOPY), A TCN record for tapecopy is created and written to OCDS. The TCN record indicates that TAPECOPY should be used to create the duplex tape. This is the default if neither TAPECOPY nor RECYCLE are specified. 
  If false, i.e. CONTINUE(RECYCLE), A TCN record for recycle is created and written to OCDS. The TCN record indicates that the original volume should be recycled in order to create new original and duplex tapes.

https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.title: DFSMShsm SWITCHTAPES Command Schema
https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.description: Schema for DFSMShsm SWITCHTAPES command -releasing mounted tapes for command data set backup

oneOf.description:
(PARTIALTAPE)) specifies the method that DFSMShsm uses to mark a single-file format output tape as full or available for reuse when a switch tape event occurs.
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opdc-switchtapes-releasing-mounted-tapes-command-data-set-backup

(PARTIALTAPE(SETSYS))) specifies that the SETSYS PARTIALTAPE value is used.(PARTIALTAPE(REUSE))) specifies that all partial tapes demounted with the SWITCHTAPES option remain selectable in the DFSMShsm inventory as partial tapes.(MARKFULL))) specifies that DFSMShsm marks full all partial tapes demounted with the SWITCHTAPES option. If backups are going to the IBM® Virtual Tape Server (VTS) subsystem, refer to the SETSYS PARTIALTAPE parameter description for performance considerations.Either PARTIALTAPE can be given alone or with anyone of the subparameter.It Cannot be specified multiple times.
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opdc-switchtapes-releasing-mounted-tapes-command-data-set-backup

dataset_backup.description:
(DSBACKUP) - Required subparameter that specifies that the data set backup function performs a demount of all mounted data set backup tapes. Default behavior: TIME(0) - no demount occurs.
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opdc-switchtapes-releasing-mounted-tapes-command-data-set-backup

oneOf.description: DSBACKUP with TIME and optional PARTIALTAPE (mutually exclusive with AUTOBACKUPEND)

ds_time.description:
(TIME(hhmm))) specifies the time of day to demount mounted data set backup tapes. For hhmm, specify the planned demount time. If you specify TIME with hhmm as zero, DFSMShsm does not demount any mounted tapes. If the tape is mounted but not actively processing a data set, the demount occurs at the time indicated by TIME. If a tape is actively processing a data set, DFSMShsm demounts the tape at the end of the current data set.(The hhmm format expresses time as a four-digit decimal number that is based on the 24-hour clock. The hh specifies the hour and mm specifies the minutes. For example, you can specify 1:15 p.m. as 1315, and you can specify midnight as 2400. The maximum value you can specify for hh is 24, the maximum value you can specify for mm is 59, and the maximum value you can specify for hhmm is 2400).TIME and AUTOBACKUPEND are mutually exclusive.
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opdc-switchtapes-releasing-mounted-tapes-command-data-set-backup

oneOf.description: DSBACKUP with AUTOBACKUPEND and optional PARTIALTAPE (mutually exclusive with TIME)

auto_backup_end.description:
(AUTOBACKUPEND)) specifies that DFSMShsm demounts all tapes that were mounted for data set backup at the end of the autobackup cycle. Before the autobackup cycle ends, all retries (data sets that were in use when the initial attempt to backup occurred) complete.TIME and AUTOBACKUPEND are mutually exclusive.
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opdc-switchtapes-releasing-mounted-tapes-command-data-set-backup

command.description:
(CMD) Specifies the PARMLIB member that DFSMShsm should start with. The CMD=00 keyword refers to the ARCCMD00 member of a PARMLIB and is discussed in Parameter libraries (PARMLIB). Throughout the DFSMShsm library the term ARCCMDxx is used to discuss the PARMLIB member. You can create more than one ARCCMDxx member and designate a different number for each PARMLIB member you create by substituting a number for xx (the last two characters of the ARCCMDxx member).
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=keywords-cmd-default-00

emergency.description:
(EMERG) Specifies whether DFSMShsm starts processing immediately. The EMERG=NO keyword allows DFSMShsm to begin functioning as soon as it is started. The EMERG=YES keyword allows DFSMShsm to start, but does not allow DFSMShsm to perform any functions until a SETSYS NOEMERGENCY command is issued.Set EMER to TRUE to indicate EMERG=YES; otherwise, set it to FALSE.
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=keywords-emerg-default-no

log_dataset_swap.description:
(LOGSW) Specifies whether to swap the DFSMShsm log data sets automatically at startup. Because the problem determination aid (PDA) logs are automatically swapped at startup, you should specify LOGSW=YES to synchronize the DFSMShsm logs with the PDA logs. If you specify LOGSW=YES, you must also change your JCL disposition (DISP) to DISP=OLD for the LOGX and LOGY data sets.TRUE to indicate YES; otherwise, set it to FALSE. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=keywords-logsw-default-no

startup.description:
(STARTUP) Specifies whether DFSMShsm displays startup messages at the operator console. set TRUE to indicate YES; otherwise, set it to FALSE. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=keywords-startup-default-no.

user_id.description:
(UID) Specifies the DFSMShsm authorized-user identification (UID) in 1 to 7 characters. You must use this UID as the first qualifier of the data set name of the SDSP data sets. In the DFSMShsm starter set sample jobs (see DFSMShsm starter set), the UID is the prefix name for the migrated and backed up data sets. The UID is also the first qualifier of the DFSMShsm log in the DFSMShsm started procedure in topic Starter set example. For the starter set, HSM is the UID. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=keywords-uid-default-hsm

host_mode.description:
(HOSTMODE)Specifies whether a DFSMShsm instance operates as MAIN (the single primary host per z/OS image that processes implicit and explicit user requests, manages ABARS, accepts MODIFY commands, and runs automatic backup/dump/space management) or as AUX (one or more optional hosts per image that accept MODIFY commands and can run automatic backup, dump, or space management); if not specified, the default is MAIN. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=keywords-hostmode-default-main

host.description:
(HOST) Unique identifier for the DFSMShsm host. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=keywords-hostx

primary.description:
(PRIMARY) Specifies whether this DFSMShsm host is the primary host within its HSMplex, and thus performs the backup and dump level functions as part of automatic processing. Automatic primary space management and automatic secondary management can be performed on any DFSMShsm host.
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=keywords-primary-default-yes

control_data_set_enqueue.description:
(CDSQ) Specifies that DFSMShsm serializes its control data sets with a global enqueue product (GRS for example) instead of serializing with volume reserves.
When you specify YES for this parameter, DFSMShsm serializes the use of the control data sets (between multiple z/OS images) with a global (SYSTEMS) exclusive enqueue and still allows multiple tasks within a single z/OS image to access the control data sets concurrently. All DFSMShsm hosts within an HSMplex must use the same serialization technique.
If you specify CDSQ=NO (without CDSSHR=RLS), the only allowable HOSTMODE for any DFSMShsm host within the HSMplex is MAIN.
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=keywords-cdsq

control_data_set_reserve.description:
(CDSR) Specifies that DFSMShsm serializes its control data sets with volume reserves.
If you have installed a global resource serialization (GRS) product, you can serialize your CDSs with GRS.
When you specify YES for this parameter, DFSMShsm serializes the use of the control data sets with a shared ENQ/RESERVE.
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=keywords-cdsr

control_data_set_shared.description:
(CDSSHR) Specifies that the DFSMShsm being started will run in a particular multiple-image or single-image environment.
 YES - DFSMShsm does multiple-host serialization of the type requested by the CDSQ and CDSR keywords.
 NO - DFSMShsm does no multiple-host serialization; no other systemshould be concurrently processing this set of CDSs. The HOSTMODE of this DFSMShsm can only be MAIN.For performance reasons, specify NO in a single image environment with no auxiliary hosts and where theindex of the MCDS is on a DASD device that is configured as shared.
 RLS - DFSMShsm performs multiple-host serialization using record level sharing (RLS). When RLS is specified, the CDSs are accessed in RLS mode and any values specified for CDSQ and CDSR are ignored.
If you do not specify the CDSSHR keyword in the startup procedure, DFSMShsmperforms multiple-host serialization if the index component of the MCDS resides on a DASD volume that has been SYSGENed as SHARED or SHAREDUP.
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=keywords-cdsshr

cells.description:
(CELLS) DFSMShsm uses the cell-pool (CPOOL) function of MVS to obtain and manage virtual storage in its address space for the dynamically obtained storage for certain high-usage modules, and for data areas DFSMShsm frequently gets and frees.The CELLS parameter provides the cell sizes for five cell pools.

host_type.description:
(HOSTTYPE) Specifies whether this DFSMShsm host should exclusively process UNIX files.
 FILE - user requests for UNIX files are automatically directed to this DFSMShsm host. The RNAMEDSN=YES and CDSR=NO options are required or defaulted. This host will not do any processing for No Volume or data sets. The default HSMplex name is ARCFILE0.
	 Restrictions:
- The HSMplex name for this host must not be the same as any Classic HSM or Full Support HSM in the sysplex.
- Do not specify PLEX0 on the SETSYS PLEXNAME() command.
 CLASSIC - user requests for UNIX files are not directed to this DFSMShsm host.
 FULL - the DFSMShsm host can process both volumes, data sets, and UNIX files. This type of host cannot coexist in the same system as a DFSMShsm host started with HOSTTYPE=FILE or HOSTTYPE=CLASSIC.
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=keywords-hosttypefullclassicfile

problem_determination_aid.description:
(PDA) Specifies that problem determination aid (PDA) tracing begins before the SETSYS PDA command has been processed. When you specify YES for this parameter, the DFSMShsm problem determination aid facility begins its tracing functions at the beginning of startup processing instead of waiting for a SETSYS PDA command or instead of waiting for DFSMShsm to complete its initialization.
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=keywords-pda-default-yes

rnamedsn.description:
(RNAMEDSN) Specifies whether to use a new serialization method so that there is no longer interference between HSMplexes that are contained within a single GRSplex. When you specify YES for this parameter, you are invoking the new method of serialization, which uses the data set name of the CDSs and the journal.
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=keywords-rnamedsn-default-no

startup_parameters_member.description:
(STR) Specifies a PARMLIB member containing DFSMShsm startup parameters, which are logically concatenated with any remaining parameters specified on the EXEC statement. The value for the STR keyword must be two characters, but it need not be the same as the value for the CMD keyword.
 If a keyword is specified both with PARM= and in the ARCSTRxx member, the specification in PARM= overrides that in the member.
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=keywords-str

provider.description: (PROVIDER) Global default cloud provider name used for all storage groups without a per-group provider. Must match the name defined in a Cloud Data Access (CDA) provider definition file. Valid characters: uppercase alphabetic, numeric, @, #, $. Required if CONTAINER is specified at the global level.

container.description: (CONTAINER) Global default container (bucket) name used for all storage groups without a per-group container. Must be 3-63 characters containing only A-Z, a-z, 0-9, period, and hyphen. Required if PROVIDER is specified at the global level.

cda_alternate_credentials.description: (CDAALTCRED) Cloud Data Access alternate credentials setting

storage_groups.description: Array of storage group configurations for this SETDISK statement

name.description: (STORAGEGROUP) Object or object backup storage group name

file_system_type.description: (L2TYPE) File system type. ZFS for z/OS File System, NFS for Network File System. This value is static and cannot be changed.

file_system_directory.description: (L2DIR) File system directory path for storing objects. This value is static and cannot be changed. Must remain available in SETDISK statement for object retrieval.

provider.description: (PROVIDER) Global default cloud provider name used for all storage groups without a per-group provider. Must match the name defined in a Cloud Data Access (CDA) provider definition file. Valid characters: uppercase alphabetic, numeric, @, #, $. Required if CONTAINER is specified at the global level.

container.description: (CONTAINER) Global default container (bucket) name used for all storage groups without a per-group container. Must be 3-63 characters containing only A-Z, a-z, 0-9, period, and hyphen. Required if PROVIDER is specified at the global level.

cda_alternate_credentials.description: (CDAALTCRED) Cloud Data Access alternate credentials setting

data_class.description: (DATACLASS) Optional SMS data class applied to Object and Object Backup storage groups that do not have their own DATACLASS on the STORAGEGROUP subparameter. Controls tape device selection, encryption, performance scaling, and volume expiration.

dsn_with_sg_name.description: (DSNWITHSGNAME) When true, appends the storage group name as a low-level qualifier to OAM tape data set names (e.g., OAM.PRIMARY.DATA.GROUP55). Allows tape management systems to associate scratch pools with specific storage groups.

tape_sdb.description: (TAPESDB) Controls the maximum block size for tape volumes. SMALL caps the block size at 32760 bytes. LARGE allows the system-determined optimal block size up to the maximum permitted. Global specification only; cannot be updated dynamically.

disable_open_type_j.description: (DISABLEOPENTYPEJ) Specifies whether Open Type=J transitions from input to output are disabled. Use INOUT when using the IBM TS7700 with synchronous mode copy to prevent synchronous deferred state. Global specification only. Default: NO.

tape_recycle_mode.description: (TAPERECYCLEMODE) Disposition of expired tape volumes. GROUP keeps them in their current storage group. MVSSCRATCH returns them to the MVS scratch pool. OAMSCRATCH places them in OAM scratch for reassignment. Default: GROUP.

max_recycle_tasks.description: (MAXRECYCLETASKS) Global maximum number of concurrent MOVEVOL tasks for RECYCLE processing. A value of 0 disables RECYCLE. Range: 0-15. Default: 1.

percent_valid.description: (PERCENTVALID) Global default threshold percentage of valid data used to determine whether a full tape volume is a candidate for RECYCLE processing. Overridden by the PV= value on the RECYCLE command. Range: 0-100. Default: 0.

demount_wait_time.description: (DEMOUNTWAITTIME) Time in seconds OAM waits before demounting and deallocating an idle tape drive. When the interval expires, OAM rewinds, unloads, and releases the device. Range: 1-9999. Default: 120.

tape_dispatcher_delay.description: (TAPEDISPATCHERDELAY) Seconds OAM waits before demounting a tape volume to allow a new read request for the same volume to arrive, reducing unnecessary mounts. Global specification only. Range: 1-60.

mount_wait_time.description: (MOUNTWAITTIME) Time in minutes OAM waits for a tape volume to be mounted before issuing message CBR6405D to the operator. Range: 1-120. Default: 5.

max_tape_retrieve_tasks.description: (MAXTAPERETRIEVETASKS) Maximum number of concurrent OAM tasks reading objects from tape. Controls the maximum number of tape drives concurrently allocated for read operations. Range: 1-100. Default: 1.

max_tape_store_tasks.description: (MAXTAPESTORETASKS) Maximum number of tape drives used for writing objects to tape volumes. Together with max_tape_retrieve_tasks, controls the total drives concurrently allocated to OAM. Range: 1-100. Default: 1.

alloc_retry_minutes.description: (ALLOCRETRYMINUTES) Time in minutes OAM retries dynamic tape allocation after a failure before issuing message CBR6400D. A value of 0 skips retries and issues CBR6400D immediately. Range: 0-5. Default: 5.

tape_expiration.description: (TAPEEXPIRATION) Year and day (YYYY/DDD) assigned to OAM tape data set expiration dates, overriding the DATACLASS expiration. Use 1999/365 or 1999/366 as a never-scratch date. YYYY: 1900-2155; DDD: 001-366.

tape_compaction.description: (TAPECOMPACTION / NOTAPECOMPACTION) When true, enables the tape drive compaction feature for this storage group (TAPECOMPACTION). When false, disables it (NOTAPECOMPACTION). If omitted, compaction is determined by DATACLASS or DEVSUPxx.

tape_percent_full.description: (TAPEPERCENTFULL) Percent utilization at which OAM stops writing to a tape volume and marks it full. Applied retroactively to all volumes in the storage group at OAM startup. Range: 1-100. Default: 100.

tape_full_threshold.description: (TAPEFULLTHRESHOLD) Free space threshold in kilobytes below which a tape volume is marked full and excluded from further writes. Default: 0.

l2_data_class.description: (L2DATACLASS) Optional SMS data class for Object storage groups using tape sublevel 2. Controls media type, encryption, and performance scaling for sublevel-2 tape allocations. Does not apply to Object Backup storage groups.

l2_tape_unit_name.description: (L2TAPEUNITNAME) MVS esoteric or generic unit name OAM uses when allocating scratch tape for tape sublevel 2 writes. Required when using the tape sublevel 2 function. Does not apply to Object Backup storage groups.

storage_groups.description: (STORAGEGROUP) Per-storage-group tape parameters for Object or Object Backup storage groups defined in ISMF. Each entry overrides or supplements the global SETOAM settings for the named group.

name.description: (STORAGEGROUP) Name of the Object or Object Backup storage group previously defined using ISMF. Maximum 8 characters.

tape_unit_name.description: (TAPEUNITNAME) Required MVS esoteric or generic unit name OAM uses to allocate scratch tape for this storage group. Saved in the TAPEVOL table and used for subsequent read and write allocations.

sg_max_tape_retrieve_tasks.description: (SGMAXTAPERETRIEVETASKS) Maximum concurrent OAM tasks reading from tape for this storage group. Cannot exceed the global max_tape_retrieve_tasks value. Range: 1-100. Default: 1.

sg_max_tape_store_tasks.description: (SGMAXTAPESTORETASKS) Maximum concurrent OAM tasks writing to tape for this storage group. Cannot exceed the global max_tape_store_tasks value. Range: 1-100.

sg_max_recycle_tasks.description: (SGMAXRECYCLETASKS) Maximum concurrent MOVEVOL RECYCLE tasks for this storage group. Cannot exceed the global max_recycle_tasks value. A value of 0 disables RECYCLE for this group. Range: 0-15. Default: 1.

tape_drive_startup.description: (TAPEDRIVESTARTUP) Threshold in megabytes of pending write data per active drive at which OAM starts an additional tape drive for this storage group. Additional drives are bounded by sg_max_tape_store_tasks. Range: 1-9999. Default: 9999.

optical_reinit_mode.description: (OPTICALREINITMODE) Reinitialization mode for rewritable optical cartridges. GROUP (default) keeps cartridges in their original storage group. OAMSCRATCH returns them to the *SCRTCH* scratch group for reassignment to any storage group.

auto_backup_all.description: (ABALL) Specifies the backup copy (BACKUP1, BACKUP2, or INACTIVE) to use when a primary object is unavailable for any reason. INACTIVE disables automatic access to backup for all reasons. Overridden by individual AB* keywords. Changes require F OAM,START,AB or F OAM,STOP,AB commands.

multi_sys_enable.description: (MULTISYSENABLE) Specifies whether Object and Object Backup storage groups enabled to more than one system are permitted in a non-OAMplex environment. YES allows it; NO (default) rejects such groups. Global specification only; cannot be updated dynamically.

db2_reconnect_wait_time.description: (DB2RECONNECTWAITTIME) Seconds OAM waits between automatic reconnect attempts to a Db2 subsystem that started in maintenance mode. Use F OAM,DB2CONN to force an immediate reconnect. Range: 10-300. Default: 300.

optical_dispatcher_delay.description: (OPTICALDISPATCHERDELAY) Seconds the OAM optical dispatcher delays processing a new request after completing a read, to allow another request for the same mounted cartridge to arrive and reduce unnecessary cartridge flipping. Range: 1-60.

mount_wait_time.description: (MOUNTWAITTIME) Time in minutes OAM waits for an optical volume to be mounted on an operator-accessible drive before issuing message CBR4426D. Range: 1-9999. Default: 5.

unload_drives.description: (UNLOADDRIVES) Number of optical drives to empty (unloading cartridges if necessary) when the unload_timer interval is reached. Range: 1-6.

unload_timer.description: (UNLOADTIMER) Period of optical drive inactivity in seconds before the drives specified by unload_drives are unloaded. Range: 1-9999.

backup_delete.description: (BACKUPDELETE) When ON, OSMC deletes existing backup copies that exceed the number required by the object's current management class. Default: OFF. Global specification only; cannot be updated dynamically.

first_backup_group.description: (FIRSTBACKUPGROUP) Default Object Backup storage group where OSMC stores the first backup copy of objects whose storage group does not specify a per-group FIRSTBACKUPGROUP, when the management class requires a backup copy.

second_backup_group.description: (SECONDBACKUPGROUP) Default Object Backup storage group where OSMC stores the second backup copy of objects whose storage group does not specify a per-group SECONDBACKUPGROUP, when the management class requires more than one backup copy.

max_recall_tasks.description: (MAXRECALLTASKS) Maximum number of concurrent RECALL tasks (both implicit OSMC recalls and explicit OSREQ RETRIEVE recalls). A value of 0 disables all recall operations. Range: 0-255. Default: 0.

clear_old_loc.description: (CLEAROLDLOC) Controls whether OSMC clears original volume location (volser/sector or block ID) from the object directory when objects are transitioned from optical or tape to Db2 or file system. OPT: clear optical; TAPE: clear tape; BOTH: clear both; NONE (default): retain all.

cycle_window.description: (CYCLEWINDOW) OSMC storage management cycle start window mode for automatically started cycles. STRTONLY (default): use the defined start time as a start-only window; processing runs to completion. STRTSTOP: use start and end times as hard boundaries; processing stops at the end time.

max_osmc_fail.description: (MAXOSMCFAIL) Maximum number of the same type of OSMC processing errors allowed before OSMC terminates. Range: 0-255. Default: 3.

recall_all.description: (RECALLALL) Days a recalled object remains on disk before OSMC returns it to its original storage tier (optical, tape, or cloud). A value of 0 means the current day only. Applies to implicit recalls. Range: 0-255. Default: 0.

recall_cloud.description: (RECALLCLOUD) Days a recalled cloud object remains on disk before OSMC returns it to cloud. A value of 0 means the current day only. Applies to implicit recalls. Range: 0-255. Default: 0.

recall_disk_sublevel.description: (RECALLDISKSUBLEVEL) Disk sublevel where recalled optical or tape objects are placed. 1: Db2 object storage tables (default); 2: file system sublevel. Applies to both explicit and implicit recalls.

recall_off.description: (RECALLOFF) Disables recall for a specific storage group regardless of the RECALL parameter on OSREQ RETRIEVE. ON: disables both explicit and implicit recalls; OFF (default): recalls enabled. Storage group level only.

recall_none.description: (RECALLNONE) When true, objects on optical, tape, or cloud are not recalled to disk when retrieved. Applies to implicit recalls only.

recall_optical.description: (RECALLOPTICAL) Days a recalled optical object remains on disk before OSMC returns it to optical. A value of 0 means the current day only. Applies to implicit recalls. Classic OAM configuration only. Range: 0-255. Default: 0.

recall_tape.description: (RECALLTAPE) Days a recalled tape object remains on disk before OSMC returns it to tape. A value of 0 means the current day only. Applies to implicit recalls. Range: 0-255. Default: 0.

entry_ignore_msg_type.description: (ENTRYIGNOREMSGTYPE) Controls how volume entry ignore messages are displayed during cartridge entry processing. DETAIL (default) shows one message per volume. SUMMARY batches up to 48 volumes per message. SUPPRESS shows a single status line for all ignored volumes.

entry_ignore_msg_dest.description: (ENTRYIGNOREMSGDEST) Destination for volume entry ignore messages during cartridge entry processing. ALL (default) sends to both console and system log. SYSLOG sends to system log only.

entry_success_msg_dest.description: (ENTRYSUCCESSMSGDEST) Destination for successful volume entry messages (CBR3610I) during cartridge entry processing. ALL (default) sends to both console and system log. SYSLOG sends to system log only.

oam_group_name.description: (OAMGROUPNAME) XCF group name that all OAM instances in this OAMplex join. 1-8 characters; valid characters are A-Z, 0-9, $, #, @. Required when OAMMEMBERNAME is specified.

oam_member_name.description: (OAMMEMBERNAME) XCF member name identifying this OAM instance within the OAMplex group. 1-16 characters; valid characters are A-Z, 0-9, $, #, @. Required when OAMGROUPNAME is specified.

xcf_timeout.description: (XCFTIMEOUT) Customizes XCF transaction timeout values for this OAM instance in an OAMplex. Each sub-value specifies the seconds to wait for a shipped transaction to complete before OAM fails the request. A value of 0 means wait indefinitely (default).

connect.description: (CONNECT) Seconds to wait for an XCF connect operation to complete.

quiesce.description: (QUIESCE) Seconds to wait for an XCF quiesce operation to complete.

xcf_opt_read_auto.description: (XCFOPTREADA) Seconds to wait for a shipped optical read request targeting an automated (real) optical library to complete.

xcf_opt_read_manual.description: (XCFOPTREADM) Seconds to wait for a shipped optical read request targeting a shelf-resident (manual) volume to complete.

xcf_opt_write_auto.description: (XCFOPTWRITEA) Seconds to wait for a shipped optical write request targeting a storage group with automated (real) optical libraries to complete.

xcf_opt_write_manual.description: (XCFOPTWRITEM) Seconds to wait for a shipped optical write request targeting a storage group with pseudo (manual) libraries to complete.

xcf_tape_read_auto.description: (XCFTAPEREADA) Seconds to wait for a shipped tape read request targeting an automated tape library dataserver (ATLDS) to complete.

xcf_tape_read_manual.description: (XCFTAPEREADM) Seconds to wait for a shipped tape read request targeting a manual tape library (MTL) to complete.

optical_configuration.description: (SETOPT) statements configuring optical library and general OAM operational options.

osmc_configuration.description: (SETOSMC) statements configuring OAM Storage Management Component (OSMC) behaviour, including recall, backup, and cycle settings.

tape_library_configuration.description: (SETTLIB) statements configuring tape library (TLIB) messaging behaviour during cartridge entry processing.
