https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.title: IGGCATxx Configuration Schema
https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.description: Schema for IGGCATxx (DFSMS Catalog Configuration) parmlib member with 29 properties. Controls DFSMS catalog system behavior including resource monitoring, GDG settings, task limits, and catalog operations. https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=sys1parmlib-iggcatxx-dfsms-catalog-configuration

allocation_lock_contention_configuration.description: (ALLOCLCK) Independent PARMLIB statement for allocation lock resource monitoring configuration. Specifies wait time and action when resource contention is detected.

wait_minutes.description: Wait time in minutes before action is taken. 0=inactive, 1-4 reset to 5, >9999 reset to 9999

action.description: Action to take when wait time expires

system_catalog_contention_configuration.description: (SYSIGGV2) Independent PARMLIB statement for SYSIGGV2 resource monitoring configuration. Specifies wait time and action when resource contention is detected.

wait_minutes.description: Wait time in minutes before action is taken. 0=inactive, 1-4 reset to 5, >9999 reset to 9999

action.description: Action to take when wait time expires

sysztiot_contention_configuration.description: (SYSZTIOT) Independent PARMLIB statement for SYSZTIOT resource monitoring configuration. Specifies wait time and action when resource contention is detected.

wait_minutes.description: Wait time in minutes before action is taken. 0=inactive, 1-4 reset to 5, >9999 reset to 9999

action.description: Action to take when wait time expires

syszvvds_contention_configuration.description: (SYSZVVDS) Independent PARMLIB statement for SYSZVVDS resource monitoring configuration. Specifies wait time and action when resource contention is detected.

wait_minutes.description: Wait time in minutes before action is taken. 0=inactive, 1-4 reset to 5, >9999 reset to 9999

action.description: Action to take when wait time expires

alias_search_level.description: (ALIASLEVEL) Multi-level alias (MLA) search level. Specifies how many levels to search when resolving catalog aliases.

enable_autoadd.description: (AUTOADD) Enable or disable the autoadd function for automatic catalog entry creation. True enables autoadd, false disables it.

maximum_concurrent_catalogs.description: (CATMAX) Maximum number of catalogs that can be open concurrently. Recommended not to exceed TIOT limits (1635 for 32K TIOT, 3273 for 64K TIOT).

issue_delete_force_warning.description: (DELFORCEWNG) Issue warning messages IDC1997I and IDC1998I when delete force operations occur. True issues warnings, false suppresses them.

issue_delete_recovery_warning.description: (DELRECOVWNG) Issue message IDC1999I when delete recovery operations occur. True issues message, false suppresses it.

enable_dataset_name_checking.description: (DSNCHECK) Enable syntax checking on catalog dataset names. True enables checking, false disables it.

enable_dynamic_dumps.description: (DUMP) Enable or disable dynamic dump availability for catalog operations. True enables dumps, false disables them.

conditional_dumps.description: (DUMPON) Conditional dump specifications based on return codes, reason codes, and module names. Multiple specifications can be defined.

return_code.description: Return code that triggers the dump

reason_code.description: Reason code that triggers the dump

module_name.description: Catalog module name where the condition occurs

occurrence_count.description: Number of occurrences before dump is taken

enable_extended_alias.description: (EXTENDEDALIAS) Enable extension records for user catalog aliases. True enables extension records, false disables them.

enable_gdg_extended.description: (GDGEXTENDED) Enable GDG extended support for generation data groups. Requires z/OS V2R2 or higher on all shared systems. True enables extended support, false disables it.

enable_gdg_fifo.description: (GDGFIFOENABLE) Enable FIFO (First In First Out) allocation order for GDGs. True enables FIFO, false uses LIFO (Last In First Out) default.

gdg_limit_maximum.description: (GDGLIMITMAX) Maximum LIMIT value for DEFINE GDG commands. 0 means no maximum. Classic GDGs limited to 255; values >255 only apply to extended GDGs.

gdg_default_purge.description: (GDGPURGE) Default PURGE setting for DEFINE GDG commands. True sets PURGE as default, false sets NOPURGE as default.

gdg_default_scratch.description: (GDGSCRATCH) Default SCRATCH setting for DEFINE GDG commands. True sets SCRATCH as default, false sets NOSCRATCH as default.

extent_notification_threshold.description: (NOTIFYEXTENT) Threshold percentage for extent usage notification. When catalog extent usage reaches this percentage, notification message is issued. 0 suppresses monitoring (but IEC361I still issued at 90%).

enable_smf_16byte_timestamp.description: (SMF16BYTETIMESTAMP) Append 16-byte timestamp to SMF record types 61, 65, and 66. True appends timestamp, false does not.

enable_symrec_creation.description: (SYMREC) Enable SYMREC record creation for catalog operations. True enables creation, false disables it.

enable_sys_percent_conversion.description: (SYS%) Enable conversion of SYS% to SYS1% in dataset names. True enables conversion, false disables it.

tape_volume_catalog_hlq.description: (TAPEHLQ) High-level qualifier for tape volume catalog entries. Valid characters: A-Z, 0-9, @, #, $

task_maximum.description: (TASKMAX) Upper limit for user service tasks. Cannot exceed 90% of task_table_size. Cannot be lower than task_minimum. If specified with task_table_size, task_table_size must be specified first in the parmlib member.

task_minimum.description: (TASKMIN) Lower limit for catalog service tasks. Must not exceed task_maximum.

task_table_size.description: (TASKTABLESIZE) Maximum possible concurrent tasks. IPL only parameter (ignored on CAS restart). If specified with task_maximum, must be specified first in the parmlib member.

issue_update_failure_message.description: (UPDTFAIL) Issue message IEC390I when VSAM update terminates abnormally. True issues message, false suppresses it.

vvds_space_allocation.description: (VVDSSPACE) VVDS (VSAM Volume Data Set) space allocation in tracks. Specifies primary and secondary allocation amounts.

secondary_tracks.description: Secondary allocation in tracks. Zero with valid primary defaults to 10 on IPL.

enable_enhanced_vvr_checking.description: (VVRCHECK) Enable enhanced VVR (VSAM Volume Record) checking on VVDS I/O operations. True enables checking, false disables it.

https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.title: EDGDEFxx DFSMSrmm Default Definitions Schema
https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.description: Schema for EDGDEFxx parmlib member - DFSMSrmm default attributes for volumes and Volume Retention Specifications (VRS). https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=guide-using-parmlib-member-edgdefxx

defaults_table.description: (DEFAULT) Array of defaults table entries. Each entry defines selection criteria and retention attributes applied when a matching data set is written to tape. Multiple DEFAULT entries may be defined. https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=edgdefxx-defining-defaults-table-entries-default

dataset_name_filter.description: (DSNAME) Data set name mask for selection. Supports wildcard characters * and %. Default is ** (all data sets). Can be abbreviated as DSN.

job_name_filter.description: (JOBNAME) Job name mask for selection (1-8 characters). Supports wildcard characters * and %. Can be abbreviated as JOB.

program_name_filter.description: (PGMNAME) Program name mask for selection (1-8 characters). Supports wildcard characters * and %.

retention_method.description: (RETENTIONMETHOD) Specifies the retention method for the tape volume set. EXPDT bases retention on expiration date; VRSEL uses vital record specifications. Can be abbreviated as RM.

retention_period.description: (RETPD) Number of days to retain the data set (0-93000), or PERM/PERMANENT for permanent retention. Optionally append ,OVERRIDE to override JCL values.

retain_by.description: (RETAINBY) Specifies how DFSMSrmm retains a volume or multivolume set. Only applies to EXPDT retention method.

vrs_value.description: (VRSVALUE) VRS management value to associate with the data set (1-8 characters). Can be abbreviated as VRSVAL or MANAGEMENTVALUE.

vrsel_exclude.description: (VRSELEXCLUDE) Whether to exclude the data set from VRSEL processing. Can be abbreviated as VX.

while_catalog.description: (WHILECATALOG) Retains data sets based on catalog status. OFF ignores catalog; ON retains while cataloged; UNTILEXPIRED retains until uncataloged then applies CATLGDAYS; ONLY retains solely based on catalog. Can be abbreviated as WC or WHILECAT.

key_date.description: (KEYDATE) Matches data sets by the EXPDT value in JCL. Format yyddd where yy=00-99, ddd=000-366. Use * to match any KEYDATE.

no_key_date.description: (NOKEYDATE) Selects data sets that do not have a KEYDATE specified in JCL or have no matching KEYDATE in the defaults table. Mutually exclusive with KEYDATE and NODATE.

no_date.description: (NODATE) Selects data sets that have no KEYDATE (EXPDT) or retention period specified in JCL. Mutually exclusive with KEYDATE and NOKEYDATE.

last_reference_days.description: (LASTREF) Number of days (0-93000) that the data set will be retained after last reference. Only applies to EXPDT retention method.

edm.description: (EDM) Marks the volume as EDM (External Data Manager) managed, preventing expiration by DFSMSrmm. Mutually exclusive with NOEDM.

no_edm.description: (NOEDM) Specifies that the volume is not to be marked as EDM managed, overriding automatic EDM marking. Mutually exclusive with EDM.

pool.description: (POOL) Selects the scratch pool prefix for write requests in MTL or stand-alone tape drives. Not compatible with KEYDATE, NOKEYDATE, or PGMNAME.

continue_search.description: (CONTINUE) When specified, if this entry matches DFSMSrmm continues searching for additional matching entries, accumulating settings. The last matching value for each parameter wins.

https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.title: DFSMShsm ARCCMDxx ADDVOL Command
https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.description:
(ADDVOL) Adds new non-SMS-managed volumes to the list of volumes that DFSMShsm manages or owns and defines the attributes of those volumes. 
 'backup', 'dump', 'migration', 'primary' are required but exclusive keys that are to specify the type of volume. 
 'volser' and 'unit_type' are also required keys. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=reference-addvol-command-adding-changing-dfsmshsm-volumes

volser.description:
(volser) Specifying the volume to be added or changed. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-volser-specifying-volume-be-added-changed

backup.description:
(BACKUP) Identify a volume to be used as a backup volume. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-backup-dump-migration-primary-identifying-type-volume 
 It can be set as either boolean or object type. 
 - For boolean type, only 'true' value is allowed, and 'BACKUP' keyword without any options, i.e. no DAILY or SPILL, will be generated in the parmlib. DFSMShsm determines which type of backup volume it needs when it selects a backup volume.  
 - For object type, the properties below apply to the 'backup' key to specify the use of the backup volume, including: 
    'backup_volume_type',  'day_in_backup_cycle' 
 - 'threshold' key is an option to the 'BACKUP' keyword but is set at the same level as the 'backup' key. If it is not specified, the default value is 90.

backup_volume_type.description:
- IF (DAILY) is specified, the key 'day_in_backup_cycle' can be used to specify the day in the backup cycle that you want this backup volume assigned to (DAILY(day)). 
   - If you do not specify a day with the DAILY parameter and DFSMShsm needs another daily backup volume, DFSMShsm assigns the volume to a day in the backup cycle. 
   - If (SPILL) is specified that the volume receives valid backup versions from DASD daily backup volumes. 
   - A tape SPILL backup volume can also receive all valid backup versions of data sets from a recycled tape backup volume. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-daily-spill-identifying-type-backup-volume

day_in_backup_cycle.description: (DAILY(day)) The day in the backup cycle that you want this backup volume assigned to.

dump.description:
(DUMP) Identify a volume to be used as the output of a full-volume dump. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-backup-dump-migration-primary-identifying-type-volume 
 It can be set as either boolean or object type. 
 - For boolean type, only 'true' value is allowed, and 'DUMP' keyword without any options, i.e. no dump class, will be generated in the parmlib. This dump volume can then be used by any dump class. 
 - For object type, the dumplass option that applies to DUMP can be set as a property of the 'dump' key, i.e. 
    'dump_class' 
 - 'tape_density' key is an option to the 'DUMP' keyword but is set at the same level as the 'dump' key. If it is not specified, the default is the highest density the device can support.

dump_class.description:
(DUMPCLASS(class)) Restricting the specified volume to use a specific dump class. 
 If dump_class is not specified, the dump volume can be used by any dump class. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opac-dumpclass-restricting-specified-volume-use-specific-dump-class

migration.description:
(MIGRATION) Identify a volume to be used as a migration volume. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-backup-dump-migration-primary-identifying-type-volume 
 It can be set as either boolean or object type. 
 - For boolean type, only 'true' value is allowed, and 'MIGRATION' keyword without any options will be generated in the parmlib. The default specifications of this migration volume are: 
    (1) not eligible for a full-volume automatic dump 
    (2) is MIGRATIONLEVEL1 volume 
    (3) no OVERFLOW 
    (4) no small data set packing  
 - For object type, the options that apply to MIGRATION can be set as properties of the 'migration' key, including: 
    'automatic_dump',  'migration_output_selection',  'migration_level',  'ml1_volume_overflow',  'small_dataset_packing' 
 - 'threshold' key is an option to the 'MIGRATION' keyword but is set at the same level as the 'migration' key. If it is not specified, the default value is 100.

automatic_dump.description:
Two optional values for this key. 
   - Array of dump class names, (AUTODUMP(class,)) specifies that the volume is eligible for a full-volume automatic dump and selects the dump classes that contain the dump copies. 
   - Boolean value, 'false', (NOAUTODUMP), specifies that the volume is NOT eligible for a full-volume automatic dump. 'true' value is not allowed because AUTODUMP needs specifying dump class name. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opac-autodump-noautodump-specifying-whether-volume-is-eligible-automatic-dumping-tape-cloud

migration_output_selection.description:
This option only applies to DASD volumes. 
   - If true, (NODRAIN) specifies that a ML1 volume can be selected for migration output or a ML2 volume can be associated with a keyrange. 
   - If false, (DRAIN) specifies that the DASD volume is to be empited and cannot be seleted as migration output. 
   - 'true' (NODRAIN) is the default. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opac-drain-nodrain-specifying-whether-volume-should-be-selected-migration-output

migration_level.description:
(MIGRATIONLEVEL1 | MIGRATIONLEVEL2) Specifying the migration level. ML1 is the default. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-migrationlevel1-migrationlevel2-specifying-migration-level

ml1_volume_overflow.description:
- If false, (NOOVERFLOW) specifies that the volume is considered with other level 1 volumes for migration data and backup versions of any size. 
   - If true, (OVERFLOW) specifies that the volume is considered if either of the following are true: 
     (1) The data you are migrating or backing up is larger than a given size, as specified on the SETSYS L1OVERFLOW(DATASETSIZE(dssize)) command. 
     (2) DFSMShsm cannot allocate enough space on a NOOVERFLOW volume.specifying the usage of a level 1 volume for data set migration and backup versions. 
   - 'false' (NOOVERFLOW) is the default. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opac-overflow-nooverflow-specifying-usage-level-1-volume-data-set-migration-backup-versions

small_dataset_packing.description:
- If true, (SMALLDATASETPACKING) specifies that small data set packing can be done on the migration level 1 volume. 
   - If false, (NOSMALLDATASETPACKING) specifies that small data set packing cannot be done on the migration level 1 volume. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opac-smalldatasetpacking-nosmalldatasetpacking-specifying-small-data-set-packing-level-1-volume

primary.description:
(PRIMARY) Identify a volume to be used as a primary volume, must be DASD. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-backup-dump-migration-primary-identifying-type-volume 
 It can be set as either boolean or object type. 
 - For boolean type, only 'true' value is allowed, and 'PRIMARY' keyword without any options will be generated in the parmlib. The default specifications of this primary volume are: 
    (1) no automatic backup 
    (2) not eligible for a full-volume automatic dump 
    (3) eligible for automatic migration 
    (4) eligible for automatic recall 
    (5) is migrated according to the number of days they have been inactive 
 - For object type, the options that apply to PRIMARY can be set as properties of the 'primary' key, including: 
    'automatic_backup',  'automatic_recall',  'automatic_migration',  'automatic_dump',  'backup_versions_reside',  'space_management_type' 
 - 'track_managed_threshold' key and 'threshold' key with both high and low values are opitons to the 'PRIMARY' keyword but are set at the same level as the 'primary' key. If those keys are not specified, the default high value 100 and the default low value is 0.

automatic_backup.description:
- If true, (AUTOBACKUP) specifies the primary volume is eligible for automatic backup. 
   - If false, (NOAUTOBACKUP) specifies the primary volume is NOT eligible for automatic backup. 
   - 'false', (NOAUTOBACKUP) is the default. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opac-autobackup-noautobackup-specifying-whether-primary-volume-is-eligible-automatic-backup

automatic_recall.description:
- If true, (AUTORECALL) specifies the primary volume is eligible for automatic recall. 
   - If false, (NOAUTORECALL) specifies the primary volume is NOT eligible for automatic recall. 
   - 'true', (AUTORECALL) is the default. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opac-autorecall-noautorecall-specifying-whether-primary-volume-is-eligible-automatic-recall

automatic_migration.description:
- If true, (AUTOMIGRATION) specifying the primary volume is eligible for automatic migration. 
   - If false, (NOAUTOMIGRATION) Specifying the primary volume is NOT eligible for automatic migration. 
   - 'true', (AUTOMIGRATION) is the default. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opac-automigration-noautomigration-specifying-whether-primary-volume-is-eligible-automatic-volume-space-management

automatic_dump.description:
Two optional values for this key. 
   - Array of dump classes names, (AUTODUMP(class,)) specifies that the volume is eligible for a full-volume automatic dump and selects the dump classes that contain the dump copies. 
   - Boolean value, 'false', (NOAUTODUMP), specifies that the volume is NOT eligible for a full-volume automatic dump. 'true' value is not allowed because AUTODUMP needs specifying dump class name. 
 if 'automatic_dump' key is not specified, (NOAUTODUMP) is the default. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opac-autodump-noautodump-specifying-whether-volume-is-eligible-automatic-dumping-tape-cloud

backup_versions_reside.description:
(BACKUPDEVICECATEGORY) Specifying where backup versions reside on, 
   - 'TAPE': tape backup volume. 
   - 'DASD': DASD daily backup volume. 
   - 'NONE': DFSMShsm selects the first available. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-backupdevicecategory-specifying-where-backup-versions-reside

space_management_type.description:
Specifying the type of space management on a primary volume. 
  'MIGRATE' is the default that specifies that the data sets that reside on a primary volume are migrated according to the number of days they have been inactive. 
  Or Specifies optional keys: 
   - migrate_inactive_days:, 
   - delete_by_age:, 
   - delete_if_backedup: 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opac-deletebyage-deleteifbackedup-migrate-specifying-type-space-management-primary-volume

migrate_inactive_days.description:
(MIGRATE(days)) Specifies the data sets on a primary volume are migrated if they have been inactive for a specified number of days. 
 If Zero specified, the number of days the data set can remain inactive before it is allowed to migrate is the value specified with the DAYS parameter of the SETSYS command.

delete_by_age.description: (DELETEBYAGE(days) Specifies that cataloged and uncataloged data sets that reside on a primary volume are scratched if they have been inactive for a specified number of days and the current expiration date has been reached.

delete_if_backedup.description: (DELETEIFBACKEDUP(days) Specifies that the data sets on a primary volume can be scratched if they have been inactive for a specified number of days and if the data sets on the primary volume have current backup versions.

tape_density.description:
(DENSITY()) Specifying the tape density. 
   - Only valid for DUMP volumes. 
   - 2: a tape density of 32 bytes per millimeter. 
   - 3: a tape density of 63 bytes per millimeter. 
   - 4: a tape density of 246 bytes per millimeter. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-density-specifying-tape-density

track_managed_threshold.description:
(TRACKMANAGEDTHRESHOLD(high low)) High and low threshold for the track-managed space of a non-SMS level 0 extended address volume (EAV). 
   - Two keys are required, 'high' and 'low'. 
   - Only valid for primary volumes. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opac-trackmanagedthreshold-specifying-high-low-threshold-track-managed-space-non-sms-level-0-extended-address-volume

high.description: (high) The high threshold percentage of the track-managed space on a EAV being occupied

low.description: (low) The low threshold percentage of the track-managed space on a EAV being occupied

threshold_primary.description:
(THRESHOLD(thresh1 thresh2)) The percentage limit of occupied space you want on a volume. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-threshold-specifying-thresholds-occupancy

high.description: (thresh1) The high threshold percentage of occupied space on a primary volume

low.description: (thresh2) The low threshold percentage of space remain occupied on a primary volume after interval migration or volume migraion

threshold_backup_migration.description:
(THRESHOLD(thresh1)) The high threshold percentage of occupied space on a volume. 
   - For DASD backup volume, if 'threshold' key is not specified, the default value is 90. 
   - For ML1 volume, if 'threshold' key is not specified, the default value is 100. 
   - This key is invalid for dump volumes. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-threshold-specifying-thresholds-occupancy

https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.title: DFSMShsm DEFINE Command
https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.description:
DFSMShsm DEFINE Command - Used to define control structures for use by DFSMShsm. See
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=dsar-define-command-defining-control-structures-use-by-dfsmshsm

migration_level_2.description:
(MIGRATIONLEVEL2 | MIGRATIONLEVEL2(...)) Specifying the division of key ranges for DASD migration level 2 volumes. When you specify MIGRATIONLEVEL2, you can also specify KEYS to indicate how data sets are assigned to the available DASD migration level 2 volumes. 
 Use the boolean value "true" to specify the default behavior (MIGRATIONLEVEL2 keyword only). When set to true, DFSMShsm assumes that you are defining one key range for all possible keys. 
 If object MIGRATIONLEVEL2(...), use the available properties to fine tune the key ranges and volumes, See
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opdc-migrationlevel2-specifying-dasd-level-2-volumes-their-associated-key-range-structure

keys.description:
(KEYS(key ...)) Specifies an ascending alphanumeric sequence of lower key-range boundaries, where the set of initial characters of the data set name is compared against the key. Any data set having the set of initial characters within the specified alphanumeric range migrates to the volume associated with that range. You specify only the lower boundary of the key range for a volume. The maximum number of key ranges you can define is 61. For key ..., substitute one or more strings of 1 to 8 characters, starting with an alphabetic or $, #, or @. The remaining characters can be alphanumeric and $, #, or @. See
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opdc-migrationlevel2-specifying-dasd-level-2-volumes-their-associated-key-range-structure

volumes.description:
(VOLUMES(volser ...)) Specifying a list of DASD migration level 2 volumes, assigned to the specified key ranges. See
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opdc-migrationlevel2-specifying-dasd-level-2-volumes-their-associated-key-range-structure

https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.title: VATLSTxx Configuration Schema
https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.description: Schema for VATLSTxx (Volume Attribute List) parmlib member. Defines mount and use attributes for DASD volumes using column-dependent format. Documentation: https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=sys1parmlib-vatlstxx-volume-attribute-list

vatdef.description: Optional configuration statement that sets default use attributes and comment processing rules. Must be first non-comment line if present. Free-format (not column-dependent).

ipluse.description: (IPLUSE) Default use attribute for permanently resident volumes brought online during IPL when no VATLST entry exists or use attribute is incorrect.

sysuse.description: (SYSUSE) Default use attribute for volumes varied online after IPL with no VATLST entry.

volume_entries.description: Array of DASD volume attribute definitions. Each entry defines mount and use attributes for specific or generic volumes using column-dependent format. Generic patterns support wildcards: * (any characters from position to end) and % (single character at position).

volume_serial.description: (Columns 1-6) Volume serial number. Required field. 1-6 alphanumeric characters, left-aligned, padded with blanks at right. Supports generic patterns using wildcards: * (matches any character(s) from position to end) and % (matches single character at position). Examples: TSO* matches TSO01, TSO123; P%%5 matches P125. If multiple generic patterns match, last entry wins.

specific_identifier.description: (Column 7) Specific volume identifier flag. Optional field. Use 'S' to indicate specific volume serial (not generic) even if contains * or %. Use comma for normal processing. Only code 'S' when volser contains wildcards but should be treated as specific volume. Error message IEA855I issued if 'S' coded for volser without wildcards.

mount_attribute.description: (Column 8) Mount attribute determines conditions under which volume can be demounted. Optional field. 0 = Normal (volume can be demounted). 1 = Permanently resident or reserved (volume cannot be demounted). Volumes with 1 are selected first during allocation, minimizing serialization and processing time. Any character other than 1 results in default (0).

use_attribute.description: (Column 10) Use attribute controls type of requests for which volume can be allocated. Optional field. 0 = STORAGE (for system data sets). 1 = PUBLIC (for general use). 2 = PRIVATE (for specific applications). Default is 1 (PUBLIC) unless VATDEF specifies different default via IPLUSE (for IPL volumes) or SYSUSE (for post-IPL volumes). Any character other than 0, 1, or 2 results in default.

device_type.description: (Columns 12-19) Device type specification. Required field. Up to 8 characters, left-aligned, padded with blanks at right. First character must start at column 12. Valid values are supported device types defined through HCD (e.g., 3330, 3350, 3380, 3390). Use * in column 12 for generic device type (applies same attributes regardless of device type). Indicates basic device, not special features like track overflow.

mount_message_suppression.description: (Column 21) Mount message suppression flag. Optional field. Blank = Issue mount messages if volume not mounted (default). N = Suppress mount messages. Any other character = Issue mount messages. Ignored for volumes defined with generic VATLST entries.

https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.title: DFSMShsm ARCCMDxx SETSYS commands for logging and diagnostics functions
https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.description:
(SETSYS LOGGING/DIAGNOSTICS) Parameters controlling logging and diagnostics functions. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-actlogmsglvl-specifying-message-level-recording-data-sets

activity_log_message_level.description:
(ACTLOGMSGLVL) Specifying the message log level for the activity log required for recording data sets processed by volume and level functions. This parameter determines which ARC0734I data set movement messages will be written to the activity log. Only the issuance of the ARC0734I message is affected. 
 If FULL, Messages are generated and logged for all activities. 
 If EXCEPTIONONLY, Messages are generated and logged for activities with a nonzero return code. 
 If REDUCED, The original space management message or backup message is generated, but messages for subsequent movement and cleanup are suppressed. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-actlogmsglvl-specifying-message-level-recording-data-sets

activity_log_type.description:
(ACTLOGTYPE) Specifying the activity log output data set type. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-actlogtype-specifying-type-output-data-set-receive-messages

spool_dasd.description:
(ACTLOGTYPE(SYSOUT|DASD)) If SYSOUT, Messages are written out to a spool data set. Optionally you can provide class. SYSOUT is the initial default setting. If class is not specified, the default will be the SETSYS ACTLOGTYPE SYSOUT class. 
 If DASD, DFSMShsm dynamically allocates DASD data sets with a unit name of SYSALLDA and a size of 20 tracks for primary allocation and 50 tracks for secondary allocation. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-abarsactlogtype-specifying-abars-activity-log-output-data-set-type

sysout_class.description:
(CLASS) An alphanumeric character for the class DFSMShsm is to use for output. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-actlogtype-specifying-type-output-data-set-receive-messages

debug.description:
(DEBUG|NODEBUG) are mutually exlusive, parameters pecifying whether DFSMShsm is to operate in debug mode. 
 DEBUG specifies that DFSMShsm operate in debug mode to monitor effects without moving or deleting data. 
 NODEBUG specifies normal operation, not to operate in debug mode. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-debug-nodebug-specifying-debug-mode

emergency.description:
(EMERGENCY|NOEMERGENCY) are mutually exlusive, parameters specifying whether emergency mode is in effect. 
 EMERGENCY mode stops all DFSMShsm automatic and command data set processing in both SMS and non-SMS environments and in both primary and secondary address spaces, including functions like aggregate backup, aggregate recovery, audit, migration, backup, recall, recovery and recycle. 
 NOEMERGENCY specifies that emergency mode is not in effect. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-emergency-noemergency-specifying-no-data-set-movement

pda.description:
(PDA(NONE|ON|OFF)) Specifies whether the problem determination aid (PDA) is enabled. The PDA facility gathers diagnostic information and records the information in a storage buffer and in DASD data sets. 
 If None, the PDA facility does not start at DFSMShsm startup. No space for the storage buffer is requested, and the trace output data sets are not opened. 
 If ON, Storage is requested for the trace buffer and the trace output data sets open. If the trace data sets are not allocated, the problem determination aid function continues to trace in internal storage. 
 If OFF, The trace facilities are suspended but the primary module is left active. The trace buffer storage area remains allocated and the output data sets remain open, but the bit to allow tracing is turned off. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-pda-specifying-whether-problem-determination-aid-is-initiated

smf.description:
Specifies whether DFSMShsm writes SMF record. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-smf-nosmf-specifying-whether-dfsmshsm-writes-smf-records

enabled.description: (SMF(smfid)|NOSMF), are mutually exclusive, specifying whether DFSMShsm writes SMF records that contain DFSMShsm statistics. When true, SMF records are enabled and smf_id must be specified. When false, renders NOSMF. https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-smf-nosmf-specifying-whether-dfsmshsm-writes-smf-records

smf_id.description:
(SMF(smfid)) Specifying that DFSMShsm write SMF records. For smfid, substitute a record identification. Use SMF user codes for the record identification in the range of 128 to 255. If you specify smfid, DFSMShsm writes records with SMF identifications of smfid and smfid+1. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-smf-nosmf-specifying-whether-dfsmshsm-writes-smf-records

system1_dump.description:
(SYS1DUMP|NOSYS1DUMP) are mutually exclusive, parameters specifying whether DFSMShsm dumps resulting from an abnormal end or error condition in primary or secondary address spaces be written in a system dump data set. 
 If true, SYS1DUMP is selected and specifies that DFSMShsm dumps be written in a system dump data set. 
 If false, NOSYS1DUMP is selected and specifies that when DFSMShsm abends, the dump produced is directed to the dump related DD statements specified in the DFSMShsm startup procedure. These DD statements are: SYSABEND, SYSUDUMP, and SYSMDUMP. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-sys1dump-nosys1dump-specifying-where-dfsmshsm-dumps-should-be-written

monitor.description:
(MONITOR) Specifies which informational messages DFSMShsm is to print at the system console, and the values DFSMShsm is to use for monitoring space in the journal and control data sets. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-monitor-specifying-which-informational-messages-print-system-console

backup_control_dataset.description:
(BACKUPCONTROLDATASET) Subparameter of the MONITOR parameter that specifies when DFSMShsm issues warning messages about the amount of space used in the BCDS. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-monitor-backupcontroldataset-monitoring-space-used-in-bcds#s4607

threshold.description:
(thresh) Substitute a decimal number from 0 to 100 that specifies a percentage value. When the occupied space in the BCDS exceeds this percentage value, DFSMShsm warns the system operator that the data set is getting full. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-monitor-backupcontroldataset-monitoring-space-used-in-bcds#s4607

journal.description:
(JOURNAL) Subparameter of the MONITOR parameter that specifies when DFSMShsm issues warning messages about the amount of space used in the journal data set. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-monitor-journal-monitoring-space-used-in-journal-data-set

threshold.description:
(thresh) Substitute a decimal number from 0 to 100 that specifies a percentage value. When the occupied space in the journal data set exceeds this percentage value, DFSMShsm warns the system operator that the data set is getting full. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-monitor-journal-monitoring-space-used-in-journal-data-set

migration_control_dataset.description:
(MIGRATIONCONTROLDATASET) Subparameter of the MONITOR parameter that specifies when DFSMShsm issues warning messages about the amount of space used in the MCDS. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-monitor-migrationcontroldataset-monitoring-space-used-in-mcds

threshold.description:
(thresh) Substitute a decimal number from 0 to 100 that specifies a percentage value. When the occupied space in the MCDS exceeds this percentage value, DFSMShsm warns the system operator that the data set is getting full. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-monitor-migrationcontroldataset-monitoring-space-used-in-mcds

offline_control_dataset.description:
(OFFLINECONTROLDATASET) Subparameter of the MONITOR parameter that specifies when DFSMShsm issues warning messages about the amount of space used in the OCDS. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-monitor-offlinecontroldataset-monitoring-space-used-in-ocds

threshold.description:
(thresh) Substitute a decimal number from 0 to 100 that specifies a percentage value. When the occupied space in the OCDS exceeds this percentage value, DFSMShsm warns the system operator that the data set is getting full. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-monitor-offlinecontroldataset-monitoring-space-used-in-ocds

space.descripion:
(SPACE|NOSPACE) SPACE and NOSPACE are mutually exclusive, parameters of the MONITOR parameter that specify whether to print volume space-use messages when DFSMShsm performs a space check for interval migration, on-demand migration, or primary space management. The three messages printed are: ARC0400I, ARC0401I, and ARC0402I. 
 If true, SPACE-Volume space-use messages are printed to the system console, the DFSMShsm log, and the appropriate activity log. 
 If false, NOSPACE-Volume space-use messages printed to the DFSMShsm log and the appropriate activity log only. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-monitor-space-nospace-printing-volume-space-use-messages

startup.descripion:
(STARTUP|NOSTARTUP) are mutually exclusive, subparameters of the MONITOR parameter that specify whether or not to print DFSMShsm startup informational messages at the system console. 
 If true, MONITOR(STARTUP) specifies that DFSMShsm startup informational messages print at the system console and in the DFSMShsm log. 
 If false, MONITOR(NOSTARTUP) specifies that DFSMShsm startup informational messages print only in the DFSMShsm log, with the exception of messages from the PATCH command, which is printed at the system console. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-monitor-startup-nostartup-printing-dfsmshsm-startup-informational-messages

volume.descripion:
(VOLUME|NOVOLUME) are mutually exclusive, subparameters of the MONITOR parameter that specify whether or not to print data set (ARC0734I) messages at the system console. 
 If true, MONITOR(VOLUME) specifies that messages print at the system console, DFSMShsm log, and appropriate activity log. DFSMShsm prints messages about data sets on volumes processed by space management, backup, and recovery. 
 If false, MONITOR(NOVOLUME) specifies that messages relating to the data sets on the volumes processed by space management, backup, and recovery print only in the DFSMShsm log and the appropriate activity log. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-monitor-volume-novolume-print-data-set-messages-during-volume-processing

sysout_hsm_output.description:
(SYSOUT)  parameter specifying the class, number of copies, and any special forms used to print output from DFSMShsm. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-sysout-directing-dfsmshsm-output

class.description:
(CLASS) class, substitute an alphanumeric character for the class that DFSMShsm uses when it prints output. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-sysout-directing-dfsmshsm-output

copies.description:
(COPIES) copies, substitute a decimal number from 1 to 99 for the number of copies to print of DFSMShsm output. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-sysout-directing-dfsmshsm-output

forms.description:
(FORMS) forms, substitute up to 4 alphanumeric characters for the special forms to use when printing DFSMShsm output. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-sysout-directing-dfsmshsm-output

https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.description: Data Management Definitions for z/OS V3R1

https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.title: DFSMShsm ARCCMDxx Set Migration Status (SETMIG) Command
https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.description:
The SETMIG command changes the space management status of a specific data set or group of data sets on level 0 volumes. It can also change the space management status of a specific primary volume. You use this command to temporarily change the type of space management for specific cases. 
 Reference: https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=dsar-setmig-command-changing-space-management-status-non-sms-managed-data-sets-volumes 
 Supported keywords: 
 set_migration_status 
 mvs_file_name 
 mvs_file_pattern 
 volume_serial_number 
 command_or_automatic_migration

mvs_file_name.description:
(DATASETNAME) Changes the space management status of a data set on a level 0 volume 
 Reference: https: //www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-datasetname-level-volume-changing-space-management-status

mvs_file_pattern.description:
(LEVEL) Changes the space management status of a group of data sets that have the same set of initial characters of the data set name. The data sets are on level 0 volumes. 
 Reference: https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-datasetname-level-volume-changing-space-management-status

volume_serial_number.description:
(VOLUME) Changes the space management status of the primary volume. 
 Reference: https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-datasetname-level-volume-changing-space-management-status

command_or_automatic_migration_dsn_vol.description:
(MIGRATION) The value true specifies that DFSMShsm will do space management automatically or by command for a data set. 
 (NOMIGRATION) The value false specifies that DFSMShsm will not do space management 
 Reference: https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-commandmigration-migration-nomigration-specifying-way-space-management-is-controlled

command_or_automatic_migration_level.description:
(MIGRATION) The value BOTH specifies that DFSMShsm will do space management automatically or by command for a data set. 
 (NOMIGRATION) The value NONE specifies that DFSMShsm will not do space management 
 (COMMANDMIGRATION) The value COMMAND specifies that DFSMShsm will do space management for a data set only by command. 
 Reference: https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-commandmigration-migration-nomigration-specifying-way-space-management-is-controlled

https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.title: DFSMShsm ARCCMDxx RELEASE Command
https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.description:
The RELEASE command releases for processing all or part of the DFSMShsm functions that have been held. You cannot release the processing of a subfunction while the processing of its main function is being held. For example, you cannot release the subfunction BACKUP(AUTO) if the main function BACKUP is held. When you release a main function, the held main function processing and its associated subfunctions processing are released. Commands that failed after you issued the HOLD command are not restarted.

If a journal becomes full, processing is held for all migration, backup, and dump functions. To resume journaling and other DFSMShsm functions, enter the BACKVOL CDS command to null the journal. If multiple systems share the journal, enter the BACKVOL CDS command on one of the systems, and then enter the RELEASE ALL command on all of the systems that share the journal.

If DFSMShsm functions are held because of a full journal, the RELEASE command will not appear to be effective until the control data sets are backed up. For more information, see Data recovery scenarios.

The RELEASE command allows migration target levels (ML1 or ML2 tape) that have become unavailable as targets because of some error condition to become available for retry. For more information, see Managing DFSMShsm media.

In addition, you can also decide to print the activity logs or you can enable the EDGTVEXT interface again after it was disabled because of an ABEND in DFSMSrmm. 


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=dsar-release-command-releasing-all-some-dfsmshsm-functions-processing

aggregate_backup.description:
(ABACKUP) is an optional parameter specifying that DFSMShsm release for processing any ABACKUP commands currently held in queues and allow new ABACKUP commands to be received.


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-abackup-releasing-aggregate-backup

aggregate_group_name.description:
ABACKUP(AGNAME) is an optional parameter specifying an SMS aggregate group. 


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-abackup-releasing-aggregate-backup

all.description:
(ALL) is an optional parameter specifying that DFSMShsm release all functions controlled by this command, except writing in the DFSMShsm log and printing the activity logs.


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-all-releasing-all-dfsmshsm-functions

aggregate_recover.description:
(ARECOVER) is an optional parameter specifying that DFSMShsm release for processing any ARECOVER commands currently held in queues and allow new ARECOVER commands to be received.


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-arecover-releasing-aggregate-recovery

aggregate_group_name.description:
(ARECOVER(AGNAME)) is an optional parameter specifying an SMS aggregate group.


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-arecover-releasing-aggregate-recovery

controlfile_dsn.description:
(ARECOVER(CONTROLFILEDSN)) is an optional parameter specifying a control file name. For controlfile_dsn, substitute the name of the control file against which you want DFSMShsm to hold processing.


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-arecover-releasing-aggregate-recovery

then.description: aggregate_group_name is mutually exclusive with controlfile_dsn
controlfile_dsn is mutually exclusive with aggregate_group_name

audit.description:
(AUDIT) is an optional parameter specifying that the audit function is released. DFSMShsm starts processing any queued AUDIT commands. Any AUDIT command that was interrupted by a HOLD command does not restart.


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-audit-releasing-audit-function

auto_expiration.description:
(AUTOEXPIRATION) is an optional parameter specifying that DFSMShsm release a hold on automatic expiration of data sets. Automatic expiration will take place during the next run of a DFSMShsm space management function.


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-autoexpiration-releasing-automatic-expiration

auto_migration.description:
(AUTOMIGRATION) is an optional parameter specifying that DFSMShsm release automatic volume and automatic secondary space management.

If tape migration has ended while DASD migration continues, or if DASD migration has ended while tape migration continues, this parameter allows both DASD and tape to resume their acceptability as migration targets. 


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=oprc-automigration-releasing-only-automatic-volume-automatic-secondary-space-management

backup.description:
(BACKUP) is an optional parameter specifying whether DFSMShsm should release all backup processing or release only:

    - All data set backup requests
    - All data set backup requests to either DASD or tape
    - Data set backups to DASD
    - Data set backups to tape
    - All automatic backups

BACKUP by itself specifies that DFSMShsm releases all backup processing.


 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-backup-releasing-backup

dataset_command.description:
(BACKUP(DSCOMMAND)) data set backups directed to ML1 DASD. Option takes 1 of 3 values...
1. true (boolean) - Releases data set backups for both tape and ML1 DASD requests.
2. DASD (enum) - Releases data set backups directed to ML1 DASD.
3. TAPE (enum) - Releases data set backups directed to tape.


 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-backup-releasing-backup

common_queue.description:
(COMMONQUEUE) is an optional parameter that specifies that DFSMShsm release all holds at the COMMONQUEUE, RECALL, PLACEMENT, and SELECTION levels. All unselected recall requests in the local queue move to the common recall queue (CRQ). 
 It can be set in two ways: 
  - boolean type, only true is allowed, i.e. (COMMONQUE) without RECALL option. 
  - object, with key 'recall'.
     -  'recall' can either be a boolean type (only true allowed), or be an object with two keys, 'placement' and 'selection'. 


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-commonqueue-releasing-holds-common-queue

recall.description:
(COMMONQUEUE(RECALL)) Specifies that if there is no hold at the COMMONQUEUE level, then release a hold at the RECALL, PLACEMENT, and SELECTION levels. All unselected recall requests in the local queue move to the common recall queue (CRQ). 
  'recall' can either be a boolean type (only true allowed), or be an object with two keys, 'placement' and 'selection'.


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-commonqueue-releasing-holds-common-queue

placement.description:
(COMMONQUEUE(RECALL(PLACEMENT)) Specifies that if there is no hold at the COMMONQUEUE level or RECALL level, then release a hold at the PLACEMENT level. All unselected recall requests in the local queue move to the common recall queue (CRQ).


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-commonqueue-releasing-holds-common-queue

selection.description:
(COMMONQUEUE(RECALL(SELECTION)) Specifies that if there is no hold at the COMMONQUEUE level or RECALL level, then release a hold at the SELECTION level. 


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-commonqueue-releasing-holds-common-queue

dump.description:
(DUMP) is an optional parameter specifying whether DFSMShsm should release both automatic dump and command dump or only automatic dump.
The parameters of the DUMP parameter are explained:

RELEASE DUMP,
RELEASE DUMP(AUTO),
RELEASE DUMP(FRBACKUP),
RELEASE DUMP(AUTO FRBACKUP),

AUTO
    Releases automatic dump processing only.
FRBACKUP
    Releases the dump processing of FRBACKUP target volumes.
ALL
    Releases both automatic dump processing and FRBACKUP dump processing.

    This command will have the same effect if the system issuing the command is connected to a dump group in the HSMplex. Dump tasks from this system will now be able to be used by the group master scheduler system for dump processing. 


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-dump-releasing-dump

event_driven_migration.description:
(EVENTDRIVENMIGRATION) is an optional parameter specifying that DFSMShsm should release both interval Migration and On-demand Migration. 


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-eventdrivenmigration-releasing-interval-demand-migration

expire_backup_versions.description:
(EXPIREBV) is an optional parameter specifying that DFSMShsm release the expire backup versions function. DFSMShsm starts processing any queued EXPIREBV commands.

Entering a RELEASE EXPIREBV command does not restart an EXPIREBV command that was in process at the time a RELEASE EXPIREBV command was issued. To continue processing, you must reenter the EXPIREBV command. If the function is held when the command is reentered, the command will be saved by DFSMShsm and processed once the function is released. 


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-expirebv-releasing-expire-backup-versions-function

fast_replication_backup.description:
(FRBACKUP) is an optional parameter that you specify to release the fast replication backup or dump functions. When you issue this command, DFSMShsm starts processing any queued FRBACKUP, FRBACKUP DUMP, or FRBACKUP DUMPONLY commands.

This command will have the same effect if the system issuing the command is connected to a dump group in the HSMplex. Dump tasks from this system will now be able to be used by the group master scheduler system for FRBACKUP processing. 


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-frbackup-releasing-fast-replication-backup-dump-function

fast_replication_recover.description:
(FRRECOV) is an optional parameter that you specify to release the fast replication recovery function. When you issue this command, DFSMShsm starts processing any queued FRRECOV commands. 
   It can either be a boolean type (only true allowed), or be a string type with three possible values as optional parameters: 
 - 'ALL', 'DATASET', 'TAPE'. 
 - 'ALL' means (DATASET TAPE). 


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-frrecov-releasing-fast-replication-recover-function

hard_copy.description:
(HARDCOPY) is an optional parameter specifying that DFSMShsm print four activity logs that have data. Printing occurs when ACTLOGTYPE is specified as SYSOUT on the SETSYS command.

If the activity logs are allocated to DASD, printing does not occur, but the current logs are closed and new copies of the logs are allocated for use. Allocating the activity logs to DASD allows you to view or browse the currently allocated activity logs for messages that may have passed too quickly from your screens.

The following activity logs can be printed with the RELEASE HARDCOPY command:

    Backup
    Dump
    Migration
    Command

After printing (or closing) these logs, DFSMShsm allocates new activity logs.


 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-hardcopy-releasing-activity-logs

list.description:
(LIST) is an optional parameter specifying that DFSMShsm release the list function. DFSMShsm starts processing any queued LIST commands. Any list operation that was in process when list was held is not restarted. 


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-list-releasing-list-function

log.description:
(LOG) is an optional parameter specifying that DFSMShsm begin recording in the DFSMShsm log. 


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-log-releasing-logging

migration.description:
(MIGRATION) is an optional parameter specifying whether DFSMShsm should release automatic volume and automatic secondary space management plus command space management or only automatic volume and automatic secondary space management. 
 The MIGRATION parameter, without any subparameters, specifies that DFSMShsm release command space management plus automatic volume and automatic secondary space management. 


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-migration-releasing-space-management

recall.description:
(RECALL) is an optional parameter specifying whether DFSMShsm should release automatic recall, recall by command, and deletion of a migrated data set with three different options: 
 - 'ALL', i.e. RECALL from all volumes, 
 - 'TAPE', i.e. RECALL(TAPE) from all tape volumes, 
 - 'TSO_TAPE', i.e. RECALL(TAPE(TSO) recalls that need tapes and were submitted by a TSO user, 
 - 'DASD', i.e. RECALL(DASD) recalls from DASD volumes only. 


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-recall-releasing-recall-deletion

recover.description:
(RECOVER) is an optional parameter specifying whether DFSMShsm should release all recovery processing or only tape data set recovery and restore processing.
The parameter of the RECOVER parameter is explained:

The RELEASE FRRECOV command has the same effect when the system that issues the command is connected to a CVQ. However, host volume recover tasks in the CVQ are used by only the master scheduler host when the following conditions are met:
If the host is the CVQ master scheduler, it is also eligible to perform MS assignment responsibilities for fast replication recovery requests.

    No other HOLD RECOVER is in place for the host.
    SETSYS MAXDUMPRECOVERTASKS(x) is specified with a value greater than 0.

Defaults

If you specify the RECOVER parameter with any other parameters, then the default is to release all recover and restore processing tasks.


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-recover-releasing-recovery-restore

recycle.description:
(RECYCLE) is an optional parameter specifying that DFSMShsm release the recycle function. DFSMShsm starts processing any queued recycle request. Any volumes that were being recycled when recycle was held are not restarted. 


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-recycle-releasing-recycle-function

report.description:
(REPORT) is an optional parameter specifying that DFSMShsm release the report function. DFSMShsm starts processing any queued report request. Any report that was in process when reporting was held is not restarted. 


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-report-releasing-report-function

rmm.description:
(RMM) is an optional parameter that enables the EDGTVEXT interface again after it was disabled because of an ABEND in DFSMSrmm. 


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-rmm-releasing-dfsmsrmm-function

tape_copy.description:
(TAPECOPY) is an optional parameter specifying that the tape copy function is released. DFSMShsm starts processing any queued TAPECOPY commands. 


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-tapecopy-releasing-tape-copy-function

tape_replacement.description:
(TAPEREPL) is an optional parameter specifying that the tape replace function is released. DFSMShsm starts processing any queued TAPEREPL commands. 


https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-taperepl-releasing-tape-replace-function

https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.title: DFSMShsm ARCCMDxx SETSYS Command

(SETSYS) DFSMShsm ARCCMDxx SETSYS Command.

https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.title: DFSMShsm DEFINE pool Command
https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.description: DEFINE ARPOOL, DEFINE POOL, and DEFINE VOLUMEPOOL establish DFSMShsm’s placement framework by specifying the logical pools and the corresponding physical volumes that control where migrated datasets, backup data, and aggregate backup objects are stored.

volume_pool.description:
(VOLUMEPOOL) is an optional parameter specifying a set of volumes where a data set is recalled based on the volume from which the data set migrated. A data set that migrates from a volume in the volume pool is recalled to a volume in the volume pool.
https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opdc-volumepool-identifying-groups-volumes-where-data-sets-are-recalled

volume_pool_id.description:
For poolid, substitute from 1 to 8 alphanumeric characters for the name of the volume pool.
https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opdc-volumepool-identifying-groups-volumes-where-data-sets-are-recalled

volumes.description:
VOLUMEPOOL(poolid VOLUMES(volser)) specifies the volumes belonging to the volume pool where the data sets are recalled. When you specify multiple volumes for a pool ID, DFSMShsm tries to recall data sets to the volume with the most space. If there is not enough space on the volume, DFSMShsm tries recalling the data set to up to four different volumes in the volume pool.
For volser, substitute the serial number of the primary volume or volumes making up the volume pool where data sets are recalled.
https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opdc-volumepool-identifying-groups-volumes-where-data-sets-are-recalled

pool.description:
(POOL) is an optional parameter specifying the set of initial characters of the data set name for a group of data sets and the set of non-SMS-managed volumes where the group of data sets is to be recalled. Each poolid and associated volume list is a user-defined pool. When recall occurs, the set of initial characters of the data set name forces the recall of those data sets to one of the specific volumes identified with the VOLUMES subparameter. To remove the association between a pool ID and its associated volumes from pool control, you omit the VOLUMES subparameter when you specify POOL.
https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opdc-pool-identifying-non-sms-managed-volumes-where-data-sets-same-first-qualifier-are-recalled

pool_id.description:
For poolid, substitute the set of initial characters of the data set name of those data sets you want recalled to the specified volume or volumes. The poolid can end with a period if POOL is the first keyword on the command.
https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opdc-pool-identifying-non-sms-managed-volumes-where-data-sets-same-first-qualifier-are-recalled

volumes.description:
POOL(poolid VOLUMES(volser ...)) specifies the volumes where the data sets with the set of initial characters specified with the POOL parameter are recalled. When you specify multiple volumes for a pool ID, DFSMShsm tries to recall data sets to the volume with the most space. If there is not enough space on the volume, DFSMShsm can try recalling the data set to up to four different volumes from the same pool.
For volser ..., substitute the serial numbers of the volumes where the group of data sets is to be recalled.
https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opdc-pool-identifying-non-sms-managed-volumes-where-data-sets-same-first-qualifier-are-recalled

aggregate_recovery_pool.description:
(ARPOOL) is an optional parameter specifying a pool of volumes to be used as target volumes during an aggregate recovery.
https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-arpool-identifying-volumes-aggregate-recovery

aggregate_group_name.description:
It specifies the name of the aggregate group. For agname substitute an aggregate group name that has been defined. The defined pool will be used for recovery of that aggregate group's data sets.
If no agname is specified, the command fails.
 * - specifies that the volumes are assigned to a general pool of aggregate recovery volumes. The general pool of volumes is used when recovering an aggregate group that does not have a specific ARPOOL defined.
https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-arpool-identifying-volumes-aggregate-recovery

all.description:
(ALL) specifies that all currently mounted ADDVOL ML1 and primary volumes be defined as the respective volume pools for aggregate recovery. Specifying the ALL parameter is equivalent to specifying the L0VOLS(*) and ML1VOLS(*) parameters. ALL is mutually exclusive with the L0VOLS and ML1VOLS parameters.
https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-arpool-identifying-volumes-aggregate-recovery

primary_volumes.description:
L0VOLS(volser ...) specifies the list of volumes used as target volumes during recovery of nonmigrated non-SMS-managed data sets. If you specify a parameter of L0VOLS(*), all currently mounted ADDVOL primary volumes (up to 59) will be used as the primary volume pool for aggregate recovery.
L0VOLS is mutually exclusive with the ALL subparameter. You can use L0VOLS with ML1VOLS.
https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-arpool-identifying-volumes-aggregate-recovery

migration_level1_volumes.description:
ML1VOLS(volser ...) specifies the list of volumes as target volumes during recovery of migrated data sets to ML1 volumes. If you specify a parameter of ML1VOLS(*), all currently mounted ADDVOL ML1 volumes will be used as the ML1 volume pool for aggregate recovery.
ML1VOLS is mutually exclusive with the ALL subparameter. You can use ML1VOLS with L0VOLS.
https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-arpool-identifying-volumes-aggregate-recovery

https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.title: DFSMShsm ARCCMDxx PATCH Command
https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.description:
(PATCH) The PATCH command changes storage within the DFSMShsm address space under the protect key of the DFSMShsm problem program. You can identify the storage location to be changed with an absolute address or a qualified address. 
https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=commands-maintenance-command-patch

change_address.description:
(address) The address of the location you want to change. 
 - Enter an absolute address as one to eight hexadecimal digits followed by a period (hhhhhhhh.). 
 - Enter a qualified address as loadmodulename.csectname.+hhhhhh or .csectname.+hhhhhh 
______________________________________________
YAML Requirements:
When this key is specified, one of the following keys is also required:
 - change_binary_data
 - change_character_data
 - change_hex_data 
https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-address-specifying-location-change

change_binary_data.description:
(BITS(bits)) The binary data you want to enter at the specified address. An eight-character string specifying which bit or bits are to be turned on or off. A period (.) means no change, a 1 means set the bit on, and a 0 means set the bit off. 
https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-bits-specifying-bits-change

change_hex_data.description:
(data) The hexadecimal data you want to enter at the specified address. You cannot specify more than 256 bytes (512 hexadecimal digits). 
https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-data-specifying-data

change_character_data.description:
(data) The character data you want to enter at the specified address. You cannot specify more than 256 bytes. 
https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-data-specifying-data

output_data_set.description:
OUTDATASET(dsname) The fully qualified name of the data set where DFSMShsm is to write the PATCH results. 
https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-outdataset-specifying-output-location-patch-results

change_mvt_volser.description:
VOLUME(volser) This is used to request the modification of a specific mounted volume table (MVT) that contains a matching volume serial number for a DFSMShsm-managed level 0 volume or migration level 1 volume. 
ww.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=oppc-volume-changing-mounted-volume-table-specific-volume-serial-number

verify_address.description:
VERIFY(address ...) The qualified or absolute address of a location to verify data from before making the change. 
https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-verify-verifying-data-before-changing-it

verify_binary_data.description:
VERIFY(... BITS(bits)) The binary data you want to verify at the specified address. An eight-character string specifying which bit or bits are to be turned on or off. A period (.) means no change, a 1 means set the bit on, and a 0 means set the bit off. 
https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-verify-verifying-data-before-changing-it

verify_hex_data.description:
VERIFY(... data) The hexadecimal data you want to verify at the specified address. You cannot specify more than 256 bytes (512 hexadecimal digits). 
https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-verify-verifying-data-before-changing-it

verify_character_data.description:
VERIFY(... data) The character data you want to verify at the specified address. You cannot specify more than 256 bytes. 
https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-verify-verifying-data-before-changing-it

verify.description:
VERIFY Verifying data before changing it. 
______________________________________________
YAML Requirements: 
When this key is specified, the following keys are also required: 
 - verify_address 
 and one of the following: 
 - verify_binary_data
 - verify_character_data
 - verify_hex_data 
https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-verify-verifying-data-before-changing-it

https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.title: Defining storage locations: LOCDEF
https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.description: Use the LOCDEF command to define installation defined storage locations to DFSMSrmm.

location.title: Location name : LOCATION(name)
location.description: Specifies the name of the location being defined. Can be any 1 to 8 character name or LOCAL, DISTANT, REMOTE, or SHELF.

management_type.title: Shelf-management technique : MANAGEMENTTYPE(BINS|NOBINS)
management_type.description: Identifies the shelf-management technique for the location. BINS assigns bin numbers to volumes. NOBINS means the location is not shelf-managed.

automove.title: Automove : AUTOMOVE(YES|NO)
automove.description: Identifies whether automated movement is allowed.

priority.title: Priority : PRIORITY(1-9999)
priority.description: Defines the priority of this location relative to other locations. Lower numbers have higher priorities.

type_of_location.title: Type of Location : TYPE(STORAGE | STORAGE,HOME | LIBRARY)

media_name_array.title: Media type identifier : MEDIANAME(media_name)
media_name_array.description: Specifies a media name. Accepts a list of media names or * for any.

https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.title: ICEPRM
https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.description: DFSORT installation Options https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=defaults-installation-options

jcl_environment.description: (JCL) Specifies that this set of installation defaults is for ICEAM1, the batch direct invocation environment. ICEAM1 is used at run time when DFSORT is invoked directly (that is, not through programs) by batch jobs, provided that an enabled time-of-day environment (ICETDx) is not activated

invocation_environment.description: (INV) Specifies that this set of installation defaults is for ICEAM2, the batch program invocation environment. ICEAM2 is used at run time when DFSORT is invoked through batch programs, provided that an enabled time-of-day installation environment (ICETDx) is not activated

tso_environment.description: (TSO) Specifies that this set of installation defaults is for ICEAM3, the TSO direct invocation environment. ICEAM3 is used at run time when DFSORT is invoked directly (that is, not through programs) by foreground TSO users, provided that an enabled time-of-day installation environment (ICETDx) is not activated

tso_program_invocation_environment.description: (TSOINV) Specifies that this set of installation defaults is for ICEAM4, the TSO program invocation environment. ICEAM4 is used at run time when DFSORT is invoked through programs by foreground TSO users, provided that an enabled time-of-day installation environment (ICETDx) is not activated

time_of_day_environment_1.description: (TD1) Specifies that this set of installation defaults is for ICETD1, the indicated time-of-day installation environment. ICETD1 is used at run time when it is activated for the time-of-day of the run, provided it is enabled by the invocation environment (ICEAMx) in effect

time_of_day_environment_2.description: (TD2) Specifies that this set of installation defaults is for ICETD2, the indicated time-of-day installation environment. ICETD2 is used at run time when it is activated for the time-of-day of the run, provided it is enabled by the invocation environment (ICEAMx) in effect

time_of_day_environment_3.description: (TD3) Specifies that this set of installation defaults is for ICETD3, the indicated time-of-day installation environment. ICETD3 is used at run time when it is activated for the time-of-day of the run, provided it is enabled by the invocation environment (ICEAMx) in effect

time_of_day_environment_4.description: (TD4) Specifies that this set of installation defaults is for ICETD4, the indicated time-of-day installation environment. ICETD4 is used at run time when it is activated for the time-of-day of the run, provided it is enabled by the invocation environment (ICEAMx) in effect

enable_td_environments.description: (ENABLE) Specifies which time-of-day installation environments (ICETDx) are enabled for this invocation environment. One or more of the ICETDx environments can be enabled for any ICEAMx environment

abend_code.description: (ABCODE) Specifies whether to abend with a user completion code equal to the critical error message number, or with a specific number between 1-99

alternate_collating_sequence.description: (ALTSEQ) Specifies changes to the alternate translation table. Any modifications you specify are applied to the standard EBCDIC translation table.

above_16mb_reserve_all.description: (ARESALL) Specifies the amount of main storage reserved above 16 MB virtual for system use while DFSORT is running. Value must be specified in bytes as a decimal value within the range of 0 to 16515072 (16128 KB)

above_16mb_reserve_invoker.description: (ARESINV) Specifies the amount of main storage reserved above 16 MB virtual, while DFSORT is running, for an invoking program's user exit routines that reside above or use space above 16 MB virtual. Value must be specified in bytes as a decimal value within the range of 0 to 16515072 (16128 KB)

enable_cache_fast_write.description: (CFW) Specifies whether DFSORT can use cache fast write when processing SORTWKdd data sets that reside on devices connected to storage subsystems that support it

enable_ch_translation.description: (CHALT) Specifies whether format CH fields are translated by the alternate collating sequence.

enable_record_count_check.description: (CHECK) Specifies whether record count should be checked for applications that use the E35 user exit routine without an output data set

enable_vsam_control_interval_access.description: (CINV) Specifies whether DFSORT can use control interval access for VSAM data sets

cobol_exit_library.description: (COBEXIT) Specifies the library for COBOL E15 and E35 routines

collation_key_rules.description: (COLLKEY) Specifies the collation rules. DFSORT's Unicode Collation behavior can be modified according to your cultural environment. Accepts predefined values (UCA600, UCA410, UCA400R1) or custom locale format (UCAnnn_L_R_V where L=Language, R=Region, V=Variant)

enable_diagnostic_messages.description: (DIAGSIM) Specifies whether all DFSORT control statements and messages, including diagnostic messages (ICE800I through ICE999I), are printed

dynamic_storage_limit.description: (DSA) Specifies the maximum amount of storage available to DFSORT for dynamic storage adjustment of a Blockset sort application when SIZE/MAINSIZE=MAX is in effect. If you specify a DSA value greater than the TMAXLIM value, you allow DFSORT to use more storage than the TMAXLIM value if doing so should improve performance. The amount of storage DFSORT uses is subject to the DSA value as well as system limits such as region size. Value must be specified in MB within the range of 0 to 2000

dataspace_size_limit.description: (DSPSIZE) Specifies the maximum amount of data space to be used for dataspace sorting. DFSORT uses data space to sort large pieces of data, reducing CPU time and elapsed time. Value can be 'maximum' to let DFSORT dynamically determine the maximum amount based on file size and system paging activity, or a numeric value in MB (0-9999) to specify a specific limit

dynamic_allocation.description: (DYNALOC) Specifies the default values to be used when dynamic allocation is requested using the DYNAUTO installation parameter or the DYNALLOC runtime parameter

device.description: The device (d) specifies the default device name for work data sets to be dynamically allocated

maximum_work_datasets.description: The number (n) specifies the default maximum number of work data sets to be dynamically allocated, from 1 to 255
The number (n) specifies the default maximum number of work data sets to be dynamically allocated, from 1 to 255

device.description: The device (d) specifies the default device name for work data sets to be dynamically allocated. Can be a device name (string) or device type number > 255

additional_work_datasets.description: (DYNAPCT) Specifies additional work data sets to be dynamically allocated with zero space. Value can be a percentage (0-254) where the number of additional work data sets is calculated as n * x% (where n is the DYNALLOC maximum), or 'auto' to allocate additional datasets only when DFSORT cannot determine file size

dynamic_work_space_allocation.description: (DYNAUTO) Specifies whether work space should automatically be dynamically allocated at run time. Value 'auto' allocates when no SORTWKdd present, 'auto_ignore_sortwkdd' allocates and deallocates SORTWKdd before sorting (except tape), 'manual' disables automatic allocation

dynamic_space_allocation.description: (DYNSPC) Specifies the total default primary space allocation for all of the dynamically allocated work data sets when the input file size is unknown, that is, when DFSORT cannot determine the input file size for a sort application and the number of records is not supplied by a FILSZ or SIZE value. Value must be in MB (1-65535)

user_exit_program.description: (EFS) Specifies the name of a user-written Extended Function Support (EFS) program to be called by DFSORT. Value can be the program name or 'NONE' to indicate no EFS program should be called

preserve_equal_record_order.description: (EQUALS) Specifies whether the order of records that collate identically for sort or merge applications should be preserved from input to output

error_response_type.description: (ERET) Specifies the action to be taken if DFSORT encounters a critical error. Value 'terminate' causes abend with user completion code equal to the appropriate message number (with ABCODE=MSG), or specific number 1-99 (ABCODE=n). Value 'return_code_16' terminates with return code 16

enable_recovery_routine.description: (ESTAE) Specifies whether DFSORT can use its ESTAE recovery routine for the entire run

exit_return_code_check.description: (EXITCK) Specifies whether DFSORT terminates or continues when it receives certain invalid return codes from E15 or E35 user exit routines

maximum_expanded_storage.description: (EXPMAX) Specifies the maximum total amount of available central storage to be used at any one time. Value 'maximum' lets DFSORT determine dynamically. Value must be specified in bytes as a decimal value within the range of 0 to 8388606 MB if 0, memory sorting is not used. Value p% (0-100%) sets maximum as percentage of configured central storage (TUNE=OLD) or available resources at runtime

maximum_old_storage.description: (EXPOLD) Specifies the maximum total amount of old central storage. Value 'maximum' lets DFSORT determine dynamically. Value must be specified in bytes as a decimal value within the range of 0 to 8388606 MB if 0, memory sorting is not used. Value p% (0-100%) sets maximum as percentage of configured central storage (TUNE=OLD) or available resources at runtime

minimum_reserved_storage.description: (EXPRES) Specifies the minimum amount of available central storage to be reserved for non-Hipersorting, non-memory object sorting, and non-dataspace sorting applications. Value 'maximum' reserves all available storage (disables memory sorting), n (0-8388606 MB) reserves fixed amount, p% (0-100%) reserves percentage of configured central storage (TUNE=OLD) or available resources at runtime (TUNE=STOR/DISK/DDYN)

estimate_input_filesize.description: (FSZEST) Specifies whether DFSORT is to treat exact filesize values as estimates
