iebgener_alias.description: (GENER) Specifies the name that ICEGENER is to use to transfer control to the IEBGENER system utility

generator_padding.description: (GNPAD) Specifies the action to be taken by ICEGENER when the SYSUT2 LRECL is larger than the SYSUT1 LRECL (LRECL padding). Issues ICE202I and continues with return code 0 (return_code_0) or 4 (return_code_4), or transfers control to IEBGENER (fallback_iebgener). Ignored when specified via JCL or TSO parameter

generator_truncation.description: (GNTRUNC) Specifies the action to be taken by ICEGENER when the SYSUT2 LRECL is smaller than the SYSUT1 LRECL (LRECL truncation). Issues ICE202I and continues with return code 0 (return_code_0) or 4 (return_code_4), or transfers control to IEBGENER (fallback_iebgener). Ignored when specified via JCL or TSO parameter

hiperspace_limit.description: (HIPRMAX) Specifies the maximum amount of Hiperspace to be committed for Hipersorting. Hiperspace is high-performance data space in central storage, reducing I/O, EXCPs, and channel usage. OPTIMAL allows dynamic determination. Specify MB value (0-32767) to limit size, or percentage (0-100%) of configured central storage

idrc_compaction_percent.description: (IDRCPCT) Specifies a percentage which represents the approximate amount of data compaction achieved by using the Improved Data Recording Capability feature of IBM tape devices that support compaction

enable_initialization_exit.description: (IEXIT) Specifies whether DFSORT is to pass control to an initialization exit (ICEIEXIT) for resource control

ignore_checkpoint_restart.description: (IGNCKPT) Specifies the action to be taken if checkpoint/restart is requested for a sort application at run time and the Blockset technique (which does not support checkpoint/restart) can be used

io_maximum_buffer_space.description: (IOMAXBF) Specifies the maximum buffer space DFSORT can use for SORTIN, SORTINnn, and SORTOUT data sets on disk as a decimal value within the range of 8388608 (8 MB) to 268435456 (256 MB)

list_control_statements.description: (LIST) Specifies whether DFSORT program control statements are printed to the message data set

list_efs_control_statements.description: (LISTX) Specifies whether to print control statements returned by an EFS program are printed to the message data set

locale.description: (LOCALE) Specifies whether locale processing is to be used and if so, designates the active locale. Locale names follow the format: Language_Territory[.Codeset][@modifier] (e.g., Fr_BE.IBM-1148@euro, En_US, FR_CA). Names are not case sensitive and can be up to 32 characters. See 'Locale naming conventions' in z/OS XL C/C++ Programming Guide for a complete description of the naming conventions for locales.

max_below_16mb_storage_bytes.description: (MAXLIM) Specifies an upper limit to the total amount of main storage, below 16 MB virtual, available to DFSORT. Specifies the number of bytes as a decimal value within the range of 90112 (88 KB) to 16777208 (16 MB minus 8 bytes)

minimum_storage_limit.description: (MINLIM) Specifies a lower limit to the amount of main storage available to DFSORT when SIZE=n or MAINSIZE=n is in effect. Specifies the number of bytes as a decimal value. The minimum value is 90112 (88 KB). Lowering below 440 KB can degrade performance for some applications

memory_object_size.description: (MOSIZE) Specifies the total amount of memory object storage to be used for memory object sorting. 'MAXIMUM' allows DFSORT to determine size dynamically. Specify MB value (0-2147483646) to limit size, or percentage (0-100%) of available central storage

enable_memory_object_workspace.description: (MOWRK) Specifies whether the memory object storage available to DFSORT for memory object sorting can be used as intermediate work space

message_console.description: (MSGCON) Specifies the class of messages to be written to the master console. ALL writes all messages except parameter-in-effect (ICE127I-ICE133I, ICE235I) and diagnostic (ICE800I-ICE999I). CRITICAL writes only critical messages. NONE disables console messages. Note: ICE097I and ICE158A always written to console regardless of this setting

message_ddname.description: (MSGDDN) Specifies an alternate ddname for the message data set. The name must be unique within the job step. Do not use a name that is used by DFSORT (for example, SORTIN). If the ddname specified is not available at run time, SYSOUT is used instead

message_print.description: (MSGPRT) Specifies the class of messages to be printed. Messages are written to the message data set. ALL prints all messages except diagnostics (ICE800I-ICE999I); control statements printed only if LIST in effect. CRITICAL prints only critical messages; control statements printed only if LIST in effect. NONE disables message and control statement printing

missing_message_dataset.description: (NOMSGDD) Specifies whether DFSORT terminates or continues when the message data set is required but not present. QUIT terminates with error message to console. ALL/CRITICAL/NONE continue processing with equivalent MSGCON setting for console messages

null_outfil.description: (NULLOFL) Specifies the action to be taken by DFSORT when there are no data records for an OUTFIL data set, as indicated by a DATA count of 0 in message ICE227I. Note: NULLOUT applies to the SORTOUT data set. NULLOFL applies to OUTFIL data sets

null_sortout.description: (NULLOUT) Specifies the action to be taken by DFSORT when there are no records for the SORTOUT data set, as indicated by an OUT count of 0 in message ICE054I. Not applicable when SORTOUT absent, tape work data sets used, or Blockset not selected for merge. Note: NULLOUT applies to the SORTOUT data set. NULLOFL applies to OUTFIL data sets

outfil_max_buffer_bytes.description: (ODMAXBF) Specifies the maximum buffer space in bytes that DFSORT can use for each OUTFIL data set as a decimal value within the range of 262144 (256 KB) to 16777216 (16 MB)

release_unused_space.description: (OUTREL) Specifies whether unused temporary output data set space is to be released

secondary_space_allocation.description: (OUTSEC) Specifies whether DFSORT uses automatic secondary allocation for output data sets that are temporary or new. YES (true) uses 25% of primary allocation as secondary. NO (false) disables automatic secondary allocation. n (1-1000) uses n percent of the primary allocation as secondary. This parameter is not used for a tape work data set sort or Conventional merge. Note: OUTSEC=0 is equivalent to OUTSEC=NO

above_region_storage.description: (OVERRGN) Specifies the amount of main storage, below 16 MB virtual, above the REGION value that Blockset attempts to obtain from the area defined by the difference between the system's IEFUSI region limit and region size values. Specifies the number of bytes as a decimal value within the range 0 to 16515072 (16128 KB). Default: 65536 (64 KB) for JCL, TSO, TD1, TD2, TD3, and TD4 environments; 16384 (16 KB) for INV and TSOINV environments

summary_field_overflow.description: (OVFLO) Specifies the action to be taken by DFSORT when BI, FI, PD or ZD summary fields overflow

output_lrecl_padding.description: (PAD) Specifies the action to be taken by DFSORT when the SORTOUT LRECL is larger than the SORTIN/SORTINnn LRECL, for the cases where DFSORT allows LRECL padding. Note: For an ICEGENER application, the GNPAD value is used and the PAD value is ignored

parameter_ddname.description: (PARMDDN) Specifies an alternate ddname for the DFSORT DFSPARM data set. If this ddname is present at run time, DFSORT uses it to override parameters from other sources. The name must be unique within the job step. Do not use a name that is used by DFSORT (for example, SYSIN)

reserve_all_below_line.description: (RESALL) Specifies the number of bytes to be reserved in a region below 16 MB virtual while DFSORT is running when SIZE/MAINSIZE=MAX is in effect. Value must be in the range of 4096 (4 KB) to 16515072 (16128 KB)

reset_vsam_datasets.description: (RESET) Specifies whether DFSORT should process a VSAM output data set defined with REUSE as a NEW or MOD data set. YES resets the high-used RBA to zero and treats the data set as initially empty. NO does not reset the high-used RBA and treats the data set as initially non-empty

reserve_invoking_program.description: (RESINV) Indicates the number of bytes to be reserved for the invoking program, while DFSORT is running, when DFSORT is program invoked and SIZE/MAINSIZE=MAX is in effect. This space is usually required for data handling by the invoking program or user exits (for example, COBOL and PL/I invoked sorts). Ignored when specified via JCL or TSO parameter

system_determined_blocksize.description: (SDB) Specifies whether DFSORT should use system-determined optimum block size for output data sets when block size is zero or defaulted to zero. large_blocks allows tape block sizes >32760 bytes for improved performance. small_blocks (alias: SDB=YES) limits to <=32760 bytes. input_based allows >32760 only when input has >32760. disabled disables system-determined block size (not recommended). Default: input_based

system_determined_blocksize_messages.description: (SDBMSG) Specifies whether the system-determined optimum block size should be used for DFSORT message data sets and ICETOOL message and list data sets when the block size is specified as zero or defaulted to zero

main_storage_size.description: (SIZE) Specifies the amount of main storage DFSORT attempts to use. MAX allows DFSORT to calculate the maximum available storage based on TMAXLIM/DSA (Blockset) or MAXLIM (non-Blockset). Specify a value in bytes (90112 to 2097152000) to set a fixed amount

smf_record_type.description: (SMF) Specifies whether DFSORT produces SMF type-16 statistical records. 'short_record' produces basic records without record-length distribution or data set sections. 'full_record' produces complete records including distribution and data set information (may degrade performance for variable-length records). 'disabled' disables SMF record production

use_reformatted_output_length.description: (SOLRF) Specifies whether DFSORT should set the SORTOUT LRECL to the reformatted record length when the SORTOUT LRECL is unknown

conventional_module_library.description: (SORTLIB) determines whether DFSORT searches LINKLIB or a private library separate from LINKLIB for the Conventional technique modules used for a tape work data set sort or Conventional merge application

spanned_record_action.description: (SPANINC) Specifies the action to be taken by DFSORT when one or more incomplete spanned records are detected in a variable spanned input data set

svc_configuration.description: (SVC) Specifies an SVC number that you choose for the DFSORT SVC routine. Specifies the SVC number and optionally selects an alternate DFSORT module

number.description: Specifies your SVC number. Must be the decimal number 109 or a decimal number between 200 and 255. The SVC number you choose must be valid at your site. Defaults to 109 when omitted with alternate_module

alternate_module.description: (ALT) When true, uses alternate DFSORT module IGX00038 instead of the default module IGX00017. Only applicable when SVC number is 109
(ALT) When true, uses alternate DFSORT module IGX00038 instead of the default module IGX00017. Only applicable when SVC number is 109

signed_zero_handling.description: (SZERO) Specifies whether DFSORT should treat numeric -0 and +0 values as signed (that is, different) or unsigned (that is, the same) for collation, comparisons, editing, conversions, minimums, and maximums

termination_exit_enabled.description: (TEXIT) Specifies whether DFSORT is to pass control to a termination exit (ICETEXIT)

maximum_main_storage.description: (TMAXLIM) Specifies an upper limit to the total amount of main storage, both above and below 16 MB virtual, available to DFSORT when SIZE/MAINSIZE=MAX is in effect and Blockset is selected. Value in bytes as decimal (maximum 2097152000 = 2000 MB)

tune_optimization.description: (TUNE) Specifies whether DFSORT should favor optimization of central storage or disk work space. 'Storage' allocates storage as needed in balanced increments and increases dynamic work dataset allocations. 'Disk' allocates all required storage at initialization and decreases dynamic work dataset allocations to minimize disk space. 'Dynamic' allocates all storage at initialization only with dynamic allocation, otherwise allocates as needed. 'Old' allocates storage as needed in fixed increments and decreases dynamic work dataset allocations

lrecl_truncation_return_code.description: (TRUNC) Specifies the action to be taken by DFSORT when the SORTOUT LRECL is smaller than the SORTIN/ SORTINnn LRECL, for the cases where DFSORT allows LRECL truncation

verify_output_sequence.description: (VERIFY) Specifies whether the sequence of output records is to be verified

allow_virtual_work_allocation.description: (VIO) Specifies whether virtual allocations for sort work data sets are dynamically reallocated to real disk locations

truncate_long_variable_length_records.description: (VLLONG) Specifies whether DFSORT is to truncate 'long' variable-length output records. A long output record has length greater than the LRECL of the SORTOUT or OUTFIL data set

pad_short_compare_fields.description: (VLSCMP) Specifies whether DFSORT is to pad 'short' variable-length INCLUDE/OMIT compare fields with binary zeros. Applies to INCLUDE and OMIT statements and INCLUDE/OMIT parameters of OUTFIL statement

allow_short_variable_fields.description: (VLSHRT) Specifies whether DFSORT is to continue processing if a 'short' variable-length SORT/MERGE control field, INCLUDE/OMIT compare field, or a SUM summary field is found. Applies to SORT, MERGE, INCLUDE, OMIT, and SUM statements, and to INCLUDE/OMIT parameters of OUTFIL statement

vsam_buffer_allocation.description: (VSAMBSP) Specifies the number of VSAM buffers DFSORT can use when sorting using the Blockset technique. 'Maximum' uses maximum buffers (most performance benefit but may cause excessive paging on storage-constrained systems). 'Optimal' uses optimal buffers (substantial performance benefit with minimal paging impact). 'Minimum' uses minimum buffers

allow_empty_vsam_input.description: (VSAMEMT) Specifies whether DFSORT should accept an empty VSAM input data set

enable_vsam_inplace_sort.description: (VSAMIO) Specifies whether DFSORT should allow a VSAM data set defined with REUSE to be sorted in-place

release_unused_work_dataset.description: (WRKREL) Specifies whether unused temporary SORTWKdd data set space is released

work_dataset_secondary_allocation.description: (WRKSEC) Specifies whether DFSORT uses automatic secondary allocation for temporary JCL SORTWKdd data sets when no secondary allocation amount is specified. 'Auto' enables automatic secondary allocation at 25% of primary allocation. 'Never' disables automatic secondary allocation. Numeric values (1-1000) enable automatic secondary allocation at the specified percentage of primary allocation

century_window.description: (Y2PAST) Specifies the sliding or fixed century window for Y2x formats to interpret two-digit years as four-digit years. For sliding window, specify a value between 0 and 100 representing the number of years to subtract from the current year to set the beginning of the window. The window slides as the current year changes (e.g., 81 would set 1925-2024 in 2006 and 1926-2025 in 2007). For fixed window, specify a value between 1000 and 3000 representing the beginning year of the window (e.g., 1962 would set 1962-2061)

printable_zoned_decimal.description: (ZDPRINT) Specifies whether positive zoned-decimal (ZD) fields resulting from summation must be converted to printable numbers (that is, whether the zone of the last digit should be changed from a hexadecimal C to a hexadecimal F)

enable_zsort_accelerator.description: (ZSORT) Specifies IBM Integrated Accelerator for Z Sort can be used for sorting

saturday_schedule.description: (SAT) Specifies a time range, consisting of a starting time (s1) and ending time (e1), during which this time-of-day installation environment can be activated for Saturday. s1 and e1 must each be specified as hhmm using a 24-hour clock where hh is in hours (00-23) and mm is in minutes (00-59). Note: A time range cannot cross midnight; the start time (s1) must not be greater than the end time (e1)

sunday_schedule.description: (SUN) Specifies a time range, consisting of a starting time (s1) and ending time (e1), during which this time-of-day installation environment can be activated for Sunday. s1 and e1 must each be specified as hhmm using a 24-hour clock where hh is in hours (00-23) and mm is in minutes (00-59). Note: A time range cannot cross midnight; the start time (s1) must not be greater than the end time (e1)

monday_schedule.description: (MON) Specifies a time range, consisting of a starting time (s1) and ending time (e1), during which this time-of-day installation environment can be activated for Monday. s1 and e1 must each be specified as hhmm using a 24-hour clock where hh is in hours (00-23) and mm is in minutes (00-59). Note: A time range cannot cross midnight; the start time (s1) must not be greater than the end time (e1)

tuesday_schedule.description: (TUE) Specifies a time range, consisting of a starting time (s1) and ending time (e1), during which this time-of-day installation environment can be activated for Tuesday. s1 and e1 must each be specified as hhmm using a 24-hour clock where hh is in hours (00-23) and mm is in minutes (00-59). Note: A time range cannot cross midnight; the start time (s1) must not be greater than the end time (e1)

wednesday_schedule.description: (WED) Specifies a time range, consisting of a starting time (s1) and ending time (e1), during which this time-of-day installation environment can be activated for Wednesday. s1 and e1 must each be specified as hhmm using a 24-hour clock where hh is in hours (00-23) and mm is in minutes (00-59). Note: A time range cannot cross midnight; the start time (s1) must not be greater than the end time (e1)

thursday_schedule.description: (THU) Specifies a time range, consisting of a starting time (s1) and ending time (e1), during which this time-of-day installation environment can be activated for Thursday. s1 and e1 must each be specified as hhmm using a 24-hour clock where hh is in hours (00-23) and mm is in minutes (00-59). Note: A time range cannot cross midnight; the start time (s1) must not be greater than the end time (e1)

friday_schedule.description: (FRI) Specifies a time range, consisting of a starting time (s1) and ending time (e1), during which this time-of-day installation environment can be activated for Friday. s1 and e1 must each be specified as hhmm using a 24-hour clock where hh is in hours (00-23) and mm is in minutes (00-59). Note: A time range cannot cross midnight; the start time (s1) must not be greater than the end time (e1)

weekday_schedule.description: (WKDAYS) Specifies a time range for weekdays (Monday through Friday) during which this time-of-day installation environment can be activated. This is equivalent to specifying MON, TUE, WED, THU, and FRI. If WKDAYS is specified, individual weekday properties (monday, tuesday, wednesday, thursday, friday) cannot be specified. Note: A time range cannot cross midnight; the start time must not be greater than the end time

weekend_schedule.description: (WKEND) Specifies a time range for weekend days (Saturday and Sunday) during which this time-of-day installation environment can be activated. This is equivalent to specifying SAT and SUN. If WKEND is specified, saturday and sunday properties cannot be specified. Note: A time range cannot cross midnight; the start time must not be greater than the end time

alldays_schedule.description: (ALLDAYS) Specifies a time range for all days of the week (Sunday through Saturday) during which this time-of-day installation environment can be activated. This is equivalent to specifying SUN, MON, TUE, WED, THU, FRI, and SAT. If ALLDAYS is specified, no other day properties (sunday, monday, tuesday, wednesday, thursday, friday, saturday, weekday, weekend) can be specified. Note: A time range cannot cross midnight; the start time must not be greater than the end time

allOf.$comment: ALLDAYS cannot be combined with any other day
WKDAYS cannot be combined with individual weekdays (MON-FRI)
WKEND cannot be combined with SUN or SAT

https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.title: DFSMShsm ARCCMDxx SETSYS commands for space management and command migration functions
https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.description:
(SETSYS) DFSMShsm SETSYS parameters controlling the space management environment. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=dsar-setsys-command-establishing-changing-values-dfsmshsm-control-parameters
https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.$comment:
(MIGRATION) Defining parameters and subparameters affecting DFSMShsm space management and migration functions. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=parameters-setsys-fast-path-dfsmshsm-functions

max_dataset_extents.description:
(MAXEXTENTS) Specifying the number of extents that, if equaled or exceeded, causes DFSMShsm to reallocate all non-VSAM data sets. 
 Specify a decimal number from 0 to 16 indicating the number of extents to allow before DFSMShsm does extent reduction. If you specify 0, DFSMShsm does not perform extent reduction. The default is 0 extents. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-maxextents-specifying-number-extents-cause-extent-reduction

max_tasks_migrate.description:
(MAXMIGRATIONTASKS) Specifying the maximum number of automatic volume space management tasks that can run concurrently. 
 You can specify a decimal number from 1 to 15 to represent the number of data set recovery tasks to be run concurrently. The default is 2 tasks. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-maxmigrationtasks-specifying-maximum-number-automatic-volume-space-management-tasks-that-can-run-concurrently

class_transition.description:
(CLASSTRANSITION) Specifying if class transitions will be performed during event-driven migration. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-classtransitions-specifying-if-class-transitions-will-be-performed-during-event-driven-migration

event_driven_migration.description: (EVENTDRIVENMIGRATION) Specifying if class transitions will be performed during event-driven migration.

enable.description:
(EVENTDRIVENMIGRATION(Y|N)) If true (Y), data sets will be class transitioned during event-driven migration. If false (N), class transitions will not occur during event-driven migration processing and only occur during primary space management. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-classtransitions-specifying-if-class-transitions-will-be-performed-during-event-driven-migration

use_serialization_exit.description:
(SERIALIZATIONEXIT(Y|N)) Specifies whether the user data set serialization error exit will be used during event-driven migration. 
 If true (Y), the user data set serialization error exits will be used during event-driven migration. 
 If false (N), the user data set serialization error exits will not be used during event-driven migration. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-classtransitions-specifying-if-class-transitions-will-be-performed-during-event-driven-migration

cloud_migration.description:
(CLOUDMIGRATION) Specifying the type of migration to CLOUD. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-cloudmigration-specifying-type-migration-cloud

allow_reconnection.description:
(RECONNECT(NONE|ALL)) Specifying data sets eligible for fast subsequent migration (FSM) can be reconnected to the CLOUD from which they were recalled. 
 If (NONE), data sets are not eligible for fast subsequent migration and are not reconnected to the CLOUD from which they were recalled. 
 If (ALL), All data sets that are eligible for standard migration and satisfy fast subsequent migration eligibility requirements are reconnected to the CLOUD that the data set was recalled from; including data sets that would have otherwise been migrated to an ML1 or ML2 volume. 
 A data set can be reconnected if all fast subsequent migration requirements are satisfied. For more information about these requirements, see fast subsequentmigration (reconnection) eligibility requirements.
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=tasks-reconnecting-data-sets-using-fast-subsequent-migration#fast_subsequent_migration_concept__fast_subsequent_migration_requirements

days_unreferenced.description:
(DAYS) specifying the number of contiguous days a data set must remain unreferenced before the data set is eligible for migration. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-days-specifying-minimum-migration-age-data-set

scratch_expired_datasets.description:
(EXPIREDDATASETS) Specifying whether DFSMShsm should scratch data sets having reached expiration dates. 
 If true (SCRATCH), DFSMShsm scratches data sets that have expired when it performs space management and migration cleanup. 
 If false (NOSCRATCH), DFSMShsm ignores the expiration date. DFSMShsm processes the data set as if the expiration date has not been reached. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-expireddatasets-specifying-whether-scratch-data-sets-expired-expiration-dates

migration_prefix.description:
(MIGRATEPREFIX) Specifying the prefix (high-level qualifier) of the data set name that DFSMShsm generates when it migrates the data set. prefix must be defined as 1 to 7 alphanumeric characters; the first character must be alphabetic only. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-migrateprefix-specifying-prefix-migration-copy-name

psm_planned_start_time.description:
(hhmm1) Specifies the planned start time for automatic primary space management. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-primaryspmgmtstart-specifying-start-stop-times-automatic-primary-space-management

psm_planned_stop_time.description:
(hhmm2) Specifies planned stop time when DFSMShsm no longer starts automatic primary space management on a new volume. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-primaryspmgmtstart-specifying-start-stop-times-automatic-primary-space-management

space_management_migrate_to_cloud.description:
(MIGRATIONAUTOCLOUD) Specifies eligible target tier during automatic space management and command space management and the method of CEC thread serialization. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-migrationautocloud-allow-host-execute-cloud-migration

target_tier.description:
(MIGRATIONAUTOCLOUD(ALL|CLOUDONLY|NOCLOUD)) Specifies the eligible target tier during automatic space management. ALL allows migration to ML1, ML2, transition, and Cloud storage. CLOUDONLY restricts migration to Cloud storage only. NOCLOUD disables cloud migration. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-migrationautocloud-allow-host-execute-cloud-migration

selection_threshold.description:
(SELECTONTHRESHOLD(percent)) Specifies the expected maximum percentage of data sets on a volume eligible to be migrated to the cloud before DFSMShsm reserves a data movement thread in the disk storage controller unique to this volume. This parameter only applies when target_tier is ALL. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-migrationautocloud-allow-host-execute-cloud-migration

migration_level1_days.description:
(MIGRATIONLEVEL1DAYS(days)) Specifying the number of contiguous days a data set must remain unreferenced before the data set is eligible for migration from a level 1 volume to a level 2 volume. For days, substitute a decimal number from 0 to 999. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-migrationlevel1days-specifying-inactive-age-data-sets-migrating-from-level-1-volumes

migrate_psm_early.description:
(MIGRATEPSMEARLY) Specifying whether to activate primary space management early checking option. 
 If true (YES), one is added to the age check, up until midnight. 
 If false (NO), the actual data set age is always used. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-migratepsmearly-activate-psm-earlier-checking-option

migration_subtasks.description:
(MIGRATIONSUBTASKS) Enabling DFSMShsm to run multiple subtasks concurrently. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-migrationsubtasks-enabling-multiple-migration-subtasks

enable.description: (MIGRATIONSUBTASKS(YES|NO)) Specifies whether multiple subtasks is enabled. If true (YES), it enables migration subtasks. If false (NO), it disables migration subtasks.

additional_subtasks.description:
(ADDITIONALSUBTASKS(number)) Allowing you to dynamically change the number of additional subtasks that the system can use, running under each migration task. Specify a number between 0 and 10. Specifying a value of zero will remove all previously-defined additional subtasks. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-migrationsubtasks-enabling-multiple-migration-subtasks

migration_unit_name.description:
(MIGUNITNAME) Identifying the type of unit that should be specified the first time DFSMShsm requests to allocate a scratch tape during migration. For unit_name specify either 3480, 3480X, 3490, 3590-1, or an esoteric name which you specify in the (USERUNITTABLE) parameter of the SETSYS command. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-migunitname-specifying-type-unit-allocating-scratch-tape-during-migration
migration_unit_name.$comment: (MIGUNITNAME) when the keyword is specified, a subparameter is required.

migration_level1_overflow.description:
(ML1OVERFLOW) Specifying minimum data set size for ML1 overflow volume preference and/or threshold for ML1 overflow volume capacity for automatic secondary space management migration from ML1 OVERFLOW to ML2 volumes. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-ml1overflow-manage-ml1-overflow-volumes

minimum_overflow_dataset_size.description:
(DATASETSIZE) Specifies the minimum size, in K bytes, of the data set for which an ML1 overflow volume is preferred for migration or backup. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-ml1overflow-manage-ml1-overflow-volumes
minimum_overflow_dataset_size.$comment: Minimum and maximum data set size is defined in ARCCPSET.

overflow_threshold.description:
(THRESHOLD) Specifies the percent of occupied space in the ML1 overflow volume before migration of data sets to ML2 volumes during automatic secondary space management. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-ml1overflow-manage-ml1-overflow-volumes

migration_scratch_frequency.description:
(SCRATCHFREQUENCY) Specifying the number of days DFSMShsm should keep list data sets. Specify a decimal number from 0 to 9999. If you specify 0, DFSMShsm scratches list data sets during the next space management of the volume. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-scratchfrequency-specifying-how-long-retain-list-data-sets

small_dataset_packing.description:
(SMALLDATASETPACKING|NOSMALLDATASETPACKING) Specifying whether to pack small data sets into predefined VSAM key-sequenced small-data-set-packing data sets on migration level 1 volumes. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-smalldatasetpacking-nosmalldatasetpacking-specifying-whether-dfsmshsm-should-use-small-data-set-packing

storage_group_affinity.description:
(STORAGEGROUPAFFINITY) Specifies a set of hosts that have affinity to process a storage group. Up to 15 host names can be specified. Each host name must be 1-8 characters starting with A-Z, #, $, or @ followed by A-Z, 0-9, #, $, or @. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-storagegroupaffinity-define-set-host-names-that-have-affinity-process-storage-group-cloud-migration

tape_migration.description:
(TAPEMIGRATION) Specifying that you want DFSMShsm to use migration level 2 (ML2) tape volumes, to limit the selection and allocation of an output volume during tape migration processing, and to attempt fast subsequent migration. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-tapemigration-specifying-type-migration-tape

tape_unittype.description: An esoteric tape unit type can be specified to target a specific class of tape device, or specify "ANY" to allow any available tape unit type.

allow_reconnection.description:
(RECONNECT(ALL|ML2DIRECTEDONLY|NONE)) Specifying data sets eligible for fast subsequent migration (FSM) can be reconnected to the TAPE from which they were recalled. 
 If (NONE), data sets are not eligible for fast subsequent migration and are not reconnected to the TAPE from which they were recalled. 
 If (ALL), All data sets that are eligible for standard migration and satisfy fast subsequent migration eligibility requirements are reconnected to the TAPE that the data set was recalled from; including data sets that would have otherwise been migrated to an ML1 or ML2 volume. 
 If (ML2DIRECTEDONLY), data sets that are eligible for direct migration to ML2 tape volumes and satisfy fast subsequent migration eligibility requirements are reconnected to the ML2 tape volume the data set was recalled from. 
 Data sets not eligible for direct migration to ML2 tape volumes are processed using the standard migration method.
 A data set can be reconnected if all fast subsequent migration requirements are satisfied. For more information about these requirements, see fast subsequentmigration (reconnection) eligibility requirements.
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=tasks-reconnecting-data-sets-using-fast-subsequent-migration#fast_subsequent_migration_concept__fast_subsequent_migration_requirements

https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.title: DFSMShsm ARCCMDxx SETSYS commands for recycle function
https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.description:
(SETSYS) DFSMShsm SETSYS parameters controlling the recycle environment. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=dsar-setsys-command-establishing-changing-values-dfsmshsm-control-parameters
https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.$comment:
(RECYCLE) Defining parameters and subparameters affecting DFSMShsm recycle functions. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=parameters-setsys-fast-path-dfsmshsm-functions

max_tasks_recycle.description:
(MAXRECYCLETASKS) Specifying the maximum number of active recycle tasks. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-maxrecycletasks-specifying-maximum-number-active-recycle-tasks

ml2_partials_not_associated_goal.description:
(ML2PARTIALSNOTASSOCIATEDGOAL(max_number|NOLIMIT)) Specifying the maximum number of allowed partial ML2 tapes. 
 Substitute max_number with an interger between 0 and 999 for the maximum number of partial ML2 tapes, or specify NOLIMIT. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-ml2partialsnotassociatedgoal-specifying-maximum-number-allowed-partial-ml2-tapes

ml2_recycle_percent.description:
(ML2RECYCLEPERCENT(percent)) is an optional parameter specifying the percent-valid criterion DFSMShsm uses to recycle tape migration level 2 volumes, if you do not specify the PERCENTVALID parameter of the RECYCLE command. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-ml2recyclepercent-specifying-maximum-percentage-valid-data-migration-tape

recycle_input_deallocation_frequency.description:
(RECYCLEINPUTDEALLOCFREQUENCY) Allowing periodic deallocation of input unit during recycle processing. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-recycleinputdeallocfrequency-allowing-periodic-deallocation-input-unit-during-recycle-processing

backup.description:
(BACKUP(backup_deallocation_frequency)) During recycle processing of backup volumes, deallocation of an input unit will occur after the specified number of input connected sets representing single-file-format cartridges have been processed. 
 For backup_deallocation_frequency, substitute a decimal number from 1 to 255 for the number of connected sets to process before deallocation of the input unit. Specifying 0 will retain the input unit until recycle processing has completed. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-recycleinputdeallocfrequency-allowing-periodic-deallocation-input-unit-during-recycle-processing

migration.description:
(MIGRATION(migration_deallocation_frequency)) During recycle processing of migration volumes, deallocation of an input unit will occur after the specified number of input connected sets representing single-file-format cartridges have been processed. 
 For migration_deallocation_frequency, substitute a decimal number from 1 to 255 for the number of connected sets to process before deallocation of the input unit. Specifying 0 will retain the input unit until recycle processing has completed. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-recycleinputdeallocfrequency-allowing-periodic-deallocation-input-unit-during-recycle-processing

recycle_output.description:
(RECYCLEOUTPUT(BACKUP MIGRATION)) is an optional parameter that you use to limit the selection and allocation of an output volume during recycle processing. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-recycleoutput-limiting-selection-allocation-output-volume-during-recycle-processing

backup.description:
(BACKUP(unit_name)) For unit_name, specify a generic or esoteric unit name. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-recycleoutput-limiting-selection-allocation-output-volume-during-recycle-processing
backup.$comment: (BACKUP(unit_name)) can be speified with or without subparameter unit_name.

anyOf.$comment: temp: put true in quotes to work around parser bug expecting string

migration.description:
(MIGRATION(unit_name)) For unit_name, specify a generic or esoteric unit name. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-recycleoutput-limiting-selection-allocation-output-volume-during-recycle-processing
migration.$comment: (MIGRATION) can be speified with or without subparameter unit_name.

anyOf.$comment: temp: put true in quotes to work around parser bug expecting string

recycle_percent.description:
(RECYCLEPERCENT(percent)) is an optional parameter specifying the percent-valid criterion DFSMShsm uses to recycle tape backup volumes, if you do not specify the PERCENTVALID parameter of the RECYCLE command. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-recyclepercent-specifying-maximum-percentage-valid-data-backup-tape

recycle_tape_takeaway_retry.description: (RECYCLETAKEAWAY) Specifying whether to automatically generate a new RECYCLE command for a tape.

allow_tape_takeaway_retry.description:
(RECYCLETAKEAWAY(YES|NO)) An optional parameter specifying whether to automatically generate a new RECYCLE command for a tape. 
 If true (YES), DFSMShsm should utomatically generate a new RECYCLE command for a tape when the original recycle must terminate due to the takeaway process, or when the tape is in use by the another DFSMShsm task. 
 If false (NO), DFSMShsm does not automatically generate a new RECYCLE command. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-recycletakeawayretry-specifying-whether-automatically-generate-new-recycle-command-tape

max_retry_attempts.description:
(MAXRETRYATTEMPTS(retry_number)) is an optional subparameter of RECYCLETAKEAWAYRETRY. Specify the maximum number of recycle retry attempts. The value can be 1-99. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-recycletakeawayretry-specifying-whether-automatically-generate-new-recycle-command-tape

delay_time.description:
(DELAY(seconds)) is an optional subparameter of RECYCLETAKEAWAYRETRY. Specify the delay interval in seconds between recycle attempts. The value can be 1-9999. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-recycletakeawayretry-specifying-whether-automatically-generate-new-recycle-command-tape

recycle_tape_allocation_wait.description:
(RECYCLETAPEALLOCATION) An optional parameter specifying whether DFSMShsm should wait until the tape unit is allocated for the source and target tape volumes. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-recycletapeallocation-specifying-if-wait-recycle-tape-be-allocated

recycle_tape_residence.description:
(RECYCLETAPERESIDENCE) Specifying which IBM VTS tape volumes should be included in RECYCLE processing. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-recycletaperesidence-specifying-which-vts-tape-volumes-should-be-included-in-recycle-processing

https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.title: DFSMShsm ARCCMDxx SETSYS commands for security settings
https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.description:
(SETSYS) DFSMShsm SETSYS parameters that controlling security settings, including: 
 - ACCEPTPSCBUSERID | NOACCEPTPSCBUSERID 
 - ERASEONSCRATCH | NOERASEONSCRATCH 
 - PROFILEBACKUP | NOPROFILEBACKUP 
 - RACFIND | NORACFIND 
 - REQUEST | NOREQUEST  
 - TAPESECURITY

accept_protected_step_control_block_user.description:
(ACCEPTPSCBUSERID | NOACCEPTPSCBUSERID) Specifying whether DFSMShsm should have a way of issuing authorized DFSMShsm commands in a TSO batch environment in installations not having RACF. 
  - true: (ACCEPTPSCBUSERID) specifies that an installation not having RACF will have DFSMShsm retrieve the user ID for TSO batch requests from the protected step control block (PSCB) and associate the user ID with the request. 
  - false: (NOACCEPTPSCBUSERID) specifies that DFSMShsm will not attempt to retrieve the user ID for TSO batch requests when RACF is not installed. 
 If you do not specify this parameter on any SETSYS command, the DFSMShsm default is NOACCEPTPSCBUSERID. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-acceptpscbuserid-noacceptpscbuserid-allowing-non-racf-installations-issue-authorized-commands-in-tmp-environment

check_erasure_dfsmshsm_data_sets.description:
(ERASEONSCRATCH | NOERASEONSCRATCH) Specifying whether DFSMShsm should check for erasure of DFSMShsm-owned data sets that have migrated or been backed up to DFSMShsm-owned volumes. 
  - true: (ERASEONSCRATCH) specifies that DFSMShsm asks RACF® for the erase status of the user's data set when backup versions and migration copies are scratched from DFSMShsm-owned DASD volumes. 
  - false: (NOERASEONSCRATCH) specifies that DFSMShsm does not ask RACF for the erase status of the user's data set when backup versions and migration copies are scratched from DFSMShsm-owned DASD volumes. 
  If you do not specify either parameter on any SETSYS command, the DFSMShsm default is NOERASEONSCRATCH. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-eraseonscratch-noeraseonscratch-specifying-check-erasure-dfsmshsm-owned-data-sets

create_backup_racf_profile.description:
(PROFILEBACKUP | NOPROFILEBACKUP) Specifying whether to create backup RACF discrete profiles for cataloged data sets. 
  - true: (PROFILEBACKUP) specifies that DFSMShsm creates a backup RACF discrete profile for the cataloged RACF-indicated data set when it backs up the data set. This backup profile applies to all backup versions of the cataloged RACF-indicated data set. 
  - false: (NOPROFILEBACKUP) specifies that DFSMShsm does not create a backup RACF discrete profile when it backs up a cataloged RACF-indicated data set. 
  If you do not specify either parameter on any SETSYS command, the default is PROFILEBACKUP. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-profilebackup-noprofilebackup-specifying-whether-create-backup-racf-discrete-profiles-cataloged-data-sets

racf_indication.description:
(RACFIND | NORACFIND) Specifying whether to put RACF-indication on migration copies and backup versions. 
  - true: (RACFIND) specifies that DFSMShsm puts RACF-indication on migration copies and backup versions. 
  - false: (NORACFIND) specifies that migration copies and backup versions are not RACF-indicated, including those data sets that are password-protected. 
 If you do not specify either parameter on any SETSYS command, the DFSMShsm default is RACFIND.
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-racfind-noracfind-specifying-whether-put-racf-indication-migration-copies-backup-versions

operator_permission_required.description:
(REQUEST | NOREQUEST) Specifying whether the operator's permission is required before DFSMShsm starts any of the following actions including: 
   'automatic primary space management', 'automatic secondary space management', 'interval migration', automatic backup', 'automatic dump'. 
  - true: (REQUEST) Operator's permission is required before DFSMShsm starts any of the actions listed above. 
 - false: (NOREQUEST) Operator's permission is not required before DFSMShsm starts any of the actions listed above. 
 If you do not specify this parameter on any SETSYS command, the DFSMShsm default is NOREQUEST. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-request-norequest-specifying-whether-operators-permission-is-required

tape_security_type.description:
(TAPESECURITY) Specifying the type of security for tape volumes. It can be a boolean type or an object type. 
 If using boolean type, only true is allowed. No subparameter will be specified. 
 If using object type, the optional keys including: 
  - 'expiration_date_protected_no_pwd | expiration_date_protected_incl_pwd': (EXPIRATION | EXPIRATIONINCLUDE) exclusive to each other 
  - 'password_protected': (PASSWORD) 
  - 'racf_tape_protected_no_pwd | racf_tape_protected_incl_pwd': (RACF | RACFINCLUDE) exclusive to each other 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-tapesecurity-specifying-type-security-tape-volumes

expiration_date_protected_no_pwd.description:
Boolean type. Only true is allowed: 
  - true: (EXPIRATION), DFSMShsm protects each tape backup, migration level 2, and dump volume with an expiration date. However, DFSMShsm does not place a backup version or migration copy of a password-protected data set on a tape volume that is not password protected unless you specify true for 'expiration_date_protected_incl_pwd' (i.e. EXPIRATIONINCLUDE) or true for the key 'racf_tape_protected_incl_pwd' (i.e. RACFINCLUDE). 
  - this key is exclusive to the key 'expiration_date_protected_incl_pwd', i.e. (EXPIRATIONINCLUDE).

expiration_date_protected_incl_pwd.description:
Boolean type.  Only true is allowed: 
  - true: (EXPIRATIONINCLUDE), DFSMShsm protects each tape backup, migration level 2, and dump volume with an expiration date. In addition, DFSMShsm backs up or migrates a password-protected data set to a tape volume that is not password protected. 
  - this key is exclusive to the key 'expiration_date_protected_no_pwd', i.e. (EXPIRATION).

password_protected.description: If specifying as true, (PASSWORD), DFSMShsm protects each tape backup, migration level 2, and dump volume with a password. false is not allowed.

racf_tape_protected_incl_pwd.description:
Boolean type. Only true is allowed: 
  - true: (RACFINCLUDE) DFSMShsm protects each tape backup, migration level 2, and dump volume with RACF. In addition, DFSMShsm backs up or migrates a password-protected data set to a tape volume that is not password protected. 
  - this key is exclusive to the key 'racf_tape_protected_no_pwd', i.e. (RACF).

racf_tape_protected_no_pwd.description:
Boolean type. Only true is allowed: 
  - true: (RACF), DFSMShsm protects with RACF each tape backup, migration level 2, and dump volume. DFSMShsm protects the tape volume with RACF by adding it to a RACF tape volume set of DFSMShsm (HSMHSM or DFHSMx). However, DFSMShsm does not place a backup version or migration copy of a password-protected data set on a tape volume that is not password protected unless you specified true for this key (i.e. RACFINCLUDE) or true for the key 'expiration_date_protected_incl_pwd' (i.e. EXPIRATIONINCLUDE). 
  - this key is exclusive to the key 'racf_tape_protected_incl_pwd', i.e. (RACFINCLUDE).

https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.title: DFSMShsm ARCCMDxx SETSYS commands for environmental prpoerties
https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.description:
(SETSYS) Parameters controlling the DFSMShsm processing environment. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=dsar-setsys-command-establishing-changing-values-dfsmshsm-control-parameters
https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Dat.$comment:
(ENVIRONMENT) Defining parameters and subparameters that are essential to your installation's DFSMShsm environment. These parameters affect multiple DFSMShsm functions. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=parameters-setsys-fast-path-dfsmshsm-functions

allow_hsm_to_be_swapped.description:
(SWAP|NOSWAP) Specifying whether the DFSMShsm address space can be swapped. If true (SWAP), it specifies that the DFSMShsm address space can be swapped by the MVS system resource manager. If false (NOSWAP), specifies that the DFSMShsm address space cannot be swapped by the MVS system resource manager. 
 If you do not specify this parameter on any SETSYS command, the DFSMShsm default is whatever your computing system would normally do with the DFSMShsm address space. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-swap-noswap-specifying-whether-dfsmshsm-address-space-can-be-swapped

job_entry_subsystem_name.description:
(JES2|JES3) Specifying the job entry subsystem. Specify either JES2 or JES3. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-jes2-jes3-specifying-job-entry-subsystem

hsm_plex_name_suffix.description:
(PLEXNAME) Specifying a name for an HSMplex. (PLEXNAME(hsmplex_suffix)) is an optional parameter that allows you to name multiple HSMplexes within a sysplex. Specify a maximum of five characters as the suffix for the HSMplex name, DFSMShsm will prepend the prefix of ARC and form the HSMplex name. The default suffix used by DFSMShsm is PLEX0. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-plexname-specifying-name-hsmplex
hsm_plex_name_suffix.$comment: If data is to be transferred to cloud storage, the HSMplex name should contain only characters from the alphabetic, numeric, and national character sets (A-Z, a-z, 0-9,and #, $, and @).

dataset_serialization_method.description:
(DFHSMDATASETSERIALIZATION|USERDATASETSERIALIZATION) Specifying data set serialization that apply to volume migration and volume backup in a multiple-DFSMShsm-host environment. 
 Specify the desired data set serialization technique. (DFHSMDATASETSERIALIZATION) specifies that data set serialization of system resources during volume migration and volume backup in a multiple-image environment is not provided by system facilities, and that DFSMShsm should implement its requirements for resource serialization. 
 (USERDATASETSERIALIZATION) specifies that data set serialization of system resources during volume migration and volume backup in a multiple-DFSMShsm-host environment is provided by system facilities. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-dfhsmdatasetserialization-userdatasetserialization-specifying-data-set-serialization

use_csa_limits.description:
(NOCSALIMIT|CSALIMITS) Specifying whether to use common service area (CSA) limiting for MWE allocation. 
 If true (CSALIMITS), it specifies the values for CSA storage allocation used during DFSMShsm processing. If false (NOCSALIMITS), it specifies that CSA limiting should not be done during DFSMShsm processing. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-csalimits-nocsalimits-specifying-whether-use-csa-limiting-mwe-allocation

active_percent.description:
(ACTIVE(percent1)) is an optional subparameter of the CSALIMITS parameter that you use to specify the percentage of CSA storage that DFSMShsm can allocate to all types of MWEs when DFSMShsm is active. 
 For percent1, specify a 1-to 3-character number indicating the percentage of CSA storage to be allocated to all types of MWEs. The number can range from 0 to 100. If you do not specify this subparameter on any SETSYS command, the DFSMShsm default is 90. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-csalimits-active-specifying-percentage-maximum-limit-be-allocated-any-type-mwe

inactive_percent.description:
(INACTIVE(percentage2)) is an optional subparameter of the CSALIMITS parameter specifying the percentage of CSA storage that DFSMShsm can allocate to NOWAIT MWEs while DFSMShsm is inactive. 
 For percent2, specify a 1-to 3-character number indicating the percentage of CSA storage to be allocated to NOWAIT MWEs while DFSMShsm is inactive. The number can range from 0 to 100. If you do not specify this subparameter on any SETSYS command, the DFSMShsm default is 30. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-csalimits-inactive-specifying-percentage-maximum-limit-be-allocated-nowait-mwes

max_kbytes.description:
(MAXIMUM(kbytes)) is an optional subparameter of the CSALIMITS parameter specifying the maximum number of KBs of CSA storage to be allocated to MWEs. 
 For kbytes, specify a 2- to 5-character decimal number indicating the number of bytes of CSA storage to be allocated to MWEs. You can specify a value from 10 to 16383. If you specify 16384 or higher, no limiting of the number of bytes allocated in CSA is done. If you do not specify this subparameter on any SETSYS command, the DFSMShsm default is 100. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-csalimits-maximum-specifying-maximum-number-csa-bytes-allocated-all-types-mwes

mwe_number.description:
(MWE(number_of_mwes)) is an optional subparameter of the CSALIMITS parameter specifying the maximum number of NOWAIT MWEs submitted by a single address space that is to be kept on the CSA queue until completed. 
 For number_of_mwes, specify a 1-to 4-character decimal number indicating how many NOWAIT MWEs per address space are kept on the CSA queue until completed. 
 To limit the number of NOWAIT MWEs kept on the CSA queue, specify a number between 0 and 8191. If you specify 0, all NOWAIT MWEs are removed from the CSA queue as soon as they are copied into the address space of DFSMShsm. If you specify 8192 or higher, the number of MWEs to keep on the CSA queue per address space is limited only by the amount of CSA available, as specified in the MAXIMUM subparameter. If you do not specify this subparameter on any SETSYS command, the DFSMShsm default is 4. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-csalimits-mwe-specifying-maximum-number-nowait-mwes-per-address-space

dump_io_buffering_technique.description:
(DUMPIO(n,m)) is an optional parameter identifying which DFSMSdss DASD I/O buffering technique to use and the number of tracks to read for each EXCP. 
 The n indicates the DFSMSdss DASD I/O buffering technique for reading tracks. This value applies to DFSMSdss physical volume dump, when using the BACKVOL command with the DUMP subparameter. The m indicates the value used for DFSMSdss logical dump. If m is not specified, the value will be the same as n. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-dumpio-specifying-dfsmsdss-dasd-io-buffering-technique

physical_volume_dump.description:
(DUMPIO(n,m)) The n indicates the DFSMSdss DASD I/O buffering technique for reading tracks. This value applies to DFSMSdss physical volume dump, when using the BACKVOL command with the DUMP subparameter. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-dumpio-specifying-dfsmsdss-dasd-io-buffering-technique

logical_dump.description:
(DUMPIO(n,m)) The m indicates the value used for DFSMSdss logical dump. If m is not specified, the value will be the same as n. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-dumpio-specifying-dfsmsdss-dasd-io-buffering-technique

auto_function_long_running_alert.description:
(ISSUEARC1902(YES|NO)) Controlling whether an alert should be issued when an automatic function is running longer than expected. 
 ISSUEARC1902(YES|NO DELAYTIME(seconds)) is an optional parameter that controls whether DFSMShsm will issue message ARC1902I when an automatic backup function is still running after its specified quiesce/end time. 
 If enabled, ARC1902I will be displayed on the operator console after the user specified amount of time, in seconds, after the quiesce/end time of an autobackup function. The ARC1902I message will be moved from the operator console if the affected automatic function completer normally. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-issuearc1902-enabledisable-issue-arc1902i-message-console

allow_auto_function_alert.description:
(ISSUEARC1902(YES|NO)) specifies the message alert is enabled. Message ARC1902I will be displayed on the operator console after the user specified amount of time, in seconds, after the quiesce/end time of an autobackup function. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-issuearc1902-enabledisable-issue-arc1902i-message-console

delay_time.description:
(DELAYTIME(delay_seconds)) Specifies the amount of time (seconds) after the quiesce/end time when DFSMShsm needs to display ARC1902I message on the console if automatic backup is still running. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-issuearc1902-enabledisable-issue-arc1902i-message-console

promote_host.description:
(PROMOTE) Specifying whether a host is eligible for promotion. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-promote-specifying-whether-host-is-eligible-promotion
promote_host.$comment: PROMOTE requires at least one of the subparameters.

allow_primary_host.description:
(PRIMARYHOST(YES|NO)) Allows you to designate if a host is eligible to take over the unique functions from a failed primary host. 
 If true (PRIMARYHOST(YES)), it specifies that this specific host in an HSMplex is eligible to take over the unique functions from a failed primary host. 
 If false (PRIMARYHOST(NO)), it specifies that this specific host in an HSMplex is disabled from being eligible for promotion.
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-promote-specifying-whether-host-is-eligible-promotion

allow_ssm_host.description:
(SSM(YES|NO)) Allows you to designate a host's eligibility to take over Secondary Space Management (SSM) functions from a failed host. 
 If true (SSM(YES)), it specifies that this specific non-SSM host in an HSMplex is eligible to take over Secondary Space Management functions from a failed host. 
 If false (SSM(NO)), it specifies that this specific host in an HSMplex is disabled from being eligible for promotion. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-promote-specifying-whether-host-is-eligible-promotion

common_queue.description:
(COMMONQUEUE) is an optional parameter that specifies settings for the DFSMShsm common queues. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-commonqueue-specifying-settings-common-queues
common_queue.$comment: COMMONQUEUE or COMMONQUEUE() without any subparm is a valid command.

common_queue_dump.description:
(DUMP) is a subparameter of the COMMONQUEUE parameter. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-commonqueue-specifying-settings-common-queues

base_name.description:
(COMMONQUEUE(DUMP(CONNECT(base_name)))) Specifying the XCF functional group name suffix for remote dump processing. 
 When it is specified, this system is allowed to send and receive dumps to and from other systems in the HSMplex that were started with the same basename. For basename, substitute four characters. The four characters can be numeric, uppercase alphabetic, and national characters. The XCF group name generated by the system from this parameter is ARCDbasename. For example, if you specify DMP1 for basename, the resulting XCF group name that this host will become a member of is ARCDDMP1. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-commonqueue-dumpconnectbasename-specifying-xcf-functional-group-name-suffix-remote-dump-processing

master_scheduler_candidate.description:
(COMMONQUEUE(DUMP(MASTERSCHEDULERCANDIDATE))) Specifying whether the host is a master scheduler candidate for the common dump queue. 
 Subsequent SETSYS commands after a CONNECT can be issued to change the MASTERSCHEDULERCANDIDATE state of this member of the dump group. 
 A specification of MSC(NO) will remove this member as a master scheduler candidate, and if the member was currently active as the master scheduler, it will be stopped. The system will reassign the master scheduler to another dump group member that was defined as a candidate, if one is available. New incoming work will be assigned to run in this new master scheduler member. Active and queued work will be allowed to complete. 
 A specification of MSC(YES) will allow this member to become the master scheduler if needed by the dump group. This stand-alone MSC specification will have no effect until the host is connected to the group. 
 If it is known at startup that a system is not a candidate for being the master scheduler, but the system needs to be a member of the dump group, the MSC(NO) and CONNECT(basename) subparameters should be specified together in the DUMP keyword. 
 MASTERSCHEDULERCANDIDATE(Y), but will have no effect until a SETSYS CQUEUE(DUMP(CONNECT(basename))) command is issued. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-commonqueue-dumpmasterschedulercandidate-specifying-whether-host-is-master-scheduler-candidate-grouped-function-dump

disconnect.description:
(COMMONQUEUE(DUMP(DISCONNECT))) Specifying that a system disconnect itself from using the currently connected XCF functional group for dump processing. If the system is the enabled master scheduler for this group, it will be stopped and the master scheduler role will be assigned to another candidate. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-commonqueudumpdisconnect-specifying-that-system-disconnect-itself-from-using-currently-connected-xcf-functional-group-dump-processing

force.description:
(FORCE) is an option that can be specified with DISCONNECT. (DUMP(DISCONNECT FORCE)) allows requests from the common queue running in this system to finish. Requests submitted to the common queue from this system are failed locally on the submitting host but may continue to be processed elsewhere in the CDQ. 
 The FORCE option, DUMP(DISCONNECT FORCE), on a master scheduler system will allow requests from the common queue for this function running in the group to finish. However, any request received from remote members in the group on this master scheduler system and are waiting to be processed will be failed. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-commonqueudumpdisconnect-specifying-that-system-disconnect-itself-from-using-currently-connected-xcf-functional-group-dump-processing

common_queue_recall.description:
(RECALL) is a subparameter of the COMMONQUEUE parameter. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-commonqueue-specifying-settings-common-queues

base_name.description:
(COMMONQUEUE(RECALL(CONNECT(base_name)))): Specifying the base name of the list structure for CRQ host connection. The list structure name must be defined in the active CFRM policy. For basename, substitute five characters. The five characters can be numeric, uppercase alphabetic, and national characters. The list structure name is SYSARC_basename_RCL. For example, if you specify PLEX1 for basename, the resulting list structure is SYSARC_PLEX1_RCL. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-commonqueue-recallconnectbasename-specifying-base-name-list-structure-crq-host-connection

common_queue_recover.description:
(RECOVER) is a subparameter of the COMMONQUEUE parameter. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=command-commonqueue-specifying-settings-common-queues

base_name.description:
(COMMONQUEUE(RECOVER(CONNECT(basename)))): Specifying the XCF functional group name suffix for remote full volume recover from dump processing. 
 When specified, this host is allowed to send volume restores to the common recover queue for processing in the HSMplex with the same basename. For basename, substitute four characters. The 4 characters can be numeric, uppercase alphabetic, and national characters. The XCF group name is ARCVbasename. For example, if you specify REC1 for basename, the resulting XCF group name that this host becomes a member of is ARCVREC1. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-commonqueue-recoverconnectbasename-specifying-xcf-functional-group-name-suffix-remote-full-volume-recover-from-dump-processing

master_scheduler_candidate.description:
(MASTERSCHEDULERCANDIDATE)) Subsequent SETSYS commands after a CONNECT can be issued to change the MASTERSCHEDULERCANDIDATE state of this member of the recover group. 
 A specification of MSC(NO) remove this member as a master scheduler candidate. In addition, if the member was currently active as the master scheduler, it is stopped. The system reassigns the master scheduler to another recover group member that is defined as a candidate. New incoming work is assigned to run in this new Master Scheduler member. Active and queued work is allowed to complete. 
 A specification of MSC(YES)allows this member to become the Master Scheduler if needed by the recover group. This stand-alone MSC specification has no effect when it is issued on a host that is not connected to the group. 
 If it is known at startup that a host is not a candidate for the master scheduler role, but the host needs to be a member of the recover group, then MSC(NO) and CONNECT(basename) subparameters can be specified together in the RECOVER keyword. Remote recover processing in the group is not performed when none of the group members are master scheduler candidates with the MSC(NO) specification. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-commonqueue-recoverconnectbasename-specifying-xcf-functional-group-name-suffix-remote-full-volume-recover-from-dump-processing

disconnect.description:
(COMMONQUEUE RECOVER(DISCONNECT)): Specifying that a system disconnect itself from using the currently connected XCF functional group for recover processing. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-commonqueue-recoverdisconnect-specifying-that-system-disconnect-itself-from-using-currently-connected-xcf-functional-group-recover-processing

force.description:
(FORCE) is a subparameter that can be issued with DISCONNECT. The DISCONNECT FORCE option should be reserved for emergency situations. With FORCE specified, requests that originated from this host and are selected to be processed in the CVQ are not waited upon for completion before disconnecting. Messages are issued to indicate that a request has been failed but still may complete in the CVQ. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-commonqueue-recoverdisconnect-specifying-that-system-disconnect-itself-from-using-currently-connected-xcf-functional-group-recover-processing

dss_cross_memory_mode.description:
(DSSXMMODE) Specifying whether DFSMSdss will be loaded in its own address space using the cross memory interface, or in the DFSMShsm address space, for backup, CDS backup, dump, migration, and full-volume and data set recovery. 
 This parameter can be issued from the ARCCMDxx PARMLIB member only and does not affect FRBACKUP and FRRECOV use of the DFSMSdss cross memory interface. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-dssxmmode-specifying-whether-dfsmsdss-will-be-loaded-in-its-own-address-space-using-cross-memory-interface-in-dfsmshsm-address-space-backup-cds-backup-dump-migration-full-volume-data-set-recovery

all.description:
(DSSXMMODE(Y|N)) is an optional parameter. DSSXMMODE(N) specifies DFSMSdss will not be loaded into its own address space for the DFSMShsm function being invoked. Instead, DFSMSdss will be loaded in the DFSMShsm address space. This is the default. DFSMSdss will be loaded into a new address space for the DFSMShsm function being invoked and will be retained for future invocations of the that function, until DFSMShsm has been shutdown or restarted. 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-dssxmmode-specifying-whether-dfsmsdss-will-be-loaded-in-its-own-address-space-using-cross-memory-interface-in-dfsmshsm-address-space-backup-cds-backup-dump-migration-full-volume-data-set-recovery

backup.description:
(DSSXMMODE(BACKUP(Y|N)) Controls where DFSMSdss for the DFSMShsm backup function will be loaded; in its own address space (Y) or in the DFSMShsm address space (N). The default is N (no).  
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-dssxmmode-specifying-whether-dfsmsdss-will-be-loaded-in-its-own-address-space-using-cross-memory-interface-in-dfsmshsm-address-space-backup-cds-backup-dump-migration-full-volume-data-set-recovery

cds_backup.description:
(DSSXMMODE(CDSBACKUP(Y|N)) Controls where DFSMSdss for the DFSMShsm CDS backup function will be loaded; in its own address space (Y) or in the DFSMShsm address space (N). The default is N (no). 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-dssxmmode-specifying-whether-dfsmsdss-will-be-loaded-in-its-own-address-space-using-cross-memory-interface-in-dfsmshsm-address-space-backup-cds-backup-dump-migration-full-volume-data-set-recovery

dump.description:
(DSSXMMODE(DUMP(Y|N)) Controls where DFSMSdss for the DFSMShsm dump function will be loaded; in its own address space (Y) or in the DFSMShsm address space (N). The default is N (no). 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-dssxmmode-specifying-whether-dfsmsdss-will-be-loaded-in-its-own-address-space-using-cross-memory-interface-in-dfsmshsm-address-space-backup-cds-backup-dump-migration-full-volume-data-set-recovery

migration.description:
DSSXMMODE(MIGRATION(Y|N)) Controls where DFSMSdss for the DFSMShsm migration function will be loaded; in its own address space (Y) or in the DFSMShsm address space (N). The default is N (no). 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-dssxmmode-specifying-whether-dfsmsdss-will-be-loaded-in-its-own-address-space-using-cross-memory-interface-in-dfsmshsm-address-space-backup-cds-backup-dump-migration-full-volume-data-set-recovery

recovery.description:
DSSXMMODE(RECOVERY(Y|N)) Controls where DFSMSdss for the DFSMShsm full-volume and data set recovery functions will be loaded; in their own address space (Y) or in the DFSMShsm address space (N). The default is N (no). 
 https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=opsc-dssxmmode-specifying-whether-dfsmsdss-will-be-loaded-in-its-own-address-space-using-cross-memory-interface-in-dfsmshsm-address-space-backup-cds-backup-dump-migration-full-volume-data-set-recovery
